So, how are things? Ready for a new task from the king? It seems you never fail to satisfy him. I've never known him to support someone that willingly. Well then, on to dealing with the storage capacity!

Uh oh… with the last delivery we imported a special kind of woodworm. It particularly likes chomping on the exotic wood we organized recently. We should process it immediately, but first we need a sawmill for this kind of wood.

Good, production is going fine as far as I can see. While the wood is being processed, I will check how to get rid of these worms. After all, we want to be able to store this wood again in the future.

Pssst… I have returned. I've found a lot of these map fragments. Since I have no real use for them, I thought it would be best to give them to you. After all, you can buy interesting adventures with them.

I knew you would be here. I've chased you so often in this direction. It was just a matter of time before I caught up with you. Now, reveal who you are!... Oh my god! This cannot be. Seraphina! Could you please leave us alone for a while?

Greetings. Good to see you again. I have heard of some trouble around here, but it does not concern me. I am just here to tell you that the construction of the buildings, whose plans we have now, will consume a lot of tools. You should think about expanding your tool production.

Hey, what happened to Lord Sardin? I've never seen him so excited. I leave for just a few short hours, and the strangest things happen. Oh by the way, I have a new letter for you with no details of who sent it.

Hello, I am back again. At least I don't need to hide anymore. Yes, I am Sardin's daughter. My pigheaded father won't allow me to join the army, which is why I keep searching for adventures. By the way, I have the coordinates for your explorer's new search.

Greetings. How are you doing? I've checked the new plans, and they are really fascinating, but we will need granite for most of the buildings. It's a rare stone we cannot find on this island, but maybe you can obtain some during your adventures?

I heard what Henry told you about the granite. He is absolutely right; we will be needing large amounts of granite. Trading is always a possibility of course, but to find more adventures and granite we really should recruit more explorers.
We've been so busy we've neglected trade a little bit, don't you think? Remember that the king places a lot of importance on supporting trade. Maybe we should concentrate on that again for a while.

We should improve your trading skills at any cost. We will need lots of coins to upgrade buildings. In general, coins are always useful for trade, which is why we should set ourselves a certain coin income as a goal.

Hey hey. It's me. I've been travelling a lot, and visited the nicest islands, but the bandits there are very well equipped. If you want to go there too, you really should rearm, and for that you will need granite as soon as possible.

Greetings. It's always a pleasure to see you. I just wanted to let you know that the amount of resources suffice, and that everything technical is working fine. However, we could do with better isolation for the storehouses here and there. Would it be possible to upgrade one or two?

Please excuse my absence. I had to deal with some private matters… Anyway, I've taught you nearly everything I know. Of course, there are a few better weapons and units you can still build, but I think you'll manage it alone. For example, we could use crossbowmen.

Greetings. Don't worry, I do not have something to ask of you, just an idea. Yesterday I found a coin lying on the floor, and I got very excited about it. I was so happy that I worked way more effectively the following day. How about spreading some coins across the city and making your settlers happy with them? I'm sure they'll work better that way!

Oh, has my daughter vanished again? Typical! She's never very comfortable when she stays too long in one place, and becomes unreliable. That's one reason why I did not want her to join the army. Whatever... Next, we should construct a Titanium smelter.
Before we can begin manufacturing swords, we need have some titanium in stock. To produce titanium takes quite some time, so you had best begin with soon.

This is getting serious. You already have a glorious city and an effective economy. Now, we should concentrate on the military, since they are not only supposed to fight well but also represent your kingdom's strength. This means we still need to increase the number of units.

Greetings. I have found something very interesting. A friend of mine forgot to take it with him. I thought a carriage like this might be useful, and who knows what use can be made of it. Maybe you should think about producing one yourself. In which case, we'll be needing a wheelmaker.

Ah, it's good to be home again. I am sorry for not contacting you for so long, but I had a lot of things to discuss with the king. He has also given me a new task for you. It's the last one, so he has promised a substantial reward.

Ah, I found them! The plans for building a carpenter. He can produce the carriages with the help of the wheels. Just inform us when we should begin construction, and remember that the plans are quite complicated, so we will need some time.
A carpenter producing carriages? Useless! We need weapon production, not these bits and pieces. For example, we need a Damascene weaponsmith. By now we should have enough titanium ready.
Best start production immediately. You will be thrilled, because these are the best weapons you can get. With them, we will easily drive all our enemies back.

Hmm… You've upgraded your military quite a lot. Let me guess, that was my father's idea. He has always believed that more is more. Anyway, the real reason I'm here is because I've found a new route for your explorer.

I just saw Seraphina. Was she here? Hmm… adventure. Well, maybe these adventures would be a good way to try out your new units. Since your home islands don't seem to have any new challenges to offer any more, produce some units and use them in an adventure.

I can see you are diligently working on making your city perfect and polished. I think we should do the same with your military. After all, the military reflects the image of its owner, so let's increase the amount of unemployed settlers to attract more potential soldiers.

I don't want to tell you which units to choose for your army. You're probably able to decide that on your own. Just make sure you mix them up a little bit - not only is it more flexible, it also looks better.

Your city has become really glorious. Now we can slowly begin finishing it off. I'm thinking particularly of the storehouses - we should align them with the cityscape. The upgrade takes a lot of time and resources, so you'd better start as soon as possible.

Hello, how are you? How's the adventure search going? Found any treasure yet? I just happen to know that those bad guys on the far off islands have robbed one of the king's coin transports and stolen all the gold. How do feel about trying to get it back?

I found it! I found it! The construction plans to upgrade carriages to cannons. We'll be needing two different buildings - a powderhut and a cannon forge. If you're interested, you should start with the powderhut.

You've nearly done everything a man can do. The time has come to make your city perfect, and upgrade your mayor's house to level 5. It's almost unbelievable to see you come this far. I never imagined you would do so well. I am proud of you.

A generous offer has arrived from the king. At the moment you are subordinated to him, but he offers you your independence if you manage to gather a certain amount of coins, by any means you soo fit. You should take him up on this offer!

I have finished preparations for the construction of the cannon forge. As soon as you give the signal, we can start. It will become a gorgeous building, just wait and see. I am convinced that Lord Sardin will have the same opinion too.
I can see my father has left. I will not go until you have become the greatest explorer of any time. However, you'll need a far greater army than you have at the moment - more units, for example.
Great challenges await you. If you want to succeed, you'll need a big army with a good mixture of melee and ranged damage units. Prepare yourself well before leaving for the adventures.

The amount of settlers you can train to become units looks alright, but remember you also need weapons. I hope you have continued to keep an eye on the efficiency of your weapon production chains, because you'll be needing a lot of weapons very shortly.

My father has written me a letter requesting we talk. Instead of joining you on your journey, I will comply with his request and meet with him. I wish you luck. We will see each other again when you have become the greatest explorer of all time.
Before I forget, with a click on a building you can see further details about it. Try it on the sawmill and see for yourself.
As you already know, we will need a lot of wood to have enough building materials. You should always have some in stock so you don't run short.
Ah, plank production is already working effectively as far as I can see. You should also raise your stock of planks a bit.
Did I mention that it is possible to have several deposits at the same time? Just send your geologist out more often. An additional stone deposit always comes in handy.
With the added resources from Theodor, we should have enough of nearly everything except stone. Produce some, because we'll be needing a lot of it during our upcoming challenges.
Remember buffs? Producing buffs takes some time, but you usually need them on short notice. That's why I recommend you always have some in stock.

In contrast to workyards like masons, mines have to be placed directly upon the deposits. As I told you a while ago, you have to keep production times short. Of course, you cannot reposition buildings - but what you can do is to build a storehouse near your mines. That keeps production times short, too.
By the way, have you been sending your geologist out regularly to find new deposits? Remember, you can always have more than one deposit at a time. How about searching for copper?
I've just returned from visiting one of your neighbours. A really nice island with interesting building structures. Why don't you visit your neighbour's islands yourself?
Good to see you. I just received a message from the king. He has heard about you producing coal already. Right now he needs some, and asks whether you can accord him some.
I know Lord Sardin is a bit severe and has you really busy, but despite all that, don't forget your economy, especially your tool production. Is it going well?

We have a lot to harvest on our farm. If you were willing to support us with food, we could multiply our yield. And that would be fantastic, wouldn't it? If you're feeling extra kind, you could give some food to the workers at your small wells as well!

Please excuse the interruption, but I have a small favor to ask of you. A farmer from a neighbouring country has made a bet that his farm has more wheat and water, and I want to prove him wrong. So, we'll be needing more wheat fields!
All we need now is some additional wells, and I will win the bet. Would you be so kind and help me once more?

Please excuse me. I know you are very busy, but I won't disturb you for long. I just wanted to say that as soon as we begin producing bread, we'll be needing a lot of wheat. Maybe it would be best to build farms now so you don't have to deal with it later on?
I see you have built multiple farms. That's good, because soon we'll be needing horses, and they consume a lot of wheat. It would be best to anticipate and start production now.

A former comrade from the military academy has asked me to help him. He has received orders to defend a village and doesn't have enough bows. I really want to help him. First of all, we'll need a large amount of wood.
We agreed on 100 bows. I wonder what he wants to do with them. You could almost win a war with that many. Whatever, it's worth it, believe me.

My greetings. How is your military planning going? I just saw that you have a trade office now. That's fantastic news! I know the mayor of a neighbouring town who also has one. He needs stone. Maybe you can trade some?
How do you like the new resources? You can make a lot out of them. Remember that marble deposits deplete quite fast. When you have several, the stonecutter will always choose the nearest one.
Something terrible has happened. One of the children has gone into a mine and the mine collapsed after them. Can you help us find the kid? It was an iron mine.
As soon as you build a mine on the deposit, we can start searching. Your mine workers can help search while they are digging.

Greetings. I have a small problem. The consumption of hardwood planks has increased a lot lately, especially since your orders for building new residences. I would be very grateful if you could raise stocks a little bit.

A kind of fortuneteller has just arrived in your city and has asked for a solid sandwich. If you help him, he says he will tell your future. Generally, I am not superstitious, but maybe we should grant his request.
I've heard talk of a group of raiders approaching. Should they decide to rest here, we will need more wheat to secure the supply of horses.
Greetings. I've just seen the assignment for the construction of stables. Have you taken into account that horses also need water? You should think about building additional wells.
Finally we can train cavalry ourselves. How is water production going? We need water for brew as well as the horses, but I don't think there's any chance we will run short of it.

Oh, you've expanded your water production a little bit. I assume that was upon the advice of Lord Sardin. Either way, it's a good move, because I took a look at trading, and it seems water is a fine good to trade with.
The bread our bakery produces tastes really good. I have a favor to ask of you. In a few days' time, some of my relatives will be coming to visit me. Could you please provide us some bread?
Nice to see you again. As expected, my relatives liked the bread very much, but there is still some left. Maybe you should process the bread into gift baskets?

Lord Sardin has come to me with an unusual request. I think he was a bit too embarrassed to tell you directly. He says he needs coal for the training of his units, but he didn't want to tell me exactly how he was going to use it. Just send your explorer to find a coal deposit.
Now the only thing left to do is commission the construction of the mine. Meanwhile, I will try to find out why exactly Lord Sardin wants coal. I'd really like to know.

Yesterday we received a newsletter which went to all nearby lands. It is an invitation to the so-called green initiative, which encourages a more responsible attitude to nature. We should take part and build a forester or two.

One of our geologists just came and told me he thinks we have gold on our island, although he wasn't sure. He needs more time to find out. Send your geologist out to find a gold deposit. Maybe we'll get lucky.

Hmm… constructing coin production should be handled very carefully, but I have to admit I don't have enough experience to give out advice. What do you think about trading a little with coins to get a feeling for their value?

You can produce coins yourself, trade them, buy them from the merchant or find them on your adventures. Sometimes, even your explorer will take some coins back. Try out all the possible ways and when you are feeling confident, we'll start organizing your own coin production.

Wow, producing units really takes a lot of time, especially when you have to wait for settlers to move to your city. If you need settlers faster, you can attract them with bread. For example, you can hire Retired Bandits in exchange for bread at your provisions house.

Greetings. I see that you are going to begin your own steel production. A good decision - Steel is a fantastic material. Just remember that it will require more coal, so you had better raise your stocks.
So, did you sleep on it? Coin production, I mean. If you want your own production, you'll need a goldmine first, and they don't come cheap, so try to keep the mine running as long as possible.

I see you've become interested in adventures lately. I am not sure where your interest comes from, but I like it. Military experience is never a bad thing, and I would advise you to boost your weapon production.

I hope you do not become too cocky. You definitely mastered the first adventure, but have you also managed to complete the other ones? To earn my respect, you first have to complete the more difficult adventures with fewer losses.

You've really been quite busy with your adventures. Did you lose a lot of units? Producing more always takes some time. How about steel production? Do you already have enough steel in stock to train a solid amount of soldiers?

Wow, steel swords. They really look strong. Could you allocate some of them to me? I will give you something really useful in return. You had better produce some more to cover those you give me, and make sure no-one gets suspicious.
And how is the goldmine going? You should always try to buff your goldmine as effectively as possible. The more expensive the production of a resource, the more it pays off to buff a building.

Greetings. I wanted to give you a status report for your farms. Production itself is running well, but some farms would work a bit more effectively if you provided them with some resources for upgrading.
Soon we'll be able to begin the second stage of coin production. First though, I would recommend creating a small stock of gold ore, because the gold smelter needs quite a lot of it.
Pssst… It is me. I've discovered there are a lot of different adventures with differing enemy types and islands. In any case, you should try out multiple ones.
However, as always, you should not be satisfied with simply completing them - they consume your resources, so try to use as few units as possible.

My greetings. Sir Oliver rendezvoused with me a few minutes ago to plan the construction of a gold smelter. You should remember that a gold smelter needs coal to produce gold bars, so you should acquire enough coal mines beforehand.

Well, now it's time to construct the gold smelter. I see you have already stocked up on coal in preparation for coin production. Very commendable. If you continue like that, soon you will no longer need my help.

I hope I'm not disturbing you. I have a favor to ask of you. There is an ancient tradition among the stone cutters that requires them to participate in a competition to see who produces marble most effectively. Could you be the adjudicator? We'll produce up to a certain stock capacity and see who has contributed the most.

Pssst… I've brought you something. In your star menu you can find two adventures I found during my journey. If you manage to complete them without incurring great losses, I have something cool for you.

Have you remembered to keep an eye on some of your older production chains? For example, check tool production. You need tools for many different buildings, so take a quick look to make sure tool production is still optimum.

Similarly to the other buildings, I would recommend you produce some bars in preparation for building the coinage. While you are taking care of production, I will create my monthly report for the king.
My greetings. I've noticed your woodworm problem. I am aware that it mainly concerns exotic wood, but I think the hardwood may also be infected. We should destroy our stock and start afresh.
Well, the time has come to construct the building that produces coins: the coinage. As you may imagine, the coinage processes gold bars into gold coins, so let's get started!

Say, you have these map fragments, don't you? I was just at the merchant's and saw that he offers adventures in exchange for map fragments. You should pay him a visit. It's worth looking into if your explorer isn't having much luck.

Hmm… I was just thrown out of my own office by Lord Sardin. He had a young woman in tow. Now I am not sure what to do with myself. Could you take me with you on one of your adventures? I've always wanted to see what it's like.

Wow, your economy really consumes a lot of coal. Do you still have enough of it? Could you please check if your coal production line is still working properly? I just need to reassure my craftspeople that there will be enough coal at their disposal.

I've just noticed that you've overworked your coal production a little bit. Just remember that buffed production buildings can make a difference. When the buff runs out, the production rate decreases again. Try it out.
Now it's time to give your coin production the acid test. Let's see how long you need to produce a certain amount of coins yourself. I am really curious.
Ha ha, look how many adventures I have. Isn't that fantastic? I think you should always have some. I always feel uneasy when I don't have any available. How about you?

Hmm… One of our geologists has just told me that we do not have any granite deposits on this island. That's a shame, as we'll need a lot in the future. Could you check whether you can find granite on the adventure islands?
Now we know where to purchase it from, it is time to do so and get some. As I already said, we'll be needing a lot, so go get! The more you find the better.

I know I said I wanted to let you do it on your own, but you mustn't forget that crossbows are made out of titanium and exotic wood. This means you'll need a stock of both these resources to produce crossbows without difficulty.

Hmm… Recently, during an adventure, I found the plans for a flower bed. If I understand correctly, it's a kind of decoration building to beautify your home island, although it doesn't have any other function. Could you please test that theory out?
Did you already notice that the trade prices for selling ore are really advantageous at the moment? Maybe we should make use of this opportunity, construct a few mines, and see if it really pays off.

Bah, my father… He doesn't have much confidence in you, so I've made a bet with him. We bet that you will incur fewer losses during your adventures than he thinks. Now, you just have to prove me right.

While you are producing titanium, we should still keep an eye on our granite problem. I know it's an exasperating topic but it has to be dealt with. We should increase our stocks. Whether you trade or find granite yourself is up to you.

Since we are currently working on increasing our stocks, we should continue doing so with exotic wood too. After all, you've been consuming a lot of it lately. Just go about it the same way as with granite.

My greetings. I really appreciate you refilling the stocks of granite and exotic wood, but I would recommend you process some of the exotic wood into planks, especially as our plank consumption has increased a lot recently.
A general (also a friend of mine) is resting at our tavern at the moment. Have you already hired multiple generals? If not, now would be a good time to start. He's a really good man.
Wow, did you also receive a letter? I've been invited to participate in the competition too. Of course, I'm going to win, but I wish you luck nonetheless. May the best man win.

I've just received the next letter for the adventure competition. I'm so excited. This time it's a bit more difficult, but I love a challenge. I'll start work on it immediately. You too should work hard on it!

I don't know what to do. I have so many help requests from other islands, but most of my soldiers have requested vacation, and if they don't get back to their families there will be a lot of awkward questions. Can you answer with the requests by sparing just a few units?

Well, now it is getting serious. The final round of the competition has come. I just received the letter. Phew, take deep breaths... I'm really excited, I have to admit. Now it will be decided who is the best explorer. Let's go!

I've just received a letter from the king. He writes that the king of another kingdom has accused us of having a useless trade network, because you cannot earn gold with it. Because he thinks a great deal of you, the king requests you prove the other king wrong.

Lummy! Lord Sardin asked me to help you oversee the training of the cannoneers, but I don't have a clue how to go about it! I don't know what to say. I think you might be able to do better than me on your own.

Well, I'm back. I've already heard how you managed to organize cannoneer training yourself. Looks like I was unnecessarily worried. However, now I'm curious to see how our cannoneers will prove themselves in battle.
Since we now have a cannon forge, we should increase our stock of cannons a little bit. Cannoneers are priceless in battle, believe me.

You will not believe what I just heard. Do you remember the king who badmouthed our trade network? He's sticking to his opinion and affirms that no one is capable of gathering a certain quantity of riches. I am sure you can prove him wrong again.

Well, I have to admit your island looks really fantastic, but one thing is still missing - an epic decoration building, a castle or something like that. I'm sure you can find something suitable during one of the adventures.

I welcome you. My name is Sir Oliver. As you may know, the king has sent me to help you. Accordingly, we should not waste any more time and begin making building material for your settlement. It would be best to start with wood.
The wood is of no great use to you in itself. However, in order to build additional buildings, you'll need planks. You should build a wood sawmill.

In the Mayor's house and your storehouses you can see the resources you have in stock, spread over several tabs. Just like the sawmill, the Mayor's house can be clicked on to show the detail window. Try it out.

Maybe you've already asked yourself whether all the trees will disappear if we keep on clearing the forest like that. You're right, and that is why we have to do something to prevent such a situation: we will build a forester.

If you open your star menu, you'll see the new geologist you hired at the tavern. He will help us find special deposits on our island. First, we need stone. Go to the star menu and send him out to search for stone by clicking on him.
Of course, stone does not cut itself. For that we need a specialist: a mason. Place him as near as possible to the deposit and the storehouse to keep the journey short.

Your storehouses are well stocked and your settlement is expanding, but your settlers want somewhere to live. You should build them suitable houses to live in. The more residences you have, the more settlers will move to your settlement.
Your settlers already have a place to work and live. They are working well, but would do better if given a buff. Consequently, we need fish.
But first you have to build a provisions house where your groceries can be processed. After all, freshly caught fish cannot be eaten immediately.

In your provisions house you can create processed food, also known as buffs, for your workyards, refillers for some of your deposits, plus a few other things. However for now, let's concentrate on buffs.
Once a buff has finished being produced, it is transferred to your star menu. From there, you can use it on whichever workyard you want. Try it out.

I have just returned from the king's library. It seems that this island has not been mapped yet. It's very likely that there's a lot we can use here, it's just that we don't know where the resources are to be found. Send an explorer to discover the hidden areas one by one. Similarly to the geologist, you can hire an explorer at the tavern.

It is time to expand your property. Since the explorer has already mapped a new area, all that is left for you to do is claim your new property by building a storehouse in the new sector. After that, you can build in the new sector as you wish.
Did you already take a look at the new sector? I heard that it might contain copper deposits. Why not send a geologist to look for them? Maybe the rumours are true.
We should definitely build a copper mine. I will write the king immediately and secure your tenure for the deposit. You look after construction.
There are different ways to obtain coal. One of them is a coking plant. That's where coal is made out of pinewood. Remember that your pinewood consumption will increase.
To produce tools, we need a toolmaker to process copper bars. It would be best to have it built and ready to go as fast as possible.

Hey Kid! I am Lord Sardin. The fat guy… what's he called… anyway, you know who I mean... he told me you need help with your military. Wait a second, you don't even have any barracks! That's not much I can do until you get some.
Don't tell me you don't know how the barracks work?! Oh man, I really have to start from the very beginning. The barracks is where you can train your troops. Take a look at it.
I know you are very busy right now creating an army… Sardin didn't even want to let me through to see you… but I have to tell you something about your buildings. You can upgrade them. Try it out.
Do not get distracted too much by the fat man! We have to concentrate on the military. That is the most important thing! I hope weapon production is running well?

The situation is getting serious. Units alone are not enough to fight with - you need someone to lead them. Me? No, I cannot guide them, I have more important things to do, but if I'm not mistaken, you own a tavern! You can hire a general there for a few coins.

To assign units to your general, you need him to make a garrison. Just go to your star menu, click on the general and then on a green field on your map. He will hit the road immediately and build his garrison.
Before you can assign units to your general, you need to produce them in your barracks. 10 recruits should be enough to start off with.
Now it is time to assign units to the general. Click on the garrison and move the slider below the recruits to the right. Normal generals can command 200 units maximum.

So, the battle begins! Try to position your garrison as effectively as possible, and cross at the least watched areas. To check whether your troop composition is effective, you can use the pre-battle feedback. Show the bandits it was a bad idea to settle on your island.
So, let us begin with training the bowmen. I think 10 will be enough to start with, but be sure always to have some more in reserve, just in case.

I just arrived. I was on a voyage and have seen lots of new and different things. The latest trend is for buildings made out of hardwood and marble. In any case, we should upgrade to keep being competitive.
Producing marble is a lot easier than hardwood. Basically, you just need a marble mason who cuts the marble directly from the deposit.
You might be able to guess what comes next: militia training. Compared to weapons, the militia need more time and resources to be built, but in return they can do more.
Additional sawmills mean more planks, and that makes construction go faster, which is exactly what we need right now. Keep an eye on your pinewood production.

Do you like the economic overview? By looking at production time and the quantities of resources produced, you can get the best out of each work yard. For example, for wood it would be two woodcutters for three foresters. The best thing would be to build another woodcutter.

Have you ever been to a tavern? You can meet the most interesting people there. It is also a good place to find people with particular skills, so-called specialists. We should build one so we can hire some.

Now that the tavern is finished, we should think about the next step. Do you remember that you can hire specialists there? With a click on the tavern, you can see which specialists are available. Go and purchase a geologist!

Phew! Building a tavern can take quite a while. Did you know that it's possible to finish construction more quickly? As soon as something is in your building queue, you can finish it instantly by clicking the blue diamond. It just costs a few gems.

It's important always to keep production paths as short as possible. The shorter they are, the faster certain workyards will produce. You can see the path lengths in the details tab for your workyards, or directly when you are about to construct a building. Moving buildings can help you make production as effective as possible.

Bad news, I'm afraid! Our very own weather prophet woke up this morning with a pain in his stomach. He believes that winter is upon us. He keeps talking of snow and all that! I don't believe him, but we need to be prepared, just in case!
The hunters need game so they can hunt. We can lure more animals by using bread and a special mixture of spices a lady sold me not so long back. I still have the spices, so all we need is the bread!

We need more fish! But it's hard to get them lately, so we're going to use a new trick, and it requires steel. What's the trick, you ask? Well, we melt the steel and form it into little cubes. Then we drop the cubes into the water and wait for the sun to shine on them and create a show of lights. Then we wait for the fish to gather around! It's that simple! Now let's get the steel!

It's very good that we're taking care of our island but let's not forget our friends! I'm not sure they're preparing for the cold that's coming, so let's be a good neighbour and prepare some hardwood for them! That way, if they ever run out, we'll be the first to send them some! Cold can only be fought with fire. Or brew, or course.
As you know, wheat won't grow during the cold weather, so we'd better fill our storehouse with as much flour as we can! Why flour? Well, because even our mills might freeze, you see?

Snow snow snow! People always want it, until it actually arrives - then everything freezes up solid. We need to get some blankets to keep the kids warm. There's a merchant on the island who has a surprising number of blankets for sale. He's asking for sausages in return, would you believe... Sounds like the perfect food for this weather...
With the news of the snow and cold weather, many people agree we're going to need soup and tea, and both require water, so let's fill up as many barrels we can.

A painter has arrived from a far away island. He claims to be the best wall painter in the kingdom, but I've never heard of him. However, we might be able to use him to our advantage. He can paint walls, you see? We could have him decorate some of the interiors of our residences. Imagine how grateful our settlers will be! Make sure you provide the painter with everything he needs!

It seems that this wall painting business requires a lot of weird things. For example, one of the painter's projects requires coins and marble. Can you believe that? He's going to use coins to decorate the walls! Heavens… Let's get him some coins then.

The painter says that some of the houses need bigger walls so he can work his magic. We won't start building any new walls ourselves, but we've promised him some stones. Maybe he can… build something himself?

One of the noble lords from our island has requested the painter paint his walls using gold. Yes, you heard me. I mean the whole island knows how rich he is, so why does he need gold on his walls? Anyway, we promised we'd do everything we could, so make sure you bring some gold ore for the painter!

The painter has asked us to loan him some of our men to help him carry around his cans of paint, and he has quite a few... We'd better make sure we have enough settlers ready to help him any time he wishes to move his work station to another house. They also need to be equipped with our best tools! Let's prepare the tools!

The painter tells me he uses a special kind of brush made from copper, and even makes paint from copper. Don't ask me how he does it. All you need to know is that he wants us to provide him with some copper ore, and we're going to do just that.

The painter claims that he can paint on marble. I'll believe it when I see it. One of the lords from our island owns a house completely built from marble, but the painting still requires some modifications. He's asked us to provide him with some good quality marble that he can use in case there are any... unfortunate accidents.

Capital Island is indeed a wonderful place to live. All the youngsters want to move there one day. The king has a dream that one day all the islands in the kingdom will be as big and flourishing as Capital Island. It's up to us to make the first step, so we need to build a lot of residences and have a lot of moms and dads. In order to expand, we need a lot of people!
In order for us to expand we need big houses! And to build big houses we're going to need big tools! It's always good to have some new tools when you build new walls, right?
We don't know how many new settlers to expect, so let's make sure we have beds for all of them. We're going to need some hardwood planks! I can't wait to live in a bigger city!

I have some bad news! When we built our first residences, we made an error regarding the positioning. Don't ask me for more details - the cousin of one of our citizens is a architect, and he alerted us to the problem. Long story short, we need to twist and turn some of the streets. And for that we need stone!

We know of course that our settlers need the water for various things. We have streets, we have houses and between them we have wells, so there's really nothing that can stop us from getting the required amount of water! They just need to be filled now. Have some water ready!

When you have a big population, they have big expectations, and they can get a bit rowdy if they're left hungry. I think that if they get some extra food, they might leave us alone for a while, and just enjoy life. It would be an amazing help! Let's go with sausages... you can never go wrong with sausages.

Though I'm sure our lords and ladies have a comfortable enough lifestyle, that doesn't mean we can just forget looking after those in high society. For a start, plain noble residences are simply not good enough for them. This is why we've decided to decorate some of the houses to look even more… noble, and that means we'll be needing some gold.

Sir! We've found a storm-damaged ship near the coast! Apparently it belongs to a merchant who was supposed to bring a group of men to Capital Island. These men were born on an island covered by sand far to the south! Imagine, all that heat... The men call themselves the "Desert Riders" and seem to have a lot to trade! So, let's get to work!

The Desert Riders can't get their eyes off our longbows! At first we thought it might be a sign of danger, but in fact they're just admiring them! They want our longbows and are ready to pay a good price, so let's not keep them waiting! Let's make them some longbows!

The Desert Riders visited our stables today. I've never seen men care for horses so lovingly. They sure know how to tend to these noble creatures! One of them mentioned that he would like to buy some of our herd! Let's make sure we provide them with all the horses they need.

The Desert Riders have come to you for wheat. They've heard that the horses we sold them love the wheat we make, so we'llneed to provide them with it. I hope the horses can adapt to whatever else they get in the desert…
The Desert Riders will be needing a lot of water if they're going to cross the ocean with so many horses! Let's make sure we give them the best water we have.

We know that the Desert Riders will take care of the horses we sold them, but I would like to make sure they know how. We need some of our trained cavalry to teach them our ways! First lesson : how to use a carriage. Let's get some carriages ready for them.

The ship the Desert Riders arrived on is really damaged and it' up to us to fix it. The structure of the ship is not what we're used to, but I'm sure our engineers can fix anything. In fact, they've requested some hardwood planks and exotic wood planks for the starboard of the ship!

You remember that old inventor who lives alone on that abandoned island? Gully Island? Well, somehow he's managed to amass a lot of coins. I guess he invented something really useful and sold it. However... he has come to us with the most disturbing request. He wants to build a cannon, a BIG cannon, big enough to shoot down the moon! Yep, you heard me. He must've gone mad form loneliness. Well, as long as he pays us, we'll help him build his cannon, right?
Though the cannon the inventor wants to build seems bigger than we could ever imagine, he still needs some additional parts. Here's the list - we need iron ore.

The inventor has told us he needs steel to coat the outer layer of the cannonball. He says that steel blocks the "cosmic radiation". I have no idea what he's talking about. That poor crazy old man... Let's just get him the steel he needs.

Our engineers working at the cannon forge went pale after talking to the inventor. Apparnetly, he told them how much gunpowder he needs to shoot the cannonball so it will reach the moon. There's no way we can provide that much gunpowder, but we're going to try our best, right?

You know what an aiming crest is? Yes, it's what you use to aim with. Duh. Anyway, the inventor tells me he wants to have an aiming crest made solely out of gold. His wish is our command! Gold ore for the man.

The inventor says he needs some sacks of saltpetre to create a secondary explosion. Then he went into detail about exactly how it would work, but I have to admit I switched off about halfway through. Let's get the man some saltpetre and some more iron and hope he finds somebody else to talk to.

The inventor has told us he has no clue how to use a cannon, and needs us to teach him. Thankfully, we do know a cannoneer who we can hire to look after the training, and we can pay with food! How nice! He told us that he loves fish.

I noticed that there have been a lot of buildings in your building construction queue lately. I should remind you firstly that it is possible to buy temporary or permanent construction slots, and secondly, that you can change the order of the buildings with the arrows. Try it out!

Oh, it looks like you are running out of available settlers. If you mouse over the settler icon in the resource bar at the top of the screen, you can see information about your settlers, like, for example, when you will get a new one and how much space is left. Check what you have to improve to get new settlers, and buy new ones from the merchant when there is enough space.

When did you last have a look at the settlers overview? I am just asking because you are running out of settlers again. I don't mean to bother you, I just want to make sure that you have enough of them when you need them. If you have enough space for settlers, you can hire some for bread in the provision house.

Have you already noticed that your deposits deplete when you destroy them? There are deposits you have to refill manually, like fish. Therefore, you have to produce a refill in your provision house and use it on the depleted deposit.

As you have no doubt already noticed, the production of goods takes a lot of time in the beginning. If you do not have time to wait, you can use trade to acquire the needed items. Either you take an already existing offer, or you make one yourself. Try it out.
Did you remember to involve trade in your planning? You have a great task ahead of you, and you should not hesitate to use your military. The king will be very happy if you do!

Your efforts to expand your military are obvious, but remember that you will need lots of settlers for the military and all the new buildings. And they in turn need a lot of space. Build some residences so that you have enough capacity

Do not get distracted by this... What was his name? Klaus? The little fat man, you know who I mean. Do not get too distracted by him. We need hard wood for longbows. Maybe you could increase the production outcome for a short time.

The situation is worse than expected! They've taken over the island, and using a mystical item called the Hoarfrost Globe, they've covered the land in ice. What is the globe? It's a mystical item filled with pure frost essence… we need to find it and destroy it! The spy said it's inside one of the many enemy camps. Let's go, we're running out of time!
This is not good - we're going to freeze here! We need to find the globe and destroy it! Let's battle our way to the next camp!

The leader has broken the globe into six pieces! They have all been hidden inside some old depleted wells around the island! You must find and destroy the depleted wells now! The ice is getting to our bones!

Wait! Our youngest spy has come back, saying there is another part to the globe! The last piece, the core, is in the hands of their leader, Odinom the Cruel! This is it - we need to find him and destroy the final piece!

Specialists always need a certain amount of time to fulfill their tasks. As you progress, your times will become longer and longer. However, if you do not like to wait, you can shorten them with just one click. Try it!

If you have a little time, I would like to share two things with you: First, you can track quests by clicking the small box next to the quests in the quest book, and secondly, you can pin the building menu if you want to prevent it from closing, when you are building streets, for example. Take a look.
You should now start your first production. Produce your first resources so they can serve as a base for further production chains.

Hey! Don't be scared! It's me, Eliot, the Pumpkin Master! I bet you're wondering why it's so dark outside, aren't you? Well, it's a bit... CREEPY! A dark presence called the Hollow Man has stolen the sun! I need your help to find the children of the night and scare the Hollow Man away! And that, is a job for my magical pumpkins! First, we'll need to own at least one pumpkin Cemetery and make some pumpkins!

I know that my little pumpkins are growing slowly, but I just might have the solution! I've heard you know of a way to speed up things using the goodies that you can produce at your Provision House! Show me!

The Hollow Man was born from pure darkness and mystery, that's why we can't see him in the dark! In order to scare him away, we need to make sure we're wise to his little tricks! Let's make some darkness at your provision house and test it… no, not on your island, but I'm sure you have some friends who wouldn't mind being... test subjects... he he he.

The Hollow Man uses pure darkness to do wrong, so we need to use pure light to repel his deeds! I found the recipe for pure light during my travels to another land. Let me show you how to make a very powerful light at your Provision house, and if any of your buildings become affected by darkness, we could even try it out!

The next step might scare you a little! BOO! Ha ha ha, I'm just kidding. In order to fight the Hollow Man we're going to need the help of the children of the night. We should start with our good friend, the Zombie. We need to summon him… or perhaps we should rather say: we need to dig him out. Sadly, he is buried very deep underground and we're going to need a lot of tools to dig him free! Bring your settler and make sure he's equipped with the best tools!

Do you know Mr. Myers? He was a great general in the olden days, but hasn't been feeling so well recently. He lives somewhere in a hidden crypt, but we have to find him as we need his help. The only way to summon him is to give him back his most beloved armour chestplate. We don't have one right now, but we can make one. We're going to need copper and iron ore for that!

The last of the children of the night is doctor Frank and Stein. He is an expert on marble. They say he owns a castle made solely from marble, can you believe that? Anyway, it would be a good idea to call on him to help us because to scare away the Hollow Man we're going to need a lot of marble! Either you produce it yourself, or ask for the doctor's help - it's your choice.

Hello, it's me Eliot! I need your help again to bring the sun back. You'll find the recipe for the Sun Buff in your provision house! It's a magical powder. Produce some and use it! If all goes well we'll have the sun back in no time!

For stable pinewood plank production, a lot of steps are necessary. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will have efficient plank production. Short quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

For stable stone production, you will need some preparation. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will have efficient stone production. Short quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

To be able to use buffs, you will have to take certain steps. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will be able to produce and use one simple buff. Short quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

To know the possibilities the game gives you for more comfortable playing you should know some functions. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will know the most important comfort features. Short quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

Claiming new lands is a complex task. By the time we complete this chain of quests, you will know everything important about conquering other areas on your home zone. Medium duration quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

For stable tool production, you will require fresh knowledge on several topics. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will have efficient tool production. Short quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

While building new production chains, older ones will get become unbalanced. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will be able to handle this problem. Long quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

Trading is an important feature. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will be able to trade and have your first trading experiences. Long quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

For stable brew production you will need lots of new buildings. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will have efficient brew production. Short quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

Battle is a complex and important topic. By the time we complete this chain of quests, you will know the basics of battle and have your first small army. Short quest chain: To complete this main quest, finish all its subquests.

You have probably already recognized the bandits on your home zone. By the time we complete this quest chain, these bandits will no longer be a problem. Long quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

Treasure search is a good way to get rare or valuable resources. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will be able to make use of all the possible treasure searches. Long quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.
You are already able to use buffs. By the time we complete this quest chain, a new buff will be available to you. Short quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

Ranged units are an important unit variant. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will have access to two different kinds of bowmen. Medium duration quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

New buildings will become available which will need new building materials. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will have all necessary buildings for these materials. Short quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

Population is always a big issue. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will be able to handle your population issues. Medium duration quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

Recruits will not suffice as units for all types of battle. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will have militia as a new unit possibility. Short quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

Storage capacity is always very important. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will have a large storage capacity and the knowledge necessary to increase it further. Long quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

Not all units attack at the same time. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will know what first strike means, and what cavalry is. Short quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

Population is always an issue, as you already know. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will have a large population capacity. Long quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

You already know the possibilities for using fish, but there are still some things you could learn. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will know everything about fish and meat. Medium duration quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

Maybe you have already figured out that there will be more types of units. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will have soldiers as a new unit possibility. Short quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.
It seems your brother has problems. By completing this quest chain, you have helped your brother. Short quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

Bandits are not just present on your home zone. By the time we complete this chain of quests, you will know everything important about adventures and how to experience them. Medium duration quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

There is still a lot to tell you about adventures. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will know absolutely everything about adventures. Medium duration quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

New buildings will become available which will need new building materials. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will know all the necessary facts about these materials. Short quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

It seems you are ready for the strongest unit types. By the time we complete this quest chain, you will have all the remaining unit types and productions. Medium duration quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

All that's left to do is to make sure your army is perfect. By the time we complete this chain of quests, you will have a well balanced weapon economy and a large army. Medium duration quest chain: To complete the main quest, finish all its subquests.

Now it's up to you to become the richest person and best merchant on the planet! When you complete this quest chain, there will be nothing more to say - and you'll have stacks of money to keep you busy. Long term quest chain: To complete this main quest, finish all sub quests.

As you no doubt remember, we introduced new building materials some time ago. However, we did not check whether we had a positive balance and had even constructed new buildings, which also produce some of these materials. So it is now time to balance these resource chains. Take a look at your economic overview and raise production of these new materials to a decent value.

The sausages our butcher produces are really good, but I've talked to him and he says he doesn't have sufficient meat to produce as many sausages as he should. Have you already had a look at meat and fish in your economic overview? Maybe an adjustment is needed.

I heard your general was defeated? Don't worry, it's not a disaster. I have put something into your star menu that you can use to heal him in no time. You should analyze why he lost, but first heal your general so he is ready for duty again.

A toy for a child is like a sword for a soldier: both would be unhappy without one. You can make swords for your soldiers, and I, Santa Claus, can make toys for the children. Help me out with some wood please.

Ho ho… *cough*. Oh my, it seems that Santa may have caught a cold. I wonder, could you perhaps make me and my elves some snowflake tea? We have the snowflakes, all we need is some warm water! Can you prepare some for us?

Come here for a moment please. I want to set up an aquarium for the children, and it will require all kinds of coloured fish! Could you talk to the fishermen for me? Tell them Santa asked them to bring some coloured fish! What joy!

One of your attendants has become very enthusiastic recently about a beverage called warm brew. Consequently, you have decided to trade some brew, boil it up, taste it, and see whether it is really as tasty as you have been told.

Have you ever heard of the fairy Vava? She works for me at the North Pole as my personal cook! Every morning, she bakes me snow coated pretzels! I want you to help her out with some flour and water so she can prepare some for your settlers!

I walked around the island and noticed that some of the settlers can't afford to own a tall Christmas tree. This is unacceptable! Help me build some proper tree holders by providing some strong hardwood planks!

Gigling Oaffy, my little aid elf, is looking out for my… erm… size. I tend to eat a lot you know. Ho ho ho! Actually, I wanted to ask you for some sausage. I've heard that you make the best! Just don't tell Gigling Oaffy about our little conversation please! It'll be our special secret...

Every year we place the yellow star on top of the Christmas tree. Sadly, this year we can't find the star because there's a shadow covering the night sky. I have called upon my hunter elf - I call him Shady Slayer. He knows how to get rid of shadows! Help him out with some iron ore so he can prepare the iron dust he'll use against the shadow!

Oh! I've been contacted by my engineer elf, Smiley Nakrul. He says my sledge has been damaged! He tells me he could fix it, but unfortunately he's left his tools at the North Pole. Can you help Smiley Nakrul, please?

Oh no! I've got so many gifts to transfer, but my sledge needs repairing. I've heard that you breed a special kind of horse on your island. Is that right? Oh joy! I'll tell Nutty Matty, my technician elf, to get everything prepared. Please, give him a hand getting the horses!

My council of elves has dispatched Timble Jude to be my consultant during the time I spend on this island. Timble Jude suggested I should ask you about your friends. Have you sent them any gifts yet? No? Well, I think the time has come to do so!

I've got my naughty or nice list over here made by Sirim Seb, one of the elf knights of the North Pole. He's a kind soul, but takes discipline very seriously. He could be a leader one day. Anyway, he needs some coal for the naughty kids, and I always forget to bring some. Can you help us?

Wow, you'll never guess what I found! There are some islands quite far away, with epic treasures like coins and special building plans. However, you'll need a huge army for the voyage, and that will require new, unemployed settlers.
I see my father has left, but I won't until you have become the greatest explorer of any time. However, you'll need far more than the army you have at the moment, including more units for example.

So this is it, our beloved home island, 1,000 years before our time! The forests are bustling with strange creatures and something seems wrong with the water. I say we stay in the open and go catch these insidious devils as quickly as possible!
We have no time to waste - I see their witchdoctors have gathered and are up to no good, that much is certain!

Over there! They seem to have begun some sort of ritual! Can you feel it? It's sending chills down my spine. We must not let them finish their abysmal deeds. Quickly now, we might still be able to prevent them from casting the curse upon all of us!

I don't mean to bother you, but sadly I have some disturbing news. Apparently, there was once a very famous pirate captain, but he died while looking for lost treasure on Skull Island. Now, some brave young pirates have decided to go and find him, or more importantly, the treasure. Don't ask me why, but King Damien insists we go stop them at once! They shall not put their dirty hands on that Skull! We should travel there immediately!

Wow, this is a small island indeed. So here's the story: The island was once occupied by an cult who worshiped some old sea god. Ages later, a famous pirate captain, Longsight Emeric, found the island and raided all their tombs, taking every last piece of treasure. However, he never left the island alive. Now these young pirates have decided they're going to find both the treasure and Emeric's Skull. Let's go and "ask" them nicely to go away.
Keep knocking on the doors - let's hope some of them are in the right mood to talk peacefully. Or not. There was a camp right at the entrance of the valley. Perhaps we should aim for that!

There are about four ruins on this island that are still explorable. Let's send some spies ahead to check them out - maybe the pirates missed something in one of them? It's not even the treasure we want to find but that Skull the King wants so bad. I wonder why it's so important?
We need to find the pirate captain! Maybe he is hiding in one of the camps, or somewhere else, I don't know! One thing is sure : if we fight off every pirate on the island, we'll find him eventually!

I don't mean to bother you, but sadly I have some disturbing news. Apparently, there was once a very famous pirate captain, but he died while looking for lost treasure on Skull Island. Now, some brave young pirates have decided to go and find him, or more importantly, the treasure. Don't ask me why, but King Damien insists we go stop them at once! They shall not put their dirty hands on that treasure! The King also mentioned he would like us to find the captain's Skull. We need to find that island and do what our King asks of us!

Crisis! The watcher in the tower sent out several warnings over the past months but none reached us until this morning. In his letter, he says that the four winds of the world are soon to be reunited in a huge storm right above our archipelago. Apparently, this event happens every 100 years, and we do have records of the last super storm. Back then, it destroyed most of our kingdom. We cannot allow this to happen again! This is a crisis! We must prepare for the worst!

We still have time before the next dawn, so we need to do the preparations step by step, following a well designed emergency plan. The first step is to send out our specialists so they can find the proper resources we will need. The reinforcement of the buildings is our biggest priority now. Do your best to get this organized, and we can move on to step two!

We can count on our miners come wind, rain or shine, and step two requires their hard work. They need to excavate the ore we need to reinforce our buildings on the island, but it seems we need the help of the Barracks. The Island's Military Forces could help us a lot. Let's keep them happy, so they help us as much as possible!

I will send out the messengers, and until the answer comes, we should keep on focusing on the storm and how to avoid it.

There is a breach in security! The bandits and pirates lurking around our islands have decided to take advantage of the crisis to rob and plunder. They've almost emptied our storage facilities, but thank the maker for our great scouts! First we must prepare to fight back! Then we must regain all the lost resources by any means! We need to be 100% sure they can't get their hands on our resources even if they dare come back for more!

Crisis! The watcher in the tower sent out several warnings over the past months but none reached us until this morning. In his letter, he says that the four winds of the world are soon to be reunited in a huge storm right above our archipelago. Apparently, this event happens every 100 years, and we do have records of the last super storm. Back then, it destroyed most of our kingdom. We cannot allow this to happen again! This is a crisis! We must prepare for the worst!

We still have time before the next dawn, so we need to do the preparations step by step, following a well designed emergency plan. The first step is to send out our specialists so they can find the proper resources we will need. The reinforcement of the buildings is our biggest priority now. Do your best to get this organized, and we can move on to step two!

Greetings! I am Master Gotenberg, bookbinder by profession. Have you ever considered how much we could increase our workshop's efficiency if everyone had access to all their craft's knowledge? Such an endeavor requires quite an infrastructure though. Can you provide that?

I can produce different sorts of documents that will allow you to share the knowledge of your brightest minds. Let us build a Bookbinder workshop, and I will show what your Settlers are really capable of!
I'm telling you, give people the right tools and they will willingly share their knowledge with the world. Let us get a Finesmith to produce some Nibs!
To enable our Settlers to archive their knowledge for future generations we still lack something essential: paper! Build a Papermill and we shall have all we need to make documents.

I'm thrilled to tell you we are now able to produce the first manuscripts. Visit me in my workshop and we'll discuss the first edition! Remember to put that knowledge to use immediately afterwards. For example, your Geologists would benefit greatly from this.
With Manuscripts, we won't be able to cover all the aspects of our more complex crafts. It is about time we expanded our capacities to accommodate better document production.

I have been struck by an idea that might just change the way we share writing. It's this concept for reusing printing stencils, but it will require all-new production methods. Provide a Lettersmith to produce the printing press letters!
Our new printing approach requires a more robust type of paper, so we will be needing some new workshops. Build an Intermediate Papermill so we can work with our new technology.
The new formats look quite impressive. I can't even imagine what knowledge they might be able to carry. I recommend producing and distributing some Tomes as soon as possible.

The Master craftsmen are asking for more distinguished volumes to share their exquisite knowledge with. We shall need more sophisticated manufacturing methods to meet this requirement. Let's make sure our economy is up to it.

To allow for the noblest and finest type of documents we will need an Ornamentalsmith. Creating a Codex requires much experience and skill. However, the result is the most amazing piece of bookbindery I am able to deliver.

By using the best materials we will be able to live up to the highest bibliophiliac standards. Let us use the experience we have gathered to build an Advanced Papermill, and create the finest paper of our era has ever known!

It is done - the manufacturing pipeline for the Codex is complete! Visit me in my workshop at any time and let's talk about producing some of these most precious volumes! This will provide you with the most advanced and secret skills and knowledge.
In order to spread writing, we will need the help of a few specialists. Get these workshops for your settlement and we shall get going.
The Manuscripts were a great starting point for the education of your Settlers. Now we should build upon this and take it one step further.
Truly secret knowledge and particularly valuable skills require a special type of book. I suggest you build workshops dedicated to the refinement of our Tomes.

That was the biggest storm I've ever experienced! It was like being caught in the middle of 105 winds, not just 104! Well, we survived the storm, but lost way too many resources and other items. It seems our work here isn't done yet, so we better start with the damage reports and get ourselves back in the game, if you know what I mean. Let's get on it.

Last night was testing, and the air was alive, swooshing from every direction as if we were battling the armies of the storms! Ahh, I should calm down. Remember the Military Force helping us with preparations? Well, they kind of need us now. The Barracks armoury was partially damaged and they lost a lot of weapons. I will alert the smiths to start work. I hope you can manage logistics. Meanwhile, don't forget we still need to get resources to help our economy recover!

A young scout has tried to deliver a letter from the King, but she couldn't find how to push through the storm, so we received it late. In this letter, the King orders every island to strengthen its population, to make sure there will be strong people on hand in case another crisis hits us. Oh, and we should making some more weapons, just in case. Off to work, then!

Terrible news! The coinmaster of our island is lost, and with him all our coin reserves! We intended using those coins to repair the damage we suffered during the storm! We need to act quickly! Go to the market and buy some coins! I wonder where our coinmaster is? That old lady at the end of the town said he might have been carried away by a moonlight shadow. Strange, I've never heard of a creature like that, but I certainly don't want it in my backyard.

We're really close to finishing, and the storm is far away on the other side of the ocean. I don't think we're going to experience it before some time, but who knows? We need to finish the last repairs, calm the people down... just do all we can to get back to the normal flow of life. I'll set up a list with the last things we need to take care of.

That was the biggest storm I've ever experienced! It was like being caught in the middle of 105 winds, not just 104! Well, we survived the storm, but lost way too many resources and other items. It seems our work here isn't done yet, so we better start with the damage reports and get ourselves back in the game, if you know what I mean. Let's get on it.

Last night was testing, and the air was alive, swooshing from every direction as if we were battling the armies of the storms! Ahh, I should calm down. Remember the Military Force helping us with preparations? Well, they kind of need us now. The Barracks armoury was partially damaged and they lost a lot of weapons. I will alert the smiths to start work. I hope you can manage logistics. Meanwhile, don't forget we still need to get resources to help our economy recover!

A young scout has tried to deliver a letter from the King, but she couldn't find how to push through the storm, so we received it late. In this letter, the King orders every island to strengthen its population, to make sure there will be strong people on hand in case another crisis hits us. Oh, and we should making some more weapons, just in case. Off to work, then!

Terrible news! The coinmaster of our island is lost, and with him all our coin reserves! We intended using those coins to repair the damage we suffered during the storm! We need to act quickly! Go to the market and buy some coins! I wonder where our coinmaster is? That old lady at the end of the town said he might have been carried away by a moonlight shadow. Strange, I've never heard of a creature like that, but I certainly don't want it in my backyard.

We're really close to finishing, and the storm is far away on the other side of the ocean. I don't think we're going to experience it before some time, but who knows? We need to finish the last repairs, calm the people down... just do all we can to get back to the normal flow of life. I'll set up a list with the last things we need to take care of.
