Strange, I've never heard of a creature like that, but I certainly don't want it in my backyard.

We're really close to finishing, and the storm is far away on the other side of the ocean. I don't think we're going to experience it before some time, but who knows? We need to finish the last repairs, calm the people down... just do all we can to get back to the normal flow of life. I'll set up a list with the last things we need to take care of.

Say, what a nice village Lord Walder has here! It would be a shame for it to be raided. Alright, I've had a meeting with the village council and got some interesting news. They want to kill two birds with one stone. Yes, exactly, while getting rid of the bandits, the council wants us to get rid of the pirates too, and they will pay us well. So let's go pirate and bandit hunting! First, we need to clear our way as they have blocked the southern roads with wooden walls.
The pirate leader seems very confused. No wonder - he's being attacked from both sides, poor fellow. I think it's time for him to consider a vacation, don't you think?
Before we reach the badlands, we need to cross the forest. Our scouts have reported some more bandit camps, so be careful!

The council has sent a scout after us. Apparently, the pirate leader has the deed of the island, a small scroll, and the council wants it back. I ordered some of our men to look for the scroll inside the compound, but they came back empty handed. However, fear not! One of the prisoners has told us the pirate leader has hidden the scroll on one of their pirate ships! We should send out some scouts to infiltrate the ships and look for it! Oh, and one more thing: burn the ships afterwards, just to be sure!

The bandits have erected a huge wooden wall at the entrance of the Badlands! I must say, it's quite impressive, isn't it? Sadly for them, even that wall won't stop our determination to get rid of them! We need to destroy at least one frontier camp, but if we destroy all three of them, we might find some sweet loot! Remember, we need to get rid of all the bandits!

We managed to capture a bandit who claims that their clan's name is "The Tropical Suns". Not really imaginative, if you ask me. That name doesn't make any sense. Hah, we should name ourselves "The Arctic Moons"...I bet that would make them as angry as a raging bull! Right, enough fooling around. We need to raid their camp and finish this whole charade once and for all! Enter the bandit leader's camp and clear it out!
Quick! We must find the time to travel to the Sunrimm Islands! There's something wrong at our friend Lord Walder's village!

To the southwest you'll find the raiders. We know they're really angry about all this vegetation, as they're used to living on barren land. Maybe it's too cold for them here, if they're used to a different, hotter climate? Who knows. All I know is we need to raid the raiders (he he), and clear the southwestern wing of the island!

Oh, the pirates! They're always so sneaky - you never know what to expect, really. I say we storm their encampment. That should teach them a lesson how to behave in a prison, or whatever this island is.

It's amazing that even on a nice island like this one, the Dark Cult can raise a tower. The construction looks menacing, but we shouldn't be intimidated by that, am I right? We need to climb to the top of the tower and clear the main chamber. I hope there are no spiders in the witch tower... I hate spiders!

There's something cold coming from the eastern wing of the island. I asked the Count and he told me he has some Nords captured over there. That's not good news - those people are crazy! We should tread carefully.

Count Hackett has asked us to clear all the Watchtowers that were occupied by the various clans. It shouldn't be a problem. Anyway, it has to be done if we want to access the other parts of the island, so… let's get to it.

Some of the captured prisoners have told us that each and every clan on this island has an invasion plan. They also told us these plans are hidden not in the main camps, but somewhere else. We should do a sweep of the island, and see if we can find the plans!

Have you heard? That prison island to the east is overwhelmed by the clans living on it. We should send a letter and see what's going on. Apparently, Count Hackett is the warden right now. Let’s deal with this problem as soon as possible!

There's a small island called Sleepy Reef where one of King Damien's ex-general lives. I've heard from a scout that there are traitors gathering around the island! This is not good news! We should head over there and stop them damaging the island and harming its citizens!
We need to fight our way through the mountains first. Then comes the forest, and eventually well reach Gregorid's village! Let's move!
Golly, this forest seems to be really dense. We're expecting the next traitor camp to be on the road to the village! Keep your eyes open!

There are two more camps before we reach the main one. One traitor camp is situated near the outskirts, and the other one is at the entrance to the village. I don't have to tell you what to do next, right?

One of the villagers has told me they saw Gregorid's daughter Sabilyn escaping the village! The villager also said she likes to hide in the forest, up in the trees. Great! We need to find her! Look in the forest or wherever you see trees!
The leader of the traitors is in the camp, grinding his teeth. That guy needs serious help - he looks completely crazy. All we have to do is storm the main camp and defeat the last of them!

A new cult has emerged on Flintrock island. They plan to revive an old sleeping volcano, and that would mean they're going to eventually burn the island to ashes. We should deal with this, as Flintrock is part of our alliance!

In order to get to the tower that is located somewhere around the middle of the island, we need to get to the village. But there are some strange towers blocking the road. We sent out a small scout group and they told us that the towers hold cult members. We need to destroy the towers so we can pass! Make it fast!

Argh! There's another tower right near the village! I wonder how they built these things so fast. Could these buildings be coming from underground? Regardless, we should destroy the next tower and head into the village.

I had a talk with the village elder. He is very grateful that we're here, and he told me an interesting secret. The mad alchemist in the tower made his flaming potion, the one he wants to revive the volcano with, using a special kind of bone dust. On this island there lived a creature that was able to combust. It was some kind of a weird lizard. Anyway, the old man told us that if we want to make sure that potion is never finished, or made again, we should find all the bones and destroy them. You heard the man! Let the search begin!

The tower stands tall over the sleeping volcano. We need to fight our way to the middle of the island and destroy the mad alchemist and all his towers and whatnots! The village elder told us that we're probably going to encounter more statues on our way, so we should be prepared.
We got an urgent letter that we must see too. Pack your bags, ready your generals, we're leaving as soon as possible!

The first sector that was occupied by the bandits is the forest, with all those woodcutters. It’s basically a lumberyard where the pirates used to get wood for their ships. We need to clear out the bandit camp!

You know how those pirates are always drinking that foul tasting special brew? Well they use some kind of special swamp reed to make it. Yes, you guessed right, the next bandit occupied sector is inside the swamp. We need to get to the bandit camp and destroy it!

The farms are situated on the north side of the island. They're harvesting the wheat to make more brew, but since the pirates retired, they've been breeding horses and baking bread. Well, the bandits just took control of the farms. Let's take it back.

Ohh. Well, the headquarters of the pirates, or the "pirate den", was occupied by the bandits. We need to breach the last line of their defences and reach the den. I must say, the veteran pirates turned the den into a nice garden villa. Nice.
The pirates also asked us to burn down the woodcutter huts inside the forest. They want us to keep them from ever building a ship again. Not sure about burning, but we'll definitely destroy them.
Wait! We need to find the special reeds and destroy them as well. So the retired pirates want to retire for good, eh? It feels like cleaning up, really.
What's this? Our scout reports that the bandits know we're here, and they've poisoned some of the crops! We should destroy the poisoned wheat fields before this gets out of hand! Let's get to it!

Our scout reported Nords activity on an abandoned island. He told us they've unloaded several barrels onto the shore. We have no idea what they're planning, but we need to take care of this matter! We can't risk another Nords invasion!
The island appears to be infested with Nords. We should clear out the camps one by one, and drive them back, but which order should we attack in? I say we should focus on the medium camps first!
It seems there are some stronger Nords camps around the island. I think they're protecting something! Maybe those barrels? Let's clear the camps out and find out more!
Yes, it's just as we thought! The barrels they want to detonate are all around the island! We should find them and throw them into the water! Find the handcarts that are loaded with the barrels!

Wait wait wait! There seem to be even more barrels around the island, hidden inside some wooden crates! It seems we didn't manage to destroy all of them in one run. Quick, let's find the remaining crates!

There is one particular stronghold on a small island in the middle of the… island. On this small island, there is a huge Nords fortress, and I guess that's their headquarters, if they even have something like that. It would be wise to destroy it. That would lower their morale, if they have any, that is. Let's try to fight our way in and destroy it.

Count Hackett from Capital island wants to build a prison on a small, star-shaped tropical island. It's not a bad idea, but to use a whole island for that… I don't think it's efficient. Anyway, we need to help them because we're going to encounter more bad guys, and it's better for the Count to take care of them!
Prisons have strong walls, so how about sending them some good quality stone?
The Count wants a repository of food sealed off from the prisoners, and we've been asked to provide the bread!
The builders hired to build the outposts have asked us for some fish. I say, let's send them some!
There is some heavy cargo that needs to be moved up and then down the ships. I think we we'll need some horses for that!
Since there are wild animals roaming the area, the guards will need weapons to save the prisoners from animal attacks. Deliver the guards some crossbows.
Each watchtower will need to have at least one cannon on top to defend against wild animals. Some of them will be installed in the mountains. Better safe than sorry!
Sir Rogen, one of our oldest generals, is due for retirement. Given that he won so many battles for us, I think we should set up a retirement plan for him.
We're going to need some resources we don't own. Luckily, our neighbour has them. Let's get friendly and help our allies out a bit!
Sir Rogen always said that allies are the most important weapon when it comes to a battle! We'd best keep that in mind! Let us help some of our allies with some goodies!

Sir Rogen deserves the best! We want to honour him with some great events! One of them would be the fountain dance! Water isn't just for fish and drinks, is it? The only problem is, we'll need a lot of it - those fountains were never refilled.

We're holding some goodbye events for Sir Rogen. One of them is a march of the last army he commanded. They're going to get in line, shoot some cannons, stuff like that. Off to the barracks - let's see if we can get that army on its feet!
In order to honour Sir Rogen, we're going to take him on an adventure one last time. As a spectator, that is.

As Sir Rogen leaves by ship, we'd like to shoot flaming arrows into the air. It's a tradition that was introduced to us a short time ago, a great way to honour our elders... or burn a city to the ground! Either way, we need longbows.

Up on Flintrock island, the villagers told one of our merchants that the whole island sits on top of a sleeping volcano - and they want to keep it that way. But last week there was a small eruption, and a hole appeared. A smoking one. They need our help to bury and seal that hole as soon as possible.
We need to get some blocks of stone to the middle of the island and there are a lot of swamps along the way. If we use enough pinewood planks, we can build some smaller roads or bridges, if needed.
We are going to use bronze cauldrons to transport the material to the hole. So guess what - in order to make bronze cauldrons, we're going to need some copper ore!
We're going to fill in the hole using marble! That way we can be sure to prevent any incident that might awaken the volcano!
We'd like to assign a small group of guards to protect our people while they're on Flintrock island. Equip them with some iron swords!
We're going to need some strong people to help us with our project. The strongest I can think of are a group of soldiers! Let's train some!
We've received a message that some ill-intentioned people want to intercept our shipments. I think we should make the first move!
Great news! King Damien is ordering a new royal ship and has invited us to participate in the project! I can't imagine a greater honour right now! We need to do our best!

Delivering all the required resources might turn out to be a tad too hard, and we may end up requesting help from our allies. I'm not sure how things will go yet, but it's probably best to strengthen our relations in any case. You'd better get on it.
A royal ship should contain all the goods a king and his guests may require. The King has asked us personally to fill the ship's hold with our quality brew!
Some of our recruits want to become sailors on the royal ship! They will be representing our guild, so I guess we should give them some proper training before we send them over to Capital Island.
One of our ships ran into a storm but was saved by one of our allies. We should thank them immediately! The ship is already on its way to Capital Island, and I'm glad to report the cargo is intact!

I've made a small miscalculation here! It seems we've delivered a little too much meat to Capital Island, and now we're running low ourselves. Just to avoid any problems, we should refill some meat deposits!
The ships even set sail at night, and we can't risk losing them! I've decided to place some longbowmen aboard to signal the ships using flaming arrows so they don't get lost. Train some longbowmen.

One of our explorers has found a yet unexplored valley! He claims to have seen lions there, and some ancient looking ruins too! This all sounds too exciting! The King wants us to find some time and prepare an expedition!
If there are lions we had better make some quality lure to capture some! Just imagine: our own lion! Please prepare some sausages - I bet they love sausages!
We're not aware of the quality of terrain inside the valley, so we should send some horsemen too. It's never bad to have some horses around. Train some cavalry!
We have no idea what awaits us inside the valley, so we should make sure our explorers and guards are prepared. Get some nice bronze swords ready for them!
The expedition to the valley needs to be well equipped. We can't expect our explorers and guards to carry around those huge bags, so we should loan them some horses!
Our explorers will eventually get hungry, and I believe one of them is a really good cook. Pack them some meat - let them have a feast or two!

The head of the exploration, our Master Explorer, has asked us for a Golden Brew Mug. Every time he leaves on a big exploration mission, he drinks his brew from a Golden Mug. I think we have one somewhere, right?

There's nothing better than waking up in the morning and having a good old piece of honey bread! Sadly, our supplier from Pollon has stopped his shipments because he has a problem with his bees! We should try and help!
The honey supplier says he wants to build a stone wall around the field where he keeps the beehives. He's asked for some stone.
I decided to loan the supplier some of our recruits, you know, to guard the area and all that. Check the barracks!

Did you know that bees prefer meat? No? Me neither. The honey supplier claims meat can be used to lure the bees to a certain spot, where the most flowers are. We need to send him some meat, but be sure to refill our deposits first!
One of our allies appears to be an expert when it comes to bees, and he has given us some great tips about how to deal with them. I think we should thank our ally for the help!
If it turns out the origin of the problem is the wildlife living in the surrounding woods, we might need to send over some army units. Please check our troop count!
We should send out a General and some troops to scout the surrounding islands. Maybe they'll be able to find the origin of the problem.

Today we've received two guests from an island called Booth, sent by King Damien himself. They seem to be brothers, and are trying out a new way of building a sort of underground tunnel system called 'sewers'. I've no idea why is that a good thing. Help them with their first experiment.

Before they started digging, they asked us about the famous Fish Platter we eat around here. They would love to try some of the fish we have. The smaller brother seems slightly overweight, and looks hungry, so we had better get a decent amount of fish.
There's a feeling these tests might end up being a little messy. We should check our troop count to make sure we have enough units if something happens and we have to deal with it.
The brothers managed to dig some tunnels, but apparently they also want to clean them. That's going to require quite a lot of water…
While the brothers are doing their digging, we should focus on our troops, especially recruits. How about sending them for a fight or two?
The brothers will need some strong tools so they can dig properly. I suggest you provide them with some iron, and let them make their own weird tools.
The brothers' digging seems to be a little bit too loud. Many animals have been seen fleeing the sector. We should check our deposits and maybe fill them up!

There is a report here. A ship that was bound for Capital Island is going to stop for a quick break, and we need to welcome them. They're transporting some special kind of furniture for one of the lords. We should help them. For a price, of course.

They're holding the furniture on stone blocks. We were asked what kind of stone we produce here on the island. I had to ask one of our people from the quarry to answer that. Apparently, we have the right kind of stone.
It seems the ship's crew is bored of the food they get each day. The first mate smelled our morning bread, and now he wants to surprise the others. Let's give him some fresh bread.

The captain came to me this morning. The ship has to be in excellent condition when it arrives at Capital Island, but right now, one of the ornaments on the eastern mast is damaged thanks to a storm they run into. He wants us to get him some marble so he can have his crew fix the ornament.

Oh! I've had a fisherman here complaining that the fancy ship has dropped anchor directly over his school of fish. I've had the ship moved, but I think we should help the fisherman out and refill his fish deposit!
The Captain is ready to pay a small fortune if we'll agree to take him on an adventure. I've asked the commander, and he's said yes.
While the ship is here, I've decided to invite the Captain to have dinner with us. I think it would make a good impression to let him have some of our finest brew in a Gold Mug!

Listen to this! They want to use birds to send letters! There's a bird-master who arrived just this morning to set up a pigeon post on the island! Sounds interesting... I mean, imagine how fast the mail could be sent and received!
The pigeons will need a specially built coop so we can breed them there. I would use pinewood planks if I were you!
We're going to need someone with a lot of patience to train the pigeons. I think using some recruits would be the best idea!

We need a special kind of bird food that can't be acquired easily. Our commander has mentioned he knows which seeds we're looking for, and he'll bring some back the next time he goes on an adventure. We've urged him to go now.
The bird-master wants to set up a smaller water system for the pigeons. Yes, you've guessed right - he needs some water.

According to the bird-master, pigeons not only eat seeds, but bread too, believe it or not! Doh… do we look that stupid? Anyway, he needs some bread so he can feed the pigeons. A waste of good bread, if you ask me.
The bird-master says that sadly, the pigeon coop will attract predators, probably eagles and other beasts. He's asked us for some longbows so he can protect his pigeons.

There is a young man here called Mike, and he's a very talented composer. He has a wooden guitar, and many folks have heard him playing it, back in the day when he lived in the mountains. Some old women say this young man's music is so enchanting, it can change seasons. Imagine getting rid of this cold winter and having spring arrive the next minute? Let's build the man a new home and make him feel welcome. Maybe he'll sing for us!
A good house has to be built of the finest planks. I've asked Mike to play for our settlers while they’re building him his new home!
He gave me a look at some really interesting instrument designs. I think if we can get enough hardwood, we might be able to make him some of these instruments!
Mike likes to play music but he also needs to eat, like everyone else. How about surprising him with a nice meal? Some sausages will do the trick!
Mike wants to write a song that would represent our armies, so we're going to need some marching cavalry to inspire him!
Mike is looking for inspiration, so he's asked us to take him to some wild lands. The commander will take him on an adventure.
Mike thinks that different emotions would trigger different rhythms in his heart. I think we should send him out on an adventure with one of your generals.
Fantastic news! Do you remember Sir Arminus, the long lost general? Apparently he has been found on a small island and would like to come home! We need to prepare a proper welcome!
One thing is sure: Sir Arminus loves his Saturday fish meal! Yes, it was some kind of a tradition at his house. Send his family some fish so they can prepare the meal!

His family's old home has been abandoned ever since he left. It's a cold and sad place these days. Let's heat the old place up, light a fire in the chimney, prepare a nice hot bath, that kind of stuff. You'll need to provide the coal.
Sir Arminus will arrive on the other side of the island, so we had better send over some horses. He loved horse riding - imagine how excited he will be.
Oh! While preparing for the welcome party, the family has found a sinkhole in the backyard! We should fix it as soon as possible using hardwood planks!
Sir Arminus was in charge of a brave army made of soldiers back in his golden days. Let's honour him for that! Prepare soldiers at the barracks!
The moment Sir Arminus arrives at the Mayor's Office, he will be awarded a medal! We want him to get the most out of the ceremony, and enjoy the whole experience, so prepare a Golden Brew Mug!

What do you know about Eagle Nest? Nothing? Let me enlighten you! Eagle Nest is a small fortress on top of that mountain there. Yes, the tallest one. The fortress has been raided by some bandits! We need to find a way to clear them out!
The bandits have destroyed the stone stairs that led up the mountain. I'm still not sure if it was intentional or just an accident. We need to carry some stone with us and fix the gaps.
Our general has done a count, and in his opinion our army is not big enough. We need more recruits in order to take back Eagle Nest!
The bandits have burned down most of the surrounding woods, and most of the wildlife has fled the area! We need to refill those deposits, fast!
The general leading this mission is not sure the army recruits are ready for such an encounter! He wants them to experience some combat first!

I know it sounds stupid, but Eagle Nest got its name because of the actual eagles living here. The eagles get agitated with all this fighting, and it’s dangerous for our troops to climb while being attacked. However, we have found a solution: fish! They love fish! Let's give them some!
The general wants to take along a Golden Brew Mug. He claims it will bring him luck in the upcoming battle at Eagle Nest.

There has been a terrible war in the land to the west, and the King's Elite Army was involved. Sadly, they were heavily wounded and must return to Capital Island to recover. Together with the other guilds, we need to lend a helping hand.
The Elite Army has some very unusual rules and habits. Apparently, all they eat while they're on a mission is wheat and anything that can be made from it. I think we should send them some wheat!
Each time the army is defeated, they like to sculpt the face of their enemy in marble. We're not going to ask why. Just prepare a marble block for them - we should have plenty, right?
The Fallen Army has a book, and we've received a copy of one of the chapters about recruit training. They want us to give them tactical feedback. We need to check it out.
Some of the fallen military units have asked to join us on our adventures. We can't say no - they need to stay in shape! Let's help!
The general of the Fallen Army has asked us to take some of his officers to experience an adventure. I guess he doesn't want them to get lazy.
Sadly, there were many wounded units. The doctor from Capital Island has asked for a number of carriages - he wants to turn them into small vehicles to help some of the wounded units move around.

We've received a letter from some settlers that used to have a colony on this island: they want to come back. Apparently they left the island in hope of a better life, but the road they’ve chosen has lead nowhere. I guess we can lend them a small part of the island. Prepare for their arrival.
We need to prepare some proper shelter for these people. I guess some stone houses would do the job. We can build them inside the forest so they won't need any additional structure. We need stone.

The colonists will need food and all sorts of agricultural tools to work the land, and weapons to defend their homes. The best we can do is send them some of our swords - our farmers are very fond of their multipurpose abilities.
Some of our people have heard about the new colony and want to go live there for a while. Good idea - it'll help them get used to our ways faster.
We need to set up a perimeter around the forest where our new guests will be settling. We don't want the pirates or anyone to harm them. Prepare some cavalry!
There are so many people wanting to help out that we’re going to run out of people to do any actual work. To avoid that, we need to get some more settlers up to the Mayor's House.
We considered preparing a nice feast for them, but the forest soil isn't great for holding a table steady. We'll need a lot strong exotic wood planks for this!

We've just heard from your cousin, Theodor. He's moved to a desert island and formed a community. I've no idea how he managed it. He has written to say he's in trouble though - surprise surprise - and needs your help. Again. His little settlement is in the middle of the desert and the sun is their biggest enemy. He needs help to save his community.
We're going to need help transporting the goods to Theodor's island, so it would be a good idea to pay a visit to our friends and take a gift!
We need to take some recruits with us. They will serve well as basic defence - I mean who's going to attack a deserted island with a small, poor town in the middle?
Theodor loves sausages, and so does the whole community, apparently. We have to bring him some - remember the last time we forgot? Ugh.
Theodor's first defence general has asked us to bring along some fine longbows so he can set up a guard on the outer walls. Sure, why not.
We've heard the town has some broken walls. I know, Theodor is family and all that, but are you sure you want to fix those walls using exotic wood planks? Really? Alright…
Theodor has asked us to take his field general to experience an adventure. For training.

The weather report we received today was not a promising one. It seems we're going to experience a lot of rain, and there's even a chance of huge storms. Just to be sure, let's prepare for a rainy year.
Using some stone, we should start reinforcing some of our workyards and other buildings. We don't need to make it too official though - let's call it 'renovation'.

It's well known that fish become more active when there's a lot of rain. I fear that the rain will stay limited to the northern parts of the island, and the fish might migrate there. Refill the fish deposits, just to make sure we won't run out.

In case we can't manage, the only way to get help is by asking Capital Island or our friends. I would stick to the second option - you know how hard it is to get anything from the King. Taking that into consideration, we should visit a friend and help out where we can.

Hardwood is the only wood that is resistant to water. That's why it's a good idea to build roofs using hardwood. Some of our residences don't have the proper kind of roofs, and in order to replace them we'll need hardwood.

The surrounding wilderness is particularly dangerous during heavy rain, with all the wolves and such, so we must set up an emergency guard around our villages. Prepare some fine steel swords for the guards!
We need to honour the new rainy year, and the best way to do that is by celebrating. Bring out a Golden Brew Mug - let's do this the proper way!

The Miner's Union has found an abandoned chamber with a huge gate blocking the way deeper into the cave system. They somehow managed to open it and found another, bigger chamber. It seems like an underground jungle of sorts. We need to explore it!

While we're exploring the mine, we'll need somebody to take care of the island. How about a quick visit? Go see your friend, take a gift with you, and hope that while we're busy you'll receive something in return!
Most of the paths inside the underground jungle are high up on rocks. Taking melee units won't be of any help - we need bowmen for this one!

We've found a circular tunnel around the underground jungle. There are a lot of cracks on the site, if you look through you can see the jungle. I say we place some longbowmen in these tunnels - if any harm comes our way, our people can protect us.

It's true that the Miner's Union has managed to open the gates to the underground jungle, but we might encounter some more obstacles as we go deeper. It would probably be best to have some tools to bring along.

Given that we know there's some kind of life deep in the underground jungle, we might even encounter humans. The best way to make new friends is to gift, and the most impressive type of gift is gold. Bring some gold ore along.

The entrance to underground jungle is partially flooded by a lake. Fishermen use this lake to fish, but we need to clear the way. We've made a deal with the fisherman in the area to fill up another deposit for him.

Every year we celebrate the "Day of the Sailors" event. Practically the entire island is flooded with sailors for a day, and we organize various events for them and share the fun. This year it's our island's turn to hold the event, so let's get to work!

A sailor's favorite food is fish, there's no doubt about that, so we've hired Piero, the world famous cook, to prepare the perfect fish soup! He is going to use a ray-finned fish called Alosa agone. What a name!
One of the most beloved events is marble pulling. Basically, two teams have to pull a block of marble from one point to another, and guess what? We have to provide the marble block!

As funny as it might sound, sailors love to catch fish with their bare hands. They sure do look funny while they're doing it. We need to fill some deposits and make sure we have enough fish for them to have fun with!
We need to designate a gift to give to the leader of the Sailor's Crew. The best one would be a Golden Brew Mug!
The sailors want to try out some melee combat, but they're used to different kinds of swords. We should prepare some fine steel swords for them to parley with!
Some of the sailors want to tag along on an adventure. They're allowed to join in as soldiers.

Up there, far to the north, are some islands that never really experience proper sunshine. It's always dark up there. No wonder they're called the Dark Lands. We're taking part of a initiative to help the people who live there.
I bet those lands have great stocks of minerals under the infinite looking snow fields, but I'm sure they're having a hard time mining them out. For starters, we should send them shipments of stone.
Hardwood can be used for many things, like housing, guard towers, boats, etc. I think a reasonable amount of hardwood would make a great gift!
We need to find someone who can help us deliver some of the gifts to the Dark Lands. I would advise a little useful diplomacy: visit a friend and lend a helping hand!

Landing on the shores of the Dark Lands will be hard, and we're expecting dangerous wildlife. Polar bears, white wolves, and who knows what else await us! We should train some militia and take them along for protection!
We're going to need a lot of food for the voyage, and it seems we've depleted some of our wildlife deposits. Before we leave, it would be a good idea to refill them.
Ohh no! One of the transport ship has sprung a leak! We need to fix it as soon as possible! The ship was built using a lot of exotic wood planks, so fixing it will require more!

Capital Island has many gardens but nothing that compares with the Royal Gardens. The King is really proud of this. He wants every guild to come and have their own garden inside the Royal Gardens. I guess it's a question of status, I don't know. We should load up, go to Capital Island, and make our own garden.
Since our friends have heard we're going to have our own garden, they keep sending us all kinds of gifts. In return, the logical move would be to thank them before we leave for Capital Island.
There should be plenty of trees in that garden, but we don’t want to harm them. If we want to build ivy hangers, tables, and benches, we're going to need to bring our own hardwood.
Our general has told us our military units could use some action before we leave. It would be a good idea to have a field drill.
We need to take along a lot of workers, but we don't want the island to lack working settlers. You should bring some new ones as soon as possible!

Some of our settlers have told me they're going to join our trip because they want to visit Capital Island. I can't say no really -they've never been off the island before. However, we will need to find people to replace them while they're away.

The King says that each and every guild garden should be guarded by soldiers. This means we need to bring along some soldiers, but I wouldn't choose the best ones. I mean, they'll need to stand in one place for a long time and not let people in, right?

There's a man in the lobby. He said his name is Will Fixit. That's a rather weird name if you ask me. He's a contractor, and for a small fee he can improve a number of things around our village, some of which I never even thought needed changing. His reasoning is quite convincing, so I suggest we give him a shot!
Will Fixit has told me the most important thing is to have good relations with thy neighbour. We do, I told him, but he insisted I take him along for a visit. Come with us.

Will Fixit believes our village defence isn't faulty, but he did have one comment. Although we have plenty of recruits walking around, he didn't see any bowmen on the top of any houses or towers. And he's right - there aren't. Let's train some bowmen and get them in place.
Will Fixit says we need a statue in the middle of the village that represents somebody powerful. Can't think of anyone yet, but let's provide the marble block for it.

The fish we've been using to cook our meals, like the Fish Platters, aren't the proper breed. I didn't even know there were several different breed around here. Will Fixit has done something to the fish school, and now he wants us to get some fish.
Will Fixit has observed our villagers' diet and tells us he's a little concerned with our meat consumption. He suggests we eat more Fish. Also he's kind of worried about the way we treat our horses.
Will Fixit wants to tag along on an adventure so he can evaluate our military forces. Our general has some negative feelings about this, but he's finally given in.

Do you know Lord Addam? Yes, Addam, with two d's. He was sailing past our island when a small storm hit his ship, the Pink Karotten. Eventually he was able to recover his crew, but he lost his most precious belongings: his white pets - a cat, a parrot, and monkey. He's asked us to help him find them.
First, we have to fix Lord Addam's ship, so we need to get some pinewood planks for his crew to start the repairs!

Lord Addam fears his pets may have been stolen by one of the pirate ships that have been stalking him for a while. If that's true, and there are indeed pirates in the vicinity of the island, we should make sure we're prepared!

In order to find the pets, we've sent out some messages to our neighbours! Some of them have already started to look for the pets! We should visit their island and thank them for the help! Bring a gift!
If we want to find the pets fast, we'll need more manpower. I would advise you to call upon some of our recruits - they move fast on land and have good knowledge of the surroundings.

We've assigned a lot of settlers to the search team. So many, that we're almost out of working settlers, and we can't afford to stop all work! I would like to ask you to get a new workforce for the island!
Lord Addam says that his pets are not really the kind you can… pet. They might get aggressive when they're away from him. Looks like we should train some soldiers and take them along, just in case…

A very particular group of five people arrived at the local inn last night. They call themselves "The Wizards" and they're looking for somebody on our island. They've asked for our assistance. Want to hear what's weirder? They didn't come by ship, they just appeared. Let's help them quickly, so they will leave as soon as possible.

One of them came to me and asked for some fish. He looked really hairy and was somewhat scared of my every move. I was scared of him too to be honest. I think we should just give him some fish and be done with it.

One of them walks and talks funny. His skin is really silvery, unnatural if you ask me! Anyway, he was interested in seeing our military force. I walked him around the barracks, but he wants to see the actual training process. Invite him to see how we train our recruits.
The thin guy wants bread. He reminded me of a scarecrow - thin as a rake. I told him to come back later. Prepare some bread for him please.

There is a girl with them, but she looks really sad. She kept telling me she wants to go home, and how she misses her friends. Then she asked me if I have any friends. I told her that I do - plenty. She wants me to take her to one of my friends. Want to join us? Please?
The tallest of them seems to be their leader. He has glasses and looks like he won't take no for an answer. He wants to borrow some of our cavalry to help him move around the island.
They've started to look for whatever they came for. I think we should keep on good terms with them, so let's honour them with our Gold Brew Mug.

You remember the island of Countess Zavora? A scout returned today with the news that the island is surrounded by a thick layer of mist. The scout ventured deeper and it appears the whole island is dead. Then, when he reached the Countess' manor, he saw her. Problem is, as everyone knows, she's been dead for years. It would be wise to investigate.

Some weird things have been happening since the scout came back. There was a huge fire out on the farms, and we lost some wheat. It would be good to help the farmers get their stocks back before we leave.

The scout's first stop was one of your friends' islands! There are reports of unusual lights inside many residences - the people are scared. How about we pay your friend a visit, and try and calm down the "spirits"?

The weirdest thing - Samuel the Deerstalker told me that last night he arrived at the fields where he usually hunts, and saw hundreds of animals gathering around a person standing in the middle. Unfortunately, he then stepped on a twig, the sound scared all the animals away, and the person was nowhere to be seen. We need to refill the field with wildlife before we leave.

Hey! The merchant told me that last night he had a weird customer, and as the guy was leaving, all the iron swords started dancing out after him. His wife confirms the story's true too. Hmm, I think they must have been tired or something. Anyway, let's help the merchant out with some iron swords before we leave.

Some settlers have reported a silvery wave of flame burning through the woods. The huge... well I suppose you'd call it a fire, has scared away most of the wildlife, and the hunters who work around here aren't happy. We should refill the wildlife before we leave to check out that island.
Our general claims he found a message carved on the side of an adventuring ship this morning. He insists we tag along before we go investigate the island!

It's here! Finally! The Day of the Frogs! Every four years we celebrate the great travelling frogs. When winter is nigh, they leave the northern ponds and migrate to the southern ponds. The event requires us to assure safe passage for the frogs that will cross our village!

For the frogs to find the right way, we need to fry some fish and form a trail using fried fish bits. The frogs will eat and follow the trail. Don't give me that look - it's how our grandfathers did it! Bring me some fish.

Birds of prey have been spotted near the frog trail - the frogs are an easy target for them on their journey. I urge you to call upon our elite Bowmen to guard the trail. We will have to compensate them though, as they're on their well-earned vacation at the moment.

We need to take out our bronze swords and let the frogs jump over them. That way we can get the blessing of the frogs. Yes, there are some recruits who believe this brings good luck in combat. Prepare some new bronze swords.
Our friend came by today and helped us prepare the frog trail. You should visit as soon as possible and return the favor!

Just imagine - our esteemed neighbours seems to have acquired a taste for frogs' legs. I suggest we send a little gift basket of sausages to satiate any appetite they might have, just so they don't get any ideas when seeing our frogs wandering about… Maybe we should sprinkle some units along our borders too, just to be sure.
Wait a second! Our general says that some military units have left their post so they can see the frog trail! Without official leave! Have an army check this out - it can’t be true!

There's a group of people here from Capital Island. They're the Wildlife Control Group, and surprisingly enough, they're here to check out our wildlife. After two days of research, they've come back with a long list. We need to fix the issues they've noted as soon as possible, or our guild may receive a fine!

They saw we're big on fishing and want to know how we treat our fish. I wanted to tell them what we kill them and eat them, but decided not to overshare. They've asked for some fish they can check. Bring them the fish, carefully.

We have been recommended to build shelter for our deer population in order to contain it a little better. Our hunters might also be grateful for that, actually. I hear some of them have been visiting our neighbour's islands lately in order to fulfill their quota...

They want to check our horses, so we have to bring them out to the field near the stables. It'll look like some kind of a horse show. I don’t want to mislead the settlers into thinking we’re holding an event and they weren't invited.

The Wildlife Control Group has reached the barracks and they want to know how many military units we have. When I asked them why they want to know, they said it's part of their routine. Please have an army check.

The Wildlife Control Group has noticed there are way too many predatory birds around our island. I don't see that as a problem, but they want us to form a longbowman unit to protect animals from the predators, if it becomes necessary. Let's train some longbowmen then.

The Wildlife Control Group has found a lake, although they say there isn't the required amount of fish in it. Did they count them, or what? How do they know that? Anyway, what's the point of arguing. Just refill the fish school and make them happy.

We've been contacted by the dean of the Village School regarding an urgent matter. Winter is closing in, and he wants the children to experience the same kind of fun they get in summer. Yep, he wants the children to have fun in the snow! Now there's an interesting guild project!

One of your friends owns a small workshop that can make sledges for children to use in winter. You should pay him a visit, help out, and maybe your friend will tell you the secret of how to make them!

There' going to be a snowball competition, so how about we make the kids a decent target? I say we use a marble block and have our sculptors carve it into something. The children can then use the marble statue as target practice! Snowball fun to the maximum!
A friend of yours used to make these amazing candy canes. Children *really* love candy canes! You should visit your friend, help out a bit, and maybe get the recipe!

Ice skating is great fun, but we can’t trust winter to froze our lakes solid, and imagine if there are any accidents! What we can do however is dig a smaller hole and fill it with some water. The small quantity will freeze solid for sure, when the right time comes! Let's store some water for when the winter comes!
We need to assign some settlers to prepare the winter games for the children. We should replace them with some new settlers, don't you think?

There is a tale of a very friendly breed of deer. It would heighten the mood to have some nice deer in the city when winter comes. The only problem is, we've no idea where to find them. Luckily, the general does, and he wants to go look.

A man has landed on our island in a very weird flying basket attached to a huge balloon. He claims to have come from the Floating Island! Have you ever heard anything so absurd? He has asked us to help him repair his flying machine. Let's do it.
He needs some stones to use as weights. Apparently, to float higher, he'll release a few bags holding the stones, but what if they hit anyone?
While helping the balloon guy, we noticed the basket landed right on a fish school. The local fisherman is really angry. We should refill his fish school.

The balloon guy has asked us for a partial escort. When his balloon is repaired, he will leave our island and head south. He wants us to escort him for a while by ship. We should take along some longbowmen in case we run into pirates.
While gathering the tools to fix his balloon, our guest would like to take a look around some other islands as well. This is great because we can ask our general to take him along an adventure.

While fixing a thing he calls an 'engine', something happened and there was a huge explosion. Not big enough to hurt anyone, but it was so loud it scared away most of the wildlife. We need to refill our wildlife in the area!

The balloon guy is about to finish his repairs, but he needs some strong men to help push the balloon toward the creek. I think we should designate some soldiers from the barracks to help - they're the strongest units after all.

The King has sent us a letter. Again. He says Warden Tatral is to build one of the biggest prisons ever built. The King has given Warden Tatral an island where he is to build the prison he intends to call "The Vault". Apparently, this prison will only hold really dangerous people. We've been asked to play a part in the planning and building of The Vault.
Warden Tatral wants to build a very interesting prison. One of the levels will be made mostly from wood. Don't ask me why. We need to prepare a shipment of pinewood planks!
There's going to be a patrol drill around the prison island, and we’ve been asked to provide some recruits for it. I think the guys will be happy to get out the barracks and just patrol.
Warden Tatral doesn't like walking. He prefers to be on horseback, and demands his guard should be mounted as well. The King has told him our horses are the best, so we're to bring over some horses!
Warden Tatrak is considering hiring some of our units, but first he wants to see them in real combat. The general agreed to take Warden Tatral along. Let's see a battle with recruits!
Warden Tatral needs to learn about military tactics before he can make plans for his prison guards. The general has offered to take the Warden on an adventure.

Warden Tatral tells us his island has no wildlife, and has asked us if he can take one or two hundred animals. Yes, well, of course he can, but we'll need to refill as soon as possible, or our hunters will have problems hunting.

Far to the south are the desert islands. Every now and then, a caravan comes visiting our island, opens the bazaar, and trades with our settlers. It's called "The Yellow Caravan" because… well, because it's yellow. We need to ensure that all the trading goes peacefully, and our guests feel welcomed.
Our friend is very sad the Caravan couldn't visit, so why don't we visit them instead? And let's take some gifts!

Our travelling friends have asked if they can restock provisions for their next big journey. They know of our baker's excellent reputation and would like to buy some bread. Also, they plan on venturing into some dangerous regions, and ask if we have any spare military they can hire.
The leader of the Caravan has told me their archers couldn't make it this year, and has asked whether we can lend him some of our longbowmen. Let's train some at the barracks!
The Caravan leader would appreciate some decent conversation, and wants to meet some of your friends! Why not visit and bring along the leader?

The Caravan contains a lot of birds, and they seem to be running out of seeds to feed them. I've offered the leader some of our wheat seeds, but he would rather feed them our bread. Alright - bread it is.

The Caravan leader has asked us if there's any way to get cannons at the market. We told him that it is indeed possible, but for some reason he doesn't want to go there. Let's go and buy him some cannons.

My faithful friend, I need your help! A few days ago I was eating some jam when some flies settled on it. I killed them all with just one blow!
Anyway, I wanted to let the whole world know, and made a belt describing the deed. Here, look! I've engraved “Seven in one fell swoop!” on it.
Unfortuantely, people have misunderstood, and think I killed seven men with one blow. Sadly, I realised this too late. Now the King thinks I’m a very strong fighter and has sent me on a quest to kill two Giants.
Giants! They can easily kill whole armies. How am I supposed to deal with one, let alone two? Can you help me with this? All of the King's rewards shall be yours.
The king seemed impressed, but now he wants me to catch an unicorn. Killing Giants is one thing, they're dumb and can be fooled, but Unicorns possess magical powers and know how to use them.

I've just returned from seeing the King. Though he said he was impressed, he didn't look quite as pleased as I had anticipated. He has given me one final quest, and promised to make me rich if I succeed. If you help me one last time, I’ll give you most of the promised treasure. We need to capture a furious boar which is terrorizing the land!

Help! Help! The King has broken his promise, and now he wants to kill me. He says I’m too dangerous, so he keeps sending me on quests where I'm sure to meet my death! Oh, I wish I'd never made that cursed belt… I barely escaped his soldiers, but they'll be here any minute!

War. Such a short word for something so powerful. It’s a good thing we have never been faced with a war - the battles we fight pale in comparison. But yes, war is raging at the outer rims of the kingdom, and, alongside his generals, our King Damien is doing his best to keep trouble from our gates. One of our kingdom's armies, the Ewanian Pioneers, is known to be composed of the most extraordinary soldiers this world has ever seen. It is the elite army of the King, and now they're at war at the rim, and a new darkness is rising. The King has ordered us all to establish an aid plan - we need to support them with all we've got, and as soon as possible!

The liberation of Randomar has taken grave toll on the King's troops. Right now every bit of help is welcome to get our men back on their feet again. They are short on food, and the barren rocks of Randomar provide hardly any shelter during the freezing nights. Let's provide what we can to help out our Pioneers!

Why were our esteemed Pioneers sent to Randomar in the first place, you're asking? Well, those barbarians have been intercepting our trade routes for decades, and were harassing our settlements, stealing whatever they could get their hands on. It's time to recover the stolen goods now! Send some Specialists to see what goods can be regained, and get rid of any spoils of war we might have in stock ourselves!

Only now have we discovered that the clan lords puppeteering the barbaric raids have taken to a desolate mountain keep - Dust Hold they dub it. And here we were thinking we had swiftly brought peace to these shaken lands... Nevertheless, before we embark on any military action again, let's send out our Pioneers in the spirit of peace and spread distribute to the civilians!

The King requests reinforcements. He wants to recruit some of our Veterans to take over Dust Hold. We will offer our most proficient men. The current bandit activities around our own settlement will give us some opportunity to survey our armies and identify the most able fighters.

It is an honour for our troops to join the king's legendary Pioneers and aid in the conquest of Dust Hold. We have to make sure our men have the best equipment at their disposal. Gather our master smiths and provide the best materials. There is little time though - Dust Hold is re-arming, and marching orders have been given. No time to lose!

We need to ramp up our standing army now. We might have to extend our economy in places, so make sure we have a basic army in place, that our boys are fit for when the King arrives with his detailed requests, and we have provided any goods needed to improve the speed of our recruitment process.

This is Dust Hold's doing! They are instigating riots in our vicinity to sidetrack us and weaken our support for the King's troops! Quickly - we must suppress the upheaval before things get out of hand! And make sure you keep our troops in good shape, so they are ready on call when the King's orders reach us!

This is it. The King's messenger reached us this morning. The King is inspecting troops from all Islands, and only the best are being accepted to join his elite forces. His demands are quite specific and there is not much time, so no dawdling - we must merit the King's trust in us!

Our scouts report great advances on the frontlines. Victory seems within reach. This is heartening news. Let's not fail to provide support for our troops though - repair and recovery is crucial out there. In the meantime, we must also not let control of our borderland territories slip. We should constantly have scouts patrolling our borders to keep an eye on those bandit-infested regions.

This is outrageous! We have got word from the Royal Advisor that Dust Hold is receiving support deliveries, the origin of which was tracked back to our borderland islands! It seems bandits on the borders of our Settlement are supplying the very barbarian stronghold our troops are currently battling! We must act immediately, rally troops, build the fastest ships we can, and purge those islands!

Well, those barbarians have been intercepting our trade routes for decades, and were harassing our settlements, stealing whatever they could get their hands on. It's time to recover the stolen goods now! Send some Specialists to see what goods can be regained, and get rid of any spoils of war we might have in stock ourselves!

Only now have we discovered that the clan lords puppeteering the barbaric raids have taken to a desolate mountain keep - Dust Hold they dub it. And here we were thinking we had swiftly brought peace to these shaken lands... Nevertheless, before we embark on any military action again, let's send out our Pioneers in the spirit of peace and spread distribute to the civilians!

The King requests reinforcements. He wants to recruit some of our Veterans to take over Dust Hold. We will offer our most proficient men. The current bandit activities around our own settlement will give us some opportunity to survey our armies and identify the most able fighters.

It is an honour for our troops to join the king's legendary Pioneers and aid in the conquest of Dust Hold. We have to make sure our men have the best equipment at their disposal. Gather our master smiths and provide the best materials. There is little time though - Dust Hold is re-arming, and marching orders have been given. No time to lose!

We need to ramp up our standing army now. We might have to extend our economy in places, so make sure we have a basic army in place, that our boys are fit for when the King arrives with his detailed requests, and we have provided any goods needed to improve the speed of our recruitment process.

This is Dust Hold's doing! They are instigating riots in our vicinity to sidetrack us and weaken our support for the King's troops! Quickly - we must suppress the upheaval before things get out of hand! And make sure you keep our troops in good shape, so they are ready on call when the King's orders reach us!

This is it. The King's messenger reached us this morning. The King is inspecting troops from all Islands, and only the best are being accepted to join his elite forces. His demands are quite specific and there is not much time, so no dawdling - we must merit the King's trust in us!

Our scouts report great advances on the frontlines. Victory seems within reach. This is heartening news. Let's not fail to provide support for our troops though - repair and recovery is crucial out there. In the meantime, we must also not let control of our borderland territories slip. We should constantly have scouts patrolling our borders to keep an eye on those bandit-infested regions.

This is outrageous! We have got word from the Royal Advisor that Dust Hold is receiving support deliveries, the origin of which was tracked back to our borderland islands! It seems bandits on the borders of our Settlement are supplying the very barbarian stronghold our troops are currently battling! We must act immediately, rally troops, build the fastest ships we can, and purge those islands!

War. Such a short word for something so powerful. It’s a good thing we have never been faced with a war - the battles we fight pale in comparison. But yes, war is raging at the outer rims of the kingdom, and, alongside his generals, our King Damien is doing his best to keep trouble from our gates. One of our kingdom's armies, the Ewanian Pioneers, is known to be composed of the most extraordinary soldiers this world has ever seen. It is the elite army of the King, and now they're at war at the rim, and a new darkness is rising. The King has ordered us all to establish an aid plan - we need to support them with all we've got, and as soon as possible!

The liberation of Randomar has taken grave toll on the King's troops. Right now every bit of help is welcome to get our men back on their feet again. They are short on food, and the barren rocks of Randomar provide hardly any shelter during the freezing nights. Let's provide what we can to help out our Pioneers!

Well, those barbarians have been intercepting our trade routes for decades, and were harassing our settlements, stealing whatever they could get their hands on. It's time to recover the stolen goods now! Send some Specialists to see what goods can be regained, and get rid of any spoils of war we might have in stock ourselves!

Hello there! Tee hee hee… Have you already heard about the big party coming up? The king himself has sent me to find out which server is the most suitable. So, help your server to become the best. How? Oh, it's easy. I will explain! Hee hee…

It is all about gathering the most balloons! The king loves balloons you know. Tee hee… You can see the number of balloons you have in your mayor's house under the new event tab. Feel free to take a look.
There are actions you can perform, which generate balloons with a certain percentage, for example using buffs. So go ahead - produce some buffs in your provision house and use them.

Another great possibility is trade! Whether you're buying or selling, each completed transaction earns them. One remark: this only works for trades via the trade office, not with friends. Hee hee hee… so, what are you waiting for? Trade!

When you have gathered some balloons, you have to donate them in order to make them count for your server. You can do this from your storage. Just click on the resource in your mayor house and choose to donate them. After that, you will see a window which looks similar to your trade window. Decide how much to donate, and confirm.

Remember the control panel beneath your avatar? It's where you can turn the sound off. Tee hee hee... Click on it and you'll see a new button - the Event Window button. Open the Event Window and you'll see all necessary information about the event, including a button allowing you to see how the servers are performing.

There have been some messages from another kingdom, saying that strange buildings are appearing on their lands. Tee hee hee… They are requesting help. It might be a side effect of our little party preparations. Could you take care of the buildings?
I am contacting you because strange looking buildings are appearing on far away islands. I heard you are a brave and adventurous person. Tee hee hee… I'm sure you can solve the problem.
Have you heard? Strange looking buildings everywhere. They are like a disease. Tee hee hee… I've said you'll take care of them. I'm sure you'll manage without any trouble.
Tee hee hee... These buildings really do look strange. Or is the landscape around them? Hmm… interesting question. Take a look for yourself. I'm eager to hear your opinion. Tee hee hee…

I wonder whether this is a side effect off our preparations, buildings appearing where they shouldn't, I mean. Either way, we need your help. I'm sure you'll know how to deal with the issue. Tee hee hee…
You look surprised. In this kingdom, everything looks a bit different. Tee hee hee... Just keep an eye out for buildings that look more like your own, and when you recognize one, simply click on it.
So, our glorious hero will save the day! Tee hee hee… just kidding. I'm hilarious, didn't you know? Anyway, have you already seen any buildings that don't seem to fit in? I can sense five of them.
My, that was a long journey. Tee hee hee… what a strange looking island. I wonder what the people who live here look like. Anyway, we're not here for entertainment! Tee hee hee… Just kidding.

So, feel free to look around and draw your own conclusions. I'm very eager to hear your opinion. By the way, I really like this retro style. It reminds me somehow of… oh, never mind. Just look around. Tee hee hee…

Here we are. I was told that there are five strange looking buildings around here. Find them and click on them. Nothing else out of the ordinary to report, except it looks a little like we've traveled back in time. Tee hee hee…

Hello there. Your achievements are really impressive. Maybe you can help me. I have a little prob… eh… concern. Nothing serious, really, but I can't do it by myself. You will be rewarded, of course. I'll make it worth your while. Tee hee hee…
While we take care of my tiny little issue, you should continue gathering and donating the balloons for our celebration party. At least when I choose your server. Tee hee hee…

Have you already heard about the strange buildings appearing on other islands? I too have received strange messages from one of them, but it seems the problem there is a bit bigger. You should prepare an army to be ready for any situation.

Well, the settler couldn't give me details, so I guess we'll have to check out the situation once we're there, but it seems it's something to do with buildings that look different from the others. Let's go and see what's happening.

Some of the settlers from the adventure we were on have asked whether they can join you. It seems you made a pretty big impression. They will come to your island a few at a time, so just lean back and relax. Tee hee hee…
Now that we have fresh settlers on the island, we can start training some new units. I've found another island exhibiting this strange phenomenon. We should be prepared for anything.

So, I was successful and found the map. We should get going as soon as possible. I'm not sure what the problem is there, but I assume it can't really wait. Also, the faster we're done, the faster we can continue relaxing. Tee hee hee…
Now that all the side effects of our party preparations have been dealt with, we can once again concentrate on gathering balloons. So, play and spend as much as possible. Make your server the winner!

Dear friend, thank you for once again arriving to help me out. The princess wants me to spend the night in a stable, with a giant bear! Luckily, I have a plan: the commoners tell me the bear likes music, so I shall simply entertain him with some songs on the violin, and hope he likes them so much he won’t want to eat me!
The catch is that I left my violin at home because I prefer to travel light. I tried to buy another, but the only one there used to be in the village has been stolen by bandits. Can you help me retrieve it?
The violin is located in bandit leader's hut. Their camp is too well guarded - it was impossible for me to sneak into it. Looks like we'll have to fight our way to the violin…

Now that I have the violin, I doubt it will be enough to keep the bear from eating me. I need something to trap the bear when things go ugly. A bench vise should do the trick. A blacksmith who lives in the forest should have one.
Look, there it is! I wonder where all those animals are coming from. They seem to be besieging the blacksmith. I’m sure he will gladly give you his bench vise if you manage to repulse them.

You should have seen that! The bear attacked me almost instantly, but as soon as I started to play he was mesmerized. He even started to dance and wanted me to teach him how to play the violin. You heard right - the bear can speak! I told him I'd need to cut his nails first, and used the vise to screw his paw tight. With the bear trapped, I got a good night’s sleep. In the morning, the princess was very impressed to see me, and she agreed to the marriage, so let’s go to the town and start the ceremony!
What did you say? The bear is no longer in the stable? Oh no! That other tailor must have freed him. I don’t want to be eaten on my wedding day. Could you search for the bear and take care of it?

Looks like I was too optimistic... My rival just attacked me and I barely escaped with my life. Could you do me a last favor and keep him occupied until the marriage is done? It looks like he's the head of the local bandits, so you'll have to fight through his goons to get to him.
Alright, you see that hut on the coast? That's his hideout. Just get in there and rough him up a bit. That should give us time to finish the wedding ceremony.

OK, here we are. It does look a bit strange here. The village with the settlers who can provide us with information is behind this mountain chain… oh, and there's a bandit horde there too. We should begin with them. Tee hee hee…
Seems like the passage is blocked somehow. Gather some of your men and pull the big rocks aside. It basically means you have to click on them. Tee hee hee…

Can you see the village? I can't see it very well either. We should get nearer, or maybe we should make our way through the bandit camps and check with the inhabitants there?! Even though we probably could reach the village without fighting, saving the villagers from the bandits will gain their trust.
We should ask around this little town. It seems some of the buildings look kind of strange here, don't you think? I'm eager to hear the story behind all this. Tee hee hee…
Hmm.. The witch is at the end of this canyon. It seems one of those bandit camps is blocking the way, so we'll have to fight. It wouldn't be any fun otherwise…
The shaman has his camp deep in these woods. I assume he will have several traps and units set up to prevent visitors from visiting. Tee hee hee… Geddit? Visitors from visiting. Tee hee hee…
Hmm… reminds me a bit of the last island we were on. However, do you see the dead trees? They are blocking the way through the forest. Remove them by clicking on them.

Just as I expected - bandits everywhere. It seems we are not going to be able to get around them, so let's clear a way through again. However, clicking will not be enough to drive them back. Tee hee hee…
I would suggest asking the settlers living here. Select the different buildings and ask around. I'm sure we'll get enough information from them.

The settlers say we need a special item to unlock the seal of the old ruins that are causing this. This means we need to reach the swamp and defeat the croaker, but there are fences and walls blocking the swamp. Let your units tear them down and defeat the toad.
If I've understood correctly, we have to defeat these cult guys in the camps near the ruins to unleash some magic energy, and that will tear down the ruins. So, let's go. Tee hee hee…

You arrive at the forest and read the little tailor’s instructions carefully: “The hermit who gave me shelter always keeps his hut well lit at night to scare off the wild animals. Just wait for night to fall and you should see the light which will guide you to me.”
And indeed, you do see a bright light at the horizon. It’s not far from here, but the terrifying howls of a nearby wolf pack worry you…

You decide to wait the rest of the night before leaving, but in the morning you are aroused by the violent sounds of screaming and roaring animals.
You hurry out of the hut, and on the other side of the nearby river you see a great black bull and a majestic stag fighting each other.
For a long time, it is uncertain which of the two is going to be victorious, but then the bull thrusts his horns into the stag’s body. Though wounded, the stag continues to fight, but it is obvious he won't be able to hold on much longer.
Suddenly the tailor runs off, with the words: “Don’t just stand there - we have to help the stag!”

Suddenly the stag rushes towards the tailor, entangles him on his antlers and runs away.
You decide to follow them. Careful though - all the wild animals the stag rushes past in his hurry are now upset, and they will attack you on sight…
You follow the tracks to a barren mountainous area. In the distance you can see a soaring tower, and your intuition tells you that you will find the little tailor there.

The little Tailor tells you what happened: “Alright, the stag didn't mean to harm me when he caught me on his antlers. He took me to this tower where I found this maiden. She had been imprisoned in a glass coffin by a dark magician, because she did not return his affection.
He also imprisoned her entire castle, together with her entire court, by diminishing it in size. And the stag is in reality her brother! And the bull he was fighting with was the dark magician transformed by dark magic!
We need to reach the Dark Magician’s castle and defeat him so we can free the maiden's shire and break the curse affecting her brother!”
"Alright, now only a few cultists stand between us and the magician. Let’s not waste any time - who knows what dark magic he is conjuring right now…"
Every journey begins with a first step, and the plan to educate this young fellow properly might turn out be a truly epic journey!
Basic training will help our friend to commit and somewhat predetermine his specialisation later on, so be careful what you teach in this phase!
Our friend has ascended to the higher reaches of geology, if one can say that about a mole like him. Now we carefully have to assess his disposition and the potential uses.

It is about time to introduce our man to the greatest teachings of geology, one might say the secrets of the earth. Choose with great care - the abilities at stake are what make a truly exceptional Geologist.

Did you notice that the Geologists often seem to settle for quite mediocre results? There's got to be more to get from these deposits! I say we give the first Manuscript to a Geologist and broaden his horizons a bit!
I'm not even sure he can actually read. He can't read a map, that much is sure! Just how can someone take so much time for every journey?
I propose we go on and teach this restless fellow the basics of navigation and travel planning first. After that, we should be able to tell what really he has a knack for.
It can't hurt to send a few of our more advanced books his way. I was thinking material sciences or a bit of history, so he can actually tell what he is bringing us.
Well, he has proven that he knows his metier, much to my astonishement, I have to admit, so it would be a good idea to provide him with our finest works now, and truly make him a specialist.

These explorers, eh? Here today, gone tomorrow! All these treasure searches and expeditions! A little groundedness wouldn't hurt, would it? Some commitment and dedication. Give them an area of expertise to specialise in - make them stand for something in life!
Bandits have occupied the village and will hinder us greatly in our search. I guess we must drive them away first, otherwise we'll need much more time to find the sons.
My first son always wanted to become a joiner. I bet we'll find him chopping wood near the forest in the west.

I have spoken with the miller in the village and he has told me that my second son is his apprentice. He has send him to find his donkey that drops gold from its mouth when you say ‘Bricklebrit!’ According to the miller he headed to the mountains, but has not returned yet. Let's go find him!
The third son is always ready for a good fight to protect others and fight evil. Maybe he is just about to beat up some bandits in the east?

The little tailor greets his son and immediately asks for forgiveness, but the son is still angry that the little tailor preferred to believe a goat more than him. Maybe he will change his mind when we help him to chop down the red tree in the north-west, but to get there we first need to fight our way through the forest and its dangerous beasts.

His eyes wide open, the son starts to speak: “Father! How glad I am to see you. The miller has given me the task of finding his gold-producing donkey. I followed its tracks to this old abandoned mine and discovered it had been stolen by a giant! I saw him walking to another old mine and just as I started following him, the inhabitants of the mine returned and I was forced to hide. Who knows what woudl have happened to me if you hadn't come and saveed me, father…
May I ask you to help me to get the gold-producing donkey back from the giant so I can finish my apprenticeship?”

You have freed the third son from his chains, but there is no time to talk. The Bandits from the other side of the river have seen your attack and are preparing to retaliate. To protect the town, you must fight your way to their leader and defeat him.

There it is, the red tree! Some say its wood has magical properties. We will soon find out, because my master has asked me to acquire it so I can create my masterwork: a magical table which can create food whenever we wish!
However, it seems the beasts of this forest don't want us to get to the tree. Once again we need to fight our way through!

With the bandits regrouping the little tailor’s son found some time to speak: “Though I have not forgotten how you sent me away, I appreciate your help here, father. However, the toughest part is just about to start. If you assist me in defeating their leader you will not only be helping the innocent townsfolk, you'll also help me finish my apprenticeship. That’s because their leader wields a magical cudgel-in-a-bag he stole from my master. And of course, my master wants it back!
What, you don’t know what a cudgel-in-a-bag is?
It’s quite simple: If you say ‘Out of the bag, Cudgel!’ it will leap out of the bag and attack the bad guys. And when you are done you say: ‘Into the bag Cudgel!’
Really convenient if you ask me.”

Thank you for assisting me once again, old friend! A greedy inn-keeper has tricked my two youngest sons and stolen our wishing table and the gold-producing donkey. I fear he may try to get the cudgel-in-a-bag too. Will you join me looking after my oldest son? Once I’m sure he's well, we can start making a plan for getting our stuff back.
Oh no - the inn-keeper has hired an assassin! How cruel. This guy will soon see what an angry father is capable of, but for now we need to stop the assassin!

I’m so relieved my sons are safe now, but the thugs managed to steal the cudgel before we arrived. We need to get it back - I want use it on that mean inn-keeper. Let’s follow them to the village. Maybe we can overtake them.
We are very close to him. Soon he will get to know the little cudgel he wanted to steal! Let’s move on to the tavern.

Oh how I do love this cudgel, but sadly he managed to escape, and our stuff is not even here. I'm guessing he's hidden it in his overly luxurious mansion in the north-east. Let’s visit him there and demand he return what is ours.
By the looks of the grim-looking welcoming party around his mansion, I'm guessing he won't give up our stuff without a fight.
