My lord, I'm sorry to bother you with my problems again. After you crush my enemy, I'll need help to rebuild the cities of my empi-, er, I mean islands. For that I will need the best resources we can find, and I was hoping it might be possible for you to prepare some exotic wood for me?

I truly appreciate the exotic wood you gave me my lord. But as you know, the wood has to be worked in order to be useful. I'm planning on building several ships to aid in transporting resources around the islands. Can you have your settlers produce some exotic wood planks please?
It seems that while we were focusing on restocking our wood supplies, we ran out of other resources, such as granite. We should let the miners know!

People that perform great deeds should be immortalized. And what better way to preserve someone's visage than by building a statue! My islands had many great men and my cities were filled with the most unique statues you have ever seen! But to construct more, I will need granite. Build a granite mason.

My lord, it seems that we might be in the need of more granite. While this island may not be rich in resources, granite can be found almost anywhere a solid patch lays. Send out your scouts to find granite deposits.
All a good mason needs is a good pickaxe to be ready for work! Now that we know where the granite is, we can start producing it. The more the better, that's what I say! Produce granite.
Granite is indeed a very strong ore! But you know what's even better? That's right - titanium! Our next task is a given!

Titanium is another ore that's hard to find and mine. My people at Wall Maria were never able to manage it, thus they left me with no option but to trade for it. It didn't come cheap, though... even the kings charge a lot for a pile. Your miners build much stronger mines than mine, so why not have them build a titanium mine and get us prepared!

Have your scouts ever attempted to find titanium ore? It's tricky, isn't it? But I know a secret! You see, there's this curious little bird breed called an "eren". These birds usually nest near titanium ore deposits, as they're partial to its smell. I smelled the ore once, but to be honest, it's foul! Why not pass this information on to your scouts and have them look for titanium ore deposits.

Because titanium is hard to work with, people started breaking it apart in huge chunks. When the night fell, the lonely chunks looked like giants ready to eat the miners. Ha ha! Imagine that. We should call upon your miners to produce some titanium ore.
According to one of your alchemists, saltpetre is the main ingredient in gunpowder! Now, as you know, gunpowder can be the difference maker in any battle - so let's get as much saltpetre as possible!

My lord, would you happen to know how to mine saltpetre? You do? Marvelous! This is the perfect chance for us to plan for the time when arrows will not suffice to fight back against our enemies. We need gunpowder, but for that we need saltpetre! Build a saltpetre mine!

It's not an easy task to look for a saltpetre deposit! One wrong hit with the pickaxe and you can send yourself flying in an explosion! I'd send only the most experienced scouts to find them, just to be on the safe side! Choose your scouts and send them out to find the saltpetre deposits.

Have you ever heard of a man called "Wild Peter"? He was a great gunslinger! Every time you saw him, he was carrying several guns, and he could fire them all off in less than five seconds flat! I saved his life once, and he offered to share his secrets with me. He taught me how to make proper gunpowder. Produce some saltpetre, and I might share my knowledge!

I joined your people last night at the camp fire. We shared stories about our lives, and somehow we ended up talking about food. It was then that one of your soldiers mentioned you have an amazing cook. I think it would be a good idea to send a small gift to your provision houses. Some barazek maybe?

My lord, have you never heard of barazek? It's only one of the most delicious cookies ever created!! While I don't know the exact recipe, I'm sure if you went on an adventure to the new lands you'd find some! Embark on a new adventure!
My lord, I know the barazek looks delicious, but you must put your workers first! Imagine how happy they'd be when they saw our gift! Please, use the barazek on your provision houses.

Curses! These bandits are causing trouble around our borders! Last night some of them snuck inside the settlement and stole several apple pies and sweets! Scoundrels! Dogs! I will not tolerate this! My lord, please, send your general and clear out the bandit camps in the area!

Remember the prisoner we rescued? It turns out his name is Captain Mapparan! He's a man of... curious habits. He's traveled the world far and wide, and knows every single place there is. But that was many years ago, and now his age has caught up with him and he's no longer able to travel. So, he's decided to build himself the world's biggest library. Of course, if you want a library, you'll need plenty of books, scrolls and relics to fill it - and it's with this he'd like our help. He promises great treasures in return! Let's start by taking care of the military part.

My world is filled with tales about lost treasures, mystical places and curious people. One of them is a boy I know called Ali Baba. The boy has this peculiar ability to find maps that usually lead to treasures. I told one of your explorers to go look for Ali Baba, perhaps he can spare a coin for the boy to share his knowledge? Send your explorer on an epic treasure search.

Captain Mapparan speaks of a pirate who stole some of his maps. These maps contain directions to islands of an unknown distance, holding secrets that anyone would love to explore. It seems to me that this Captain is an adventurous one? Good - let us prepare our platinum smelters and complete all that the Captain requests from us!

I have here a report from your storehouse master. He tells me that the production of exotic wood is currently not optimal, as the settlers in charge have found a small lamp that allegedly makes their wishes come true. I'm sure they're really just looking for an excuse to go slacking off. Talk with your storehouse master and have him optimize your exotic wood production!

Come closer my lord, and listen to this. The Captain wants his home to not only resemble a ship, but to actually be a ship! I was under the impression he was joking, but no - he actually wants us to build him a ship for a home! And not a small one, I might add! My lord, we'll need a lot of wood for this - and the means to carry the heavy logs. See to it!

My lord? I was visiting the granite mines the other day, and something caught my eye - they have no proper equipment! I talked to the artisans around the settlement, and ordered them to use the proper clothing and tools. But this small distraction has also caused a small delay, so it would be wise if you could optimize our granite production.

The blueprints suggest that Captain Mapparan wants the ship's inner floors to be laden with granite! Now, I can understand the good captain wanting some elegance, but granite is not easy to find... Here's hoping the rewards are worth it, considering all he's asking of us. Let's tend to the Granite.

I'm afraid I bring bad news! Last night, while the moon was shining bright, there was a small accident at one of the saltpetre deposits. One of the miners decided to cook a duck, but forgot to put out the fire! The fire burned its way towards the hut, but thankfully they were able to stop it in time. However, this small incident has caused some delay so it would be a good idea to quickly optimize our saltpetre production.

Cannons? Now he wants his home... ship... whatever it is to have cannons!? He claims that he just knows that pirates will try to take over his ship, and thus he needs protection! Very well! The good news is that he actually has the cannons and the cannon balls, but he's lacking gunpowder. On to the saltpetre mines we go!

Something's not right! Since your men found that lamp, we've been flooded with problems. Several chunks of titanium were left unattended, and one of them fell on the next, creating a chain reaction! Eventually the last chunk crashed into one of the outhouses, but luckily nobody was inside. The miners spent most of the day cleaning up the mess. You should help them optimize their titanium production.

As I mentioned before, a library needs books! When Captain Mapparan brings his books to his ship, he'll need to have some proper fittings for them. Now, I know that proper fittings require titanium, as it is the strongest ore out there... But I've also heard that titanium can protect the reader from evil curses! Seeing as this could be a problem, I say that we make the captain some good book fittings from titanium.
The day has come! We have all the resources we need to build Captain Mapparan's ship!

The blueprints are ready, the resources are ready and the men are eager to start. Captain Mapparan will arrive soon, along with his company of men to supervise the construction. My lord, order your settlers to build Captain Mapparan's ship!

Ah, how about paying a visit to Captain Mapparan? I'm sure he has several tasks for us, and I've heard that the rewards he's giving out are also noteworthy! Let's complete some of the tasks he's offering!

My lord. As you may have heard, my islands are filled with a thousand (and one) stories. Some of us spend their whole lives travelling along the sand dunes telling stories to those who are willing to hear them. One of these storytellers, a young woman, has arrived at one of the platinum deposits. Unfortunately, she's spent so long telling stories that the men forgot their tasks. Optimize the platinum production.

My lord! Captain Mapparan approached me looking for a considerable loan. He claims he needs to pay several mercenaries to do the dirty work for him. However, I'm not sure your current treasury would allow you to give him the loan… What? You want to know how much he asked for? No my lord, I cannot say, I fear you might faint! I have been keeping an eye on the market and it seems that the price of platinum ore is fluctuating. How about you buy some, and then sell it on for profit?
My lord, where I come from I was kind of a lord as well. Now, I'm not being impolite here, no, I just... I just think that maybe the time has come for us to move to a… bigger house?

I saw a picture of a manor! I think a building like that would be much more appropriate for a lord! I've asked around the settlement, but the only man who can build a manor is old Pa Custeau! Though he's a very old man, his blueprints are certainly impressive! What are you waiting for? Let's build a manor!

We may have a manor now, but we shouldn't forget about our settlers! They are also on foreign land, and scared of the unknown! I think we should build new houses for them! Raise your population by building more houses.

Ugh! One of the merchants coming from the east was attacked by bandits! It seems that these rats will not stop interfering in our dealings! The merchant was kind enough to share the location of the bandit camp. I say we wake up your general and have him take care of this problem. Defeat the bandit camps!

My lord, I have good news! Captain Mapparan wants to thank you for all the help! He's called upon his friends from far off lands to come together for the feast of the century! I heard that my good friend, King Schahri will be attending as well! We need to prepare our best foods and drinks. Send the captain some meat, fish, bread and of course, a lot of brew!
Captain Mapparan's presence on our island is very important, and we should do everything in our power to keep him here! I think we need to prove to him how adventurous we are!

It's all about treasure. Everything is all about treasure. Captain Mapparan still keeps us up every night with his amazing stories! He keeps claiming that nobody knows as much about this world as he does! I want to prove him wrong! My lord, we should complete more treasure hunts, and learn all that we can!
We have an army, and we have a strong, productive settlement! All we need is now to take back the archipelago that belongs to me! Let us prepare the final steps!
My lord! May I have your undivided attention? Your people are ready to take back the islands. Prepare the resources for your men and ready your generals! It is time to clear out all the sectors!

My lord, it is time for me to reveal my true identity! I am not a lord! In truth, I am a Sultan! In disguise! But... do you think you could keep it to yourself? Please, don't tell a soul! I love travelling the world in disguise. No man has ever been so kind and helpful to me as you were, my good lord. I just have one last request, and then I shall leave you be! Conquer all the sectors and reclaim them!

My lord! I have learned that there are many magical creatures out there. Would you be so kind as to take me on an adventure, so that I can see these creatures with my own eyes? Please, play a fairytale adventure.
Armies are lead by captains and generals, but who knows what names they have in other lands? Your army needs a major general, so it would be best to send for one!
I see your men at the sawmill were impressed by the quality of the mahogany wood. Do not let them down - have them produce more mahogany planks!
I know I keep saying it, but mahogany is very rare! Therefore, I would advise you to engage in more adventures and gather more mahogany wood!
Now that we have plenty of exotic wood, you should order your settlers to prepare it! Have them make some exotic wood planks!

You know, my family had a very costly habit: they liked to coat everything in gold. I know it sounds silly, but… when I was a child, I had a woolen blanket that was coloured gold. It reminds me of my dear mother. Can you produce some more wool please?
Some of the soldiers are worried we might not have enough cloth! I think we should put their minds at rest, and produce more cloth, just to be on the safe side.
A horseman pointed out that it's very important to have saddles of all shapes and sizes. They have small horses and big horses, after all… I think we should produce more saddle cloth!
I heard there's a land far away, where there's a man who can create the most unique garments in the whole empire. I would like to ask you to send me, along with your general, on the tailor adventure!

My lord! Have you ever heard of the land of endless deserts? There are many mysteries between the dunes, and many treasures to be found! I urge you to send your generals into the adventure of the 1001 nights!
We now have a map that shows us where the adventure is! Ready your general, and send him out to gather the precious resources!

These adventures are amazing! I think we should send our troops on regular adventures so they can train for battle against our enemies. But first things first: send out one of your explorers to find a fairytale epic adventure!
I have bad news! There's been a fire in one of the exotic woods nearby. The woodcutter's requested our help! Refill the affected exotic wood deposits!

Our army needs to use real weapons for their training, and with all the adventures we've been going on, there's a small chance that the weapons may be unusable once the troops have returned. To avoid any awkward situations, I would suggest we make an extra order of weapons!
The land of the fairies seems to be a perfect place to train our troops, and collect rare resources! Order your general to engage in more fairytale adventures!

I believe I've told you about my trades with the most honoured King Schahri already! Every year I send him a gift to show him my gratitude. But this year I have nothing! I beg you, my lord, help me! I have to send him three items! One of them is a silver hunter gun. I have the gun recovered, but I will need quality gunpowder! Refill a saltpetre deposit and then upgrade your saltpetre mines so we get the best quality!

My friend, King Schahri is a man of a thousand tastes. He loves good food more than anything! I have met your Aunt Irma, and her cooking is out of this world! I would like to ask you to have her produce some food for me, as a gift - the famous Aunt Irma's Baskets!

The third gift I want to send to King Schahri is a bit complicated. It's not a something - it's a somebody. I usually send him some of my best fighters to serve at the king's court as bodyguards! Could my lord spare some of his knights? Train them so one day we can send them to the king!

I had a word with your alchemist, and he shared his concerns with me. Apparently, he thinks that the platinum we're mining is not of the best quality. He says he's heard that there's a deposit of perfect quality platinum out there. I think you should send out one of your explorers on an epic treasure search so he can look for that special platinum ore.

My lord must have noticed that the winds on these islands are much stronger than they should be. These winds may actually cause some damage to the buildings. I advise you to produce some more exotic wood that can be used for the eventual repairs.

Heavy wagons and horseshoes cause extensive damage to the roads we're using. There are already several holes already on the main roads that need filling! You should have your men produce more granite!

Our miners use dynamite and all other kinds of explosives to dig deeper into their mines. Just to be sure, have your men produce some saltpetre, so if there's need for more gunpowder, your alchemists can make it quickly. Produce saltpetre!
Eh? The latest report from the storehouse claims we're low on titanium! But this cannot be! Have your settlers produce more titanium!
I have spoken with the captain from the ship. He's challenged us to complete a certain number of tasks! I love a challenge! Accept and complete tasks.
We have a new master at the storehouse. While he was doing his first inspection, he found that our platinum supplies were running low. I think it's time to produce more platinum ore.
Your generals have been in many battles, but I heard that there is one more adventure that's worth trying. Return to the deserts and complete the final "1001 Nights" Adventure.

My lord, my eyes have seen wonderful places and people. I've travelled the world, seen the snowy fields of the north and the mountains to the east. I've seen the jungles of the west and the deserts of the south. In each of these countries, each of their capitals had a so called "royal neighbourhood". If you want King Schahri to consider visiting us, we should build a royal neighbourhood too. Have your settlers build manors, and make sure they're upgraded accordingly.

King Schahri is here! I will personally make sure his needs are tended to! After all, I know how to treat royalty! The king's first wish is to visit the most expensive looking place we have! I think a gold mine fits the bill! Select a gold mine for the king to visit, but make sure it's upgraded!

My lord! Before agreeing to be our friend and ally, the king would like to see how generous you are! I think the best way is to prepare some gifts for your friends! Let the king see how generous you are, prepare some buffs and help out your friends.

Ali Baba tells a tale of an oasis of legend somewhere on this island, and he's sure the thief leaders will be near it. You spot several thief caravans in the distance, and you decide to follow them through the huge desert.
You see some of the fleeing thieves head towards an ancient ruin in the distance. You deduce they are headed to where their main base is and decide to give chase to them.

You intercept one of the thief messengers, who was about to send a warning to the main base about your arrival. Ali Baba feels relieved to confirm his suspicions. You decide it's time to push forward to the thieves' main camp.

Your troops arrive on the island, but Ali Baba is nowhere to be found. He specifically asked you to wait for his arrival, as he could be of great help here. While you wait for his arrival, you decide to survey the surroundings for thief camps.

Ali Baba has arrived on the island. He praises your proactiveness, and mentions that the information will be a big help for his plan. He knows of a secret passage that leads directly to the core of the stronghold, but it's blocked by a huge boulder. He asks for your help to remove it.

With the secret passage revealed, Ali Baba goes in without a second thought and beckons you to follow him. The cave is long and treacherous, but he assures you it's a lot safer than the alternative. You decide to follow him through the cave.
You and your troops are relieved to finally see the sunlight again. Ali Baba smiles and points to where the main stronghold camp is. You prepare for the final attack on the stronghold core.

Upon arriving on the island, you're greeted by a huge mountain, which is virtually impossible to climb. Ali Baba manages to spot a few bandit camps on the higher levels, which means that there must be some way up - and you're not the only ones after the treasure.

You quickly realize that the mountain's labyrinth-like nature is going to make the climb difficult to say the least. On your way up, you spot a horrific plant monster guarding one of the pathways. You decide to take action against it.

Arriving at the island, you encounter the remains of an ancient civilization that lived here years, if not centuries ago. You see some raider camps around who don't look very pleased to see you. Given their clearly hostile intentions, you decide to take up arms against them.

With the plant monster gone, the goal is finally at hand. You spot the ancient library in the distance, but it's too late. The bandits are already looting the place. You plan your final offensive with the intention of stopping them before they can find the treasure.

The first camps seem to have been only a diversion to keep you busy while tomb raiders violently loot the ancient's tombs. Irritated by the lack of respect to such an ancient culture, you decide to put an end to it.

You receive some good news from Ali Baba. The raiders have not managed to access the main temple due to its ancient defence system. You understand why this is good news, but you're concerned about how exactly you're going to get through the defence system yourself!

Sinbad warmly greets you, and you share your information. He mentions that there is a city nearby where you may be able to get some more information about your goals. Some raiders stand between you and the city and demand you surrender. It's time to show them what you're made of.

Sinbad returns after a quick exploration of the area, and informs you that the city has been overrun with frenzied apes. Putting your main objective aside, you decide to drive the apes away from the city and back into their habitat.

Aladdin tells you that he has an informant that knows where the oil lamp could be, and that he may also know where Scheherezade is being held captive. In between you and the informant, though, there are many bandits that are not willing to let you through, so you ready your weapons to push through by force.
The shady informant flees to the east, trying to escape from you. You know he's hiding something, and he's too valuable to let him get away, so you quickly give chase.
The informant has been cornered, yet he still refuses to talk to you. You will need to be more "persuasive" and get the information you need by force if necessary.

You meet Sinbad, an experienced sailor, upon your arrival. He tells you that he has heard rumours among other sailors of a great treasure hidden on this island. In order for them to share more information, however, you'll have to win them over by doing what they like doing the most - brawling.
You decide to make your way to the cave the sailors mentioned. You seem to not be the only one after the treasure, though, as there are some bandits heading over there too.

You and Aladdin arrive at the island where the informant mentioned Scheherezade was being held. It surprises you how barren everything looks, to the point where you question the information received. You quickly clear your suspicion, however, as you see that bandit camps have been set up to protect their base. They were expecting you.

While Aladdin celebrates having finally found the oil lamp, you find a small crumbled piece of paper on the ground. It reads: "They are taking us to the Oasis in the east. Please help us! There isn't much time! - Scheherezade". What could she possibly mean by "us"?

Right before you finish dismantling the camp, you see a horse sprinting away towards the old palace carrying a bandit and two women. You're certain that Scheherezade is one of them, and quickly give chase.
Wait, what? Has that island always been there? I've just noticed it! No matter, we can always use the extra space. We need a Sector Deed to be able to claim the land.
These islands look nice and cozy, but it's better if we don't get our guard down. Who knows what might be waiting under that thick fog?
If we're going to start a new settlement on these islands, it's best if we stockpile as many construction materials as possible, just in case. How are the exotic wood and granite reserves looking?

My Lord, I know it's been a long time since you explored a sector, but it's best we don't forget that it took a lot of fighting to claim our initial island! If we are to claim new islands, it's best we prepare ourselves for anything.
With the weapons ready, we're only missing manpower now. We need to make sure we have enough room to hold a big army and our workers. You know what they say: "better safe than sorry".

It works! The pure water's weakened him! Just imagine what a few more canisters would do!
Quick - let's produce enough pure water to bring him down!
- Defeat the golem by using enough pure water.

I'm afraid another golem has gone astray on your island. I've already gathered everything I need from him, but I'd expect your settlers would be grateful if you could defeat this one too.
- Defeat the golem by using enough purified water on it.

I'm afraid another golem has gone astray on your island. I've already gathered everything I need from him, but I'd expect your settlers would be grateful if you could defeat this one too.
- Defeat the golem by using enough purified water on it.

I'm afraid another golem has gone astray on your island. I've already gathered everything I need from him, but I'd expect your settlers would be grateful if you could defeat this one too.
- Defeat the golem by using enough purified water on it.

Wow, yet another type of golem!! This one's even bigger - and it's on fire! Looks like the enriched water isn't working now either. In fact, it almost looks like this thing's protected by a curse of some kind.
For this, I think we'll need to call in the big guns - it's time to break out the holy water, to douse this golem's inner fire!
Produce enough holy water to bring the ancient golem down.
- Defeat the ancient golem by using enough holy water.

I'm afraid another golem has gone astray on your island. I've already gathered everything I need from him, but I'd expect your settlers would be grateful if you could defeat this one too.
- Defeat the ancient golem by using enough holy water on it

I'm afraid another golem has gone astray on your island. I've already gathered everything I need from him, but I'd expect your settlers would be grateful if you could defeat this one too.
- Defeat the ancient golem by using enough holy water on it

I'm afraid another golem has gone astray on your island. I've already gathered everything I need from him, but I'd expect your settlers would be grateful if you could defeat this one too.
- Defeat the ancient golem by using enough holy water on it

I'm afraid another golem has gone astray on your island. I've already gathered everything I need from him, but I'd expect your settlers would be grateful if you could defeat this one too.
- Defeat the ancient golem by using enough holy water on it

What?! That golem looks somehow... different? And bigger!? Looks like the purified water we were using is no longer effective. But what else can we try?
Ah - our settlers do have another technique for making enriched water! Perhaps that could put out the golem's inner fire!
Come on - let's make some enriched water, and bring the greater golem down.
- Defeat the greater golem by using enough enriched water.

I'm afraid another golem has gone astray on your island. I've already gathered everything I need from him, but I'd expect your settlers would be grateful if you could defeat this one too.
- Defeat the ancient golem by using enough enriched water on it

I'm afraid another golem has gone astray on your island. I've already gathered everything I need from him, but I'd expect your settlers would be grateful if you could defeat this one too.
- Defeat the greater golem by using enough enriched water on it

I'm afraid another golem has gone astray on your island. I've already gathered everything I need from him, but I'd expect your settlers would be grateful if you could defeat this one too.
- Defeat the greater golem by using enough enriched water on it

I'm afraid another golem has gone astray on your island. I've already gathered everything I need from him, but I'd expect your settlers would be grateful if you could defeat this one too.
- Defeat the greater golem by using enough enriched water on it

I'm afraid another golem has gone astray on your island. I've already gathered everything I need from him, but I'd expect your settlers would be grateful if you could defeat this one too.
- Defeat the golem by using enough purified water on it.

Before we can overcome the golem, we have to get you to a certain level. There's no way you'll be able to take him on as you are! Keep on leveling as you were, and I'll come back to you when you're ready.

Listen closely my friend, because I have a cunning plan. Things aren't looking great as they stand. Our weapons cannot harm its stony-skin. Even our cannons are shrugged off like mosquito-bites. But there is another way to defeat him.
What animates this golem is its inner fire. If we could extinguish it, it should freeze and turn into stone. We tried regular water, but it had no effect. Perhaps now we should take the concentrated approach, and try purified water instead!
It's worth a try. Tell your settlers to drop what they're doing, and start producing purified water as soon as they can!
Alright, now let’s test those canisters of purified water! Simply click on the golem and a new window will appear. You can use your purified water there.

Have we met before? Your face looks... familiar. But where are my manners! My name is Eliot and you look like you're confused about what's happening on your island. Don't worry - I'll talk you through everything you need to know. So, where shall we begin?!

First of all, you should try to get as many pumpkins as you can! Why? Because you can buy cool stuff with them, of course! Even buildings! One way of getting them is through buying pumpkin cemeteries. You find them at the merchant. There are different kinds, sizes and speeds available, so why not take a look and buy some?

Of course, you can also collect pumpkins in other ways. Besides pumpkin cemeteries, you can earn them as rewards for quests, by taking part in several adventures, as collectibles in your home zone, by buying them at the merchant, or as a reward for defeating a golem! Trading with other players is also possible too! So happy collecting!

My lord, I cannot understate how important it is for you to fully understand the options menu. This time I would like to tell you about the advanced options. These ones are particularly valuable when it comes to increasing your performance. Why not give them a look?
Now that we can finally extract granite directly from the source, we should be able to amass plenty of it in a short space of time! Let’s keep going. We can never have enough granite in our storage!

Along with having our production chains stable and working, it's equally important to boost their productivity whenever possible. By now, you know all about how important buffs are, so let’s create some extra buffs for us and our allies!
Despite being able to mine new, rare minerals, we mustn’t forget about essential materials like marble! Make sure to keep your geologists busy so they can find as many deposits as possible!

Platinum is scarce, and we'll need to get as much as we can to be able to complete the hardest adventures. Remember that another way of obtaining platinum is to send your explorers on prolonged treasure searches. Please get them to find some platinum ore for us!
Remember that claiming colonies is another great way to get an extra boost in certain resources, including the precious granite! Prepare your expedition army and claim a colony for our kingdom!

I may be repeating myself here, but with all the new discoveries we've been making, and new buildings we've designed, granite has become vital to our economy. You can never have enough in your storage! Do you know what one of the best ways to obtain it is? Well, from adventures of course!

There are some places the elite army simply cannot go - and that’s why it’s always important to keep a decent number of units in our conventional army too. Let’s train some recruits, soldiers and horsemen. They will prove useful to our kingdom soon enough.
Our allies help keep our kingdom strong - and I’m sure they'd say the same about us too! Why not show them a bit of appreciation by buffing some of their workyards?

There's always a high demand for platinum ore - but my sixth sense tells me that this may be the perfect time to place some of ours on the market and cut a good profit. I’m sure someone will be interested if we price it right!
It’s always a pleasure to see you! I’m glad you're keeping a watchful eye on your land, always ensuring everyone's doing their best at work. Would you come in for at least three days this week?

Buffs have become a critical part of our economy nowadays, but let’s not forget that if it’s one of our allies who comes and buffs one of our buildings, the effect will last for much longer than if we used it ourselves. Please ask our allies to buff 5 of our buildings!

I'm sure you're already aware of the benefits of having marksmen and armoured marksmen in our elite army, so I guess it won’t come as a surprise that I have a request for extra arquebuses and additional battle horses, right?

Gold is easily our most desired resource right now, but gold itself is not what we seek - instead, we want what we can manufacture with it. Make sure our production chains for gold and coins are in optimal shape. Don’t forget to use buffs!
We should always maintain a steady income of platinum ore and platinum, both for our needs and theirs. Let’s make sure we have a proper production chain for platinum.

If there's huge loot to be found, you can be sure we'll find it in fairytale adventures. We should complete at least one to make the most of both our conventional and our elite armies! Will we help out the little tailor? Or perhaps live an “Arabian nights” adventure? I’m so excited!
Our expedition marshals are hunkering for a bigger challenge. Let’s make this a bit harder for them. Claim control of at least two colonies this week. Make sure you have enough iron in your storage!

Even though mahogany wood has proven to be very useful - and rare - we mustn’t forget about the wide variety of uses that exotic wood still has. I’m a bit impatient when it comes to gathering it though, so let’s get a good quantity of exotic wood through adventure loot.

That last adventure we had with our conventional army has left it a little… maimed. We should replenish our ranks with top soldiers armed with the finest equipment. Particularly elite soldiers, cannoneers and crossbowmen.

Some of our production chains could use a little boost, and unfortunately, our buffs no longer cut it. We need more power. Something that lasts longer. We need our friends to buff our buildings for us!

We need to have more coins in our storage, whether we're saving to upgrade buildings or re-selling them for profit. Speaking of profits, maybe we could try selling some of our spare platinum swords, so we can buy something we really need right now?

The market may be the best place to get what you need - but you’re not the only one looking for some essential supplies. Try selling some rare materials at the market. But don’t do it for free! Make sure you get a nice deal in return!

Personally, I love scenario adventures. One of my particular favorites is “Storm Recovery” - I love the message of hope we leave to the inhabitants of the islands we help. I feel so alive every time we complete it! Do you think we could complete one this week?

You may think it’s pointless using valuable grout on depletable buildings like mines, but the benefits can be huge. Get some mines to level 6, and combine with refillers and buffs to see what I’m talking about!

This is terrible! I just received a letter from one of my cousins. He and his army are pinned down in the desert by bandits! He has sent an urgent request for elite weapons and horses. Please, I beg of you! Help my cousin!

Aunt Irma mentioned the other day that she hasn’t had time to breathe recently, she's been so busy making gift baskets for people she doesn’t even know! With this in mind, she's requested some holiday to recoup. This is unprecedented, but I think she may be right. How about we boost our production with potions of endless energy instead? If you’re missing some collectibles, I’m sure your friends can help, or you can find some in the market.

These “Arabian nights” adventures have proven to be quite a challenge, but their loot is most definitely valuable. In fact, there are very few generals out there that have completed the full raid. Do you think your generals will manage to be amongst them? Send them to complete an “Arabian Nights” adventure and let’s find out!

The only thing harder than taking on an expedition? Taking on several at the same time! You guessed it: I’m officially challenging your marshals to claim and maintain 3 colonies simultaneously over the next week!

Magic beans can be used for many things, including producing beanstalks to get valuable sector deeds. However, there's just one catch - they can only be obtained through fairytale adventures. Gather some friends and try to collect some for us!

Colonies are very useful - especially for topping up our resources - but they can only reach their maximum potential when they're properly defended. Please capture some colonies so we can get a decent amount of granite out of them.

Anyone who wants to keep their production output high will have to make a lot of buffs. We all have friends who practically never stop making new buffs. And if I know people like I think I know people, do you know what I think they'd love? A barazek buff right in the provision house. Wouldn’t you agree?

Perfect timing! This is going to be a busy week for our production workyards, so we’re going to need you to come over every day to make sure everyone's working as hard as they can. Can we count on you to do that?

We need to send a massive delivery of weapons to all of our barracks, and our current production chain will struggle to get the order completed in time. I’m afraid we'll need help from your allies to buff some of our production chains again. Can you please ask them?

Now that we know what gifts we need to deliver, we should start to produce them! Go to your Provision House and produce some of the objects required. We're going to need them if we want to make everyone happy!
Hint: If you have a Rarity Provision House, you can produce the same items there much faster.

Now that we know what gifts we need to deliver, we should start to produce them! Go to your Provision House and produce some of the objects required. We're going to need them if we want to make everyone happy!
Hint: If you have a Rarity Provision House, you can produce the same items there much faster.

Now that we know what gifts we need to deliver, we should start to produce them! Go to your Provision House and produce some of the objects required. We're going to need them if we want to make everyone happy!
Hint: If you have a Rarity Provision House, you can produce the same items there much faster.
Now finish delivering the presents to all the inhabitants on that island. This should give Santa a bit of a helping hand!

Merry Christmas, old friend! I’ve brought some new things with me to make this year’s Christmas even better!
Let me show you the new Christmas surprise, and how to get presents!
My reindeers are gone! Someone must have stolen them! How am I ever going to deliver those presents now!? This is your chance! You can save the day!
I found the evildoer who stole my Reindeers! He's hiding on an Island. I guess we should set sail and pay him a visit!
I found the evildoer who stole my Reindeers! He's hiding on an Island. I guess we should set sail and pay him a visit!
I found the evildoer who stole my Reindeers! He's hiding on an Island. I guess we should set sail and pay him a visit!
The next thing I want to show you requires you to be Level 16. Please come back when you've gained enough experience. For someone with your potential, that shouldn't take too long!
For the next task you need to be Level 23. Please come back when you've gained enough experience.
For the next task you need to be Level 26. Please come back when you've gained enough experience.

First, let's take a look at the brand-new Christmas surprise. Every day, you get to open a door, and find valuable things inside!
For special days like Christmas Eve or New Year’s Eve, you can choose in advance what reward you'd like to have.
And if you manage to open all the doors, you'll get a really special reward!
Even if you miss a door, you can always come back and open it afterwards with some gems.

The next thing I want to show you is how you can produce your own Christmas presents.
For this we need Christmas Bells, Candy Canes and Gingerbread. You can find those things on your Island - all you have to do is pick them up.
To get information about the Christmas event, open the Event Window. You can reach it via the option panel right underneath your avatar picture

Now that we have enough things to build our presents, we should give it a try!
Click on your mayor's house, select the "Collections" tab and produce a basket of presents.

The last thing I wanted to tell you is that your explorers can also find presents during their treasure searches.
Try it out, and send one of your explorers on a treasure search (short).

Let me tell you a little secret. It's not the reindeers that let my sleigh fly. They're just for show. I mean, I could use kittens, but imagine how silly that would look…
The trick here is a magic potion which can make any animal fly. So here's the plan: First, we'll train some horses, and we'll gather some wood to build fake antlers with. After all, they need to look like reindeers when people see them flying!
Then I simply give them my potion, and they should be able to help me deliver my presents.

I'm back, but I'm afraid I can't find the ingredients I need to brew the potion...
Perhaps you could help me out?
Here, take this list. That's everything you need to get. Oh, and could you bring me some malt brew while you’re at it?

Unfortunately, the guy who stole my reindeers has bribed the rulers of the island to protect him!
It seems we'll need to take an army with us if we're going to get them back!

Unfortunately, the guy who stole my reindeers has bribed the rulers of the island to protect him!
It seems we'll need to take an Army with us if we're going to get them back!

Unfortunately, the guy who stole my reindeers has bribed the rulers of the island to protect him!
It seems we'll need to take an Army with us if we're going to get them back!

I should have known! The evildoer was hired by the Croaker!
I don't know where he's hiding right now, but I think we need to build ourselves back up, and get ready for a showdown.

I should have known! The evildoer was hired by the Croaker!
I don't know where he's hiding right now, but I think we need to build ourselves back up, and get ready for a showdown.

I should have known! The evildoer was hired by the Croaker!
I don't know where he's hiding right now, but I think we need to build ourselves back up, and get ready for a showdown.

Look at all this destruction! The Nords have gone too far this time! I've spoken to the chief of the native villages, and he says the raiders stopped at nothing. They destroyed the people's dwellings, plundered their winter stocks and are now hunting the wildlife for sport. If you don't step in, the natives are doomed.
The Nords have built encampments all around the coast. Before we can fix the damage they've done, you must send them off the island.

You've dealt the Nords a heavy blow, but they refuse to surrender. They have taken refuge on their ships and continue to take potshots and send raiding parties. Lucky for us, the ships appear to be laden with black powder. If a lone saboteur can sneak on board, he may be able to set fire to them, and detonate them. I have a design for a timed fuse that will ensure the saboteur's safety. You'll need to provide some metal from your own storage, and collect some of the highly flammable wood found on this island.

Good news! The ships were carrying the pelts of the animals the Nords had slaughtered. We can use those to repair the villagers' tents. The bad news is that the explosions scattered them all over the island…
The natives are on the brink of starvation, but the wildlife needs time to recover from the Nords' thoughtless poaching. I'm afraid their survival hinges on your generosity.

Have you heard the ancient stories about the grand City of Glory? All my research regarding its location points to this very island. But except for some altars and the odd building, there is no trace of it to be found. Let us not give up too easy though. We will unearth the truth, and get access to the city's secrets together!
Bandits have set up camp on the island, and have been interfering with our research. We won't be able to properly investigate until we take care of them.

Have you noticed the altars scattered around the island? No wonder the bandits seem drawn to them. They seem to hold some sort of mysterious power. If we were to perform the proper rites at one of them, it could make it easier to liberate the others. Clear all bandits from a site's sector, produce the proper ritual item and offer it at the altar. You won't be disappointed!

I've had another look at the old reports and tales about the City of Glory. It should be located at the center of this island, but alas, there is nothing to be seen there but the desert. The only explanation I can come up with is that it must be buried beneath the sand. So, let's grab some shovels and get digging!

The glyphs hint that there's some sort of a connection between the six altars... If I understand this correctly, you have to activate all of them. Once that is taken care of, I will be able to lift the wards.

This must be the place. According to the people of this land, the Dragon calls itself Flafir. Could it be the same Flafir who terrorized these islands a hundred years ago? Incredible! As much as I want to study a live dragon, I'm afraid we cannot tolerate the destruction he is wreaking.

The island is teeming with the Flafir's minions. Not only does his presence corrupt the wildlife, but he's even amassed a following of cultists! Who would be crazy enough to worship a dragon? You'll have to fight them to get to Flafir.

Flafir is clever. His lair is at the top of the highest mountain, and your army's path is blocked by many obstacles. We'll need bridges to get through the swamp. We can find the basic materials here, but you'll have to use some of your own resources as well. The path up the mountain is littered with large boulders. Nothing that some strong soldiers with pickaxes can't handle, but you'll need to supply said pickaxes.

If this really is the same Flafir from a hundred years ago, then the legends speaking of dragons' immortality must be true! Which presents something of a problem for us. However, I did some research on local folklore, and might have found a way to slay one for good - a sword enchanted according to a specific ritual. The main ingredient, the dragonsbane herb, grows on this very island.
It is time to face Flafir himself. I won't lie, I'm actually kind of excited to see him. Don't let yourself be intimidated though - he may be an incredible sight, but he's still the enemy!
Some of our settlers are concerned that they'll be freezing their pants off when winter comes. They could use some extra coal, if we can spare it.

Our local tailor thinks he can develop a new kind of blanket that will keep everyone warm - even if they leave their home... He says he's going to need a bunch of cloth to create a sample, though. Can you give him what he needs?
The painter claims he's had an epiphany, and needs someone to write his memoirs. This could go on for a while... Do we have enough nibs?
The painter has heard some of our soldiers talking about their adventures in the desert, and he's asked if he can go along too. Could you take him on our next one? I just hope he doesn't get lost...

The inventor seems to be having second thoughts about shooting down the moon, so he wants a plan B. Apparently, that plan B is a giant grappling gun. He's asked if we can send him some crossbows to dismantle, so he can analyze their design.

You might want to sit down. I'm afraid the inventor has another request - he now wants a place to securely store the moon when he manages to shoot it down. He wants the finest cloth to wrap it in, and perhaps some titanium to secure it.

It seems the damage to the ship is actually a lot worse than originally thought. The riders want to hire a few volunteers to help with the repairs, but they'll need a LOT of tools for that. Can we spare some?

Our librarian has suggested that in order to get more... "classy" scholars here, we may need to adorn our books with a bit more... finery. Let's provide a bunch of classy book fittings, and see if that helps.

They've taken such a liking to our island, once they're all set for sailing they'd like to grab a bunch of souvenirs to take with them. They've suggested that we might want to attach some wheels to the souvenirs for easier transportation.

The king just mentioned that, apparently, people from high society don't like having to walk everywhere. For some reason, they'd rather have someone in a carriage take them around? I don't get it. How will they see the beauty of our island if they don't walk?

The legend says that anyone who looks into the mirror ponds will see a beautiful reflection. I'd like to put that to the test. Send our ugliest men there to see if it's true. How about the cannoneers?
In order to make this pond truly special, I thought it would be nice if we made some platinum decorations for it. Lady Amidale will love it, for sure!
One of the things that would really help us build these ships is if we had some robust cranes to transport materials. And what metal is more robust than titanium? We should make a titanium crane!
I'm starting to think that our regular horses won't be up to this. I know it's not their main purpose, but it may be a good idea to use battle horses this time instead? Can you bring a few?
It seems that we may have underestimated the amount of granite we needed for this request. Our guild mates cannot keep up. Can you perhaps help them out with some of your reserves?

When you're laying the foundations of an artificial mountain, you need to go really deep. I heard that platinum seems to absorb sunlight for a while, making it both a great tool and a flashlight in one! Handy! Let's put that theory to the test.

The miners want to put our structures to the test. They're planning to take some cannons down there, and fire them all at the same time. Personally, I think that's insane, but they seem rather confident. For their sake, I hope they know what they're doing.

One of the miners came out as white as a sheet. He says he heard a terrifying growling down in the mine, and he thinks there's a monster in there! Send some swordsmen in, and see if there's anything to worry about.

Having to carry our materials up into the trees, so high up in the air, is going to be an exhausting task. We should manufacture some sort of service lift that can hold a lot of weight. That should make our guild mates' tasks a lot easier!
Once everything's up there, we'll need to transport it across the bridges. A mahogany wheelbarrow should make things a lot easier. Why mahogany? Best weight-sturdiness ratio, of course!

Our local inventor has had an idea. He wants to make a comfortable parasol out of... hardwood. I know it sounds ridiculous, but hear me out! What other object offers great protection from the sun - AND from enemy arrows. Let's make one for the steel guard!

It's not that I don't trust the steel guard to get the job done, but you can never take too many precautions with these things. How about sending a few of our elite units to support them on their journey?

As the old saying goes - it's not a "feast" without a BBQ zone! We've finished the preparations, all we need now is to put the coal on the grill, and light up the sausages... Or is it the other way around?

Our local gourmet chef wants to share his latest invention with us. He says that all you have to do is to cook some toast on a fire made of mahogany. He calls it the best invention since... well, toast.
You know what we should do? We should throw a party for the travellers that come in. Some music, a few brews and our finest meat sausages. I can even do stand-up comedy if you want? No? Oh, ok...

When I was young, my momma took me to the town fair, and there was this nice booth where people could shoot some targets and get fluffy prizes. How about we modify some arquebuses and re-create the stall?

You may think that this is no ordinary birthday party - and I'd agree with you. But let's not forget that this is, after all, a child's birthday. Let's make an outdoors picnic for him and all of his guests.

His magnanimous majesty, the king's nephew would like to hold an award ceremony for the settlers that worked the hardest on making his birthday party perfect. We'll need a prize for them. Let's make golden mugs for the winners!

I've been thinking... What if we just move the hunter's hut a little bit further away? If he doesn't hunt any animals, we may be closer to winning the competition, right? Do you think this would count as cheating?

We should make a new stable. One specially designed to hold as many horses and battle horses as possible. Mahogany seems like a good choice. Its scent soothes the animals, and it's sturdy like... well, a horse.
We need to make some containers that are sturdy enough to transport fragile materials. A set of exotic planks reinforced with titanium should do it. Can you carry them to the workshop?

Once everything here is done, there's a high chance that we may have some problems with thieves. We'll need to install some kind of anti-theft system. I had mortars in mind. They make noise and scare the thieves away!

How convenient! A weapons dealer who only wants to be called "Mr. Metal" and claims to be "the best there is at what he does" wants to teach us a bit about the weapons trade. He wants us to buy some cannons.
The army is shaping up nicely thanks to the guild's efforts, but it's time to make things a bit trickier. Let's take them to a practical drill in the desert, so they know what we're up against.

Most of the troops we've lost were on adventures trying to make our kingdom better in every way. The best way to honour their lives would be to take our army on an adventure, and pay our respects to their memory in the process, don't you think?

Aside from the wall, the king would like a parade to be performed in memoriam of those who lost their lives. The general suggested that we should lead the parade with the finest battle horses, so let's do that.

The pretzel is obviously going to be eaten, but while we're supplying the coal for the massive oven, it would be a good idea to start telling our friends about it so they can try a bit. What better way to spread the word than by giving them a gift basket?

We have a problem. The world's biggest pretzel has attracted the attention of some of the world's biggest pigeons that want to eat it! But don't worry, I have a cunning plan! Spread as much bread as you can, as far away from it as possible, and the pigeons will go there instead!

The new roads will need better signs, so people know where the forks in the road lead to. They'll also have to be robust, so they don't get blown away by the wind. How about using some exotic wood planks for that?

In order to keep our economy stable, the king has ordered the construction of toll booths at several points across the kingdom. These booths will give a single platinum chip to whoever pays the toll - and we have to produce said chips.

If the queen is around here, but nobody's seen her for a while, she may be in trouble. I'd like to think that's not the case, but it's better if we make a few extra crossbows, just to be on the safe side.

The scouts aren't being very effective, so I'd like to create a separate party of your knights to become an official Search Task Force. Perhaps if the queen notices their shiny armour, she may come to the knights herself.

The musician has requested that we provide some materials so they can build a gorgeous stage made of marble. I've never seen even the wealthiest of singers on a stage made with such a fancy material, let alone chickens! Oh well, we'd best go along with it...

It seems that the chickens may have stage fright... Apparently, this is a common thing when performing for humans? The musician told us that the chickens would be a lot more comfortable performing before an animal audience, and asked us if we could round some up...

While our guild mates take care of the situation on Dagger Island, we should make sure that the bandits don't get reinforcements from the Nords. We should perform a pre-emptive strike on their island.

If I were a bandit (which I'm not), I would probably try to make contact with the east in search of potential allies. We cannot let that happen. To be sure, we should embark on an adventure in the desert!

Despite being a bunch of "expert" collectors, they've never seen any platinum ore. Now they've seen some of ours, they've asked if we can provide them with some of it so they can investigate where it comes from.
The ore collectors have been from island to island, but they haven't seen how titanium is collected yet. Can you perhaps take them to one of our mines, and see that they learn the trade?
We have been tasked with keeping our geologists in shape so they can keep up with the race. Let's prepare some meat for them so they're always on the top of their game!

Our geologists are the ones that have the most experience in searching for the rarest of materials. Therefore, it's up to us to top the rankings in this category. Let's try getting some saltpetre and titanium deposits working!
The clues we've gathered so far are vague and ambiguous, but there's a chance that the pirate buried his treasure on a certain adventure island. Maybe it's worth a check.

Some of our knights seem to be quite interested in the swashbuckling skills of pirates. They've requested some time, and a few weapons to study, so they can become an "Anti-Pirate Force", should we encounter any on our quests.

It's no surprise that we'll need a huge amount of marble to make this bridge, but our architect believes that the foundations of the bridge should be made of a more robust material. She suggests granite for that.
If we are to prevent another hurricane from tearing down the buildings here, we need to reinforce them with really strong materials. This sounds like a job for granite. Let's get some.

Marble is beautiful, but it's also a very heavy material for a bridge. We need to make sure that the links are not going to give in, so they have to be made from the toughest of metals: titanium. Please produce some!

The reason why grout is so valuable is because it's so very good at fixing materials together. It is extremely valuable, but in this time of emergency, I say we should give some of our own to those affected by the hurricane.

I've had an idea to ease the situation. A friendly competition of marksmanship. The nobles will test their skill against each other by shooting targets with a crossbow, and the winner will take a prize. Do you like it? Then let's get to it!

It seems the situation isn't going to get any easier. The nobles are being louder and rowdier than usual. Perhaps it would be a good idea to subtly remind them who's in charge here. Have some of your elite cavalry "casually stroll" around the area.
If we want to show how safe our island is, we'll need to prove we have the best of the best when it comes to weaponry. Make enough titanium swords to equip a small squad of soldiers!
We may have the edge in the technology stakes, so we should make sure we show it off to the judges. Let's give them a live demonstration of how our mortars work when operated by capable besiegers.
Just in case we run into trouble, we should bring enough gunpowder to load the ship's cannons. Make sure you produce enough!
I just had a thought... Maybe the captain landed on a deserted island. And by deserted I don't mean "without people", but an island with a desert on it. We should check the ones we know of for clues.
Coron wants to have printed versions of his maps at some point, including detailed explanations of each area. He needs us to provide the means for him to write these annotations.

Coron mentioned that when his work is done, he'd like to sell his maps in a "collector's edition". I guess there are collectors for everything! He's requested the finest paper, and an example of a really nice-looking book.
Your army needs to have a powerful artillery if it wants to be taken seriously. Can you provide the necessary gunpowder for this request?

As you know by now, the most powerful armies are equipped with the finest platinum swords. The blacksmith has taken a bet that he can produce platinum swords quicker than anyone else, so let's help him win this bet!

The general has had the idea of setting up some watchtowers, so the archers will have a clear view of their surroundings, as well as some protection from the bandits. He suggested said protection be made of granite, so let's provide him with some.

Archers are great, but you know what can't be beaten in terms of ranged weapons? Arquebuses. I'm sure that none of their troops has ever seen one, so let's make a few and show them what it's all about.
Your young apprentice arrived, and he's ready to join you in your adventure! We heard he's very brave, so he wants to be on the frontlines with our crossbowmen. Let's provide some.
Your young apprentice arrived, and he is ready to join you in your adventure! We heard he's very kind and friendly, so he wants to learn and practice the art of diplomacy with your allies.

If we ever had to deal with an escaped prisoner, we'd need someone who could put a stop to him in the blink of an eye. In this regard, an archer won't cut it. We'll need to deploy a few crossbowmen to watch the perimeter.

We should also prepare for the possibility of any of the prisoners' allies trying to stage a breakout. We need to make sure that we have the appropriate long-range defences to deal with enemy ships. Prepare some mortars.

We would like to throw a surprise party for Sir Rogen. We know he has a lot of friends where our allies live, so why not invite them over to the party as well? Tell them to bring a gift basket for him, too!

I think Sir Rogen deserves a fireworks show, and our chief engineer has offered to modify a few of our mortars to make the biggest and flashiest fireworks you'll ever see. Let's take him some mortars!

The Flintrock volcano has been a bit agitated lately. One way to make sure it doesn't explode any time soon is by throwing some water inside. After all, we all know water puts out fires, right? We'll need a lot of it, though, so get to it!

One of the locals told us that the volcano acts as the island's "stomach". The rumbles mean the island's tummy is hurting, and he suggests that we use a saline solution to calm it down a bit. Sounds like nonsense to me, but let's see if they're right!
Hardwood planks are fine. Exotic planks are better. But nothing beats mahogany planks for building a ship. Let's provide some for our engineers!

Grout is an excellent adhesive, as you know. What you probably didn't know is that once it dries out, it's completely waterproof! The king's engineers are scratching their heads about this. Can you obtain some grout so we can show them?
We can cover more ground if we split up. Let's call some of our friends and see if they can help us map out the area.

I noticed some mountains in the distance. We should probably check to see if they might be a source of the rare materials we need, but our geologist doesn't know exactly what he's looking for. Show him some platinum ore!

It seems that the bees in one of our beehives have gone a bit wild! I once heard from my grandpa that one of the best ways to get the bees to calm down again is to use smoke. Unfortunately, all I could find is this gunpowder. Oh well, close enough - let's give it a try.
The Queen is in danger! Some bandits have appeared and want to kidnap her! Quick, bring some arquebuses and let's defend her!
The brothers said they'll need some adhesive to make some "pipes", in order to test how they affect the sea wildlife. I have no idea what these are for, but whatever. Let's give them some grout.

The brothers heard that we had some magic beans with us, and they're a bit concerned in case any mutations happen due to water pollution. Let's build a mahogany fence and show them how we grow them so they can rest easy.

May I suggest something? As a gesture of goodwill, perhaps we might craft some exotic wood furniture and share the plans with our new guests? I'm sure they'll appreciate it - and it'll get us in the king's good books too!

Our guests have seen our mahogany reserves, and have asked for a lesson in the economy of mahogany production. I told them all they need to do is invest in some magic beans and craft the planks with adventure spoils, but they're insisting on a demonstration.

The bird trainer informs me that birds are incredibly sensitive of their surroundings. They tend to be a lot more comfortable if the forests around them are blooming with wildlife. Let's help the birds feel at home!

The trainer suggests we build a separate, bigger cage for the fastest birds. It should be made of exotic wood and granite. Apparently, exotic wood reminds them of their homeland, so they're a lot more comfortable there. Let's make it!

The composer has had an idea. He's suggested that we could use our cannons as percussion in his songs, but first he needs to understand how a cannon works. Can you take him into an open area with some cannoneers?
Our local musician has become great friends with Mike, and they want to put on a concert at our tavern! The problem is, his lute broke, so he needs a new one fast. Can we help him?

Sir Arminus will undoubtedly have a lot of interesting stories to tell about his experience. It's important that we document his adventures, so I've hired a professional writer to jot his tales down. Only problem is, I haven't paid him yet. Can you do that?
The military changed a lot while Sir Arminus was away. We should show him our new technology. Let's forge some platinum swords so he can get a good feel for our new "toys"!
Here's an idea. Certain parts of that mountain are inaccessible by road. If we make some staircases and climb up to their blind spots, we may be able to surprise the bandits. Let's try that!

At some point, some bandits will undoubtedly try to escape and make a break for freedom. We should provide some mounted marksmen to prevent this from happening - but we can't afford them to be inexperienced. Take them on an adventure first!
The king's blacksmith has reported that there's a shortage of weapons! We need to provide some additional hands at the blacksmith's to ensure the troops have enough titanium equipment.

Just because they weren't happy on their previous island doesn't mean there isn't a perfect place waiting for them, somewhere out there. Send a few horsemen on some adventures, and scout the terrain for other alternatives.

The king has issued an official statement declaring that he requires reinforcements for his personal army. We've been tasked with providing some mounted marksmen and knights for the war. For the kingdom!

The first refugees have started arriving on our island. We know how hard it is to start a new life, so let's make things a bit easier by showing them how to process granite and titanium. This will save them a lot of time.
Theodor's soldiers are only equipped with regular iron swords, which may not be the best idea if you want to appear strong. Let's show him how we produce titanium swords.
When we asked Theodor about his diplomatic plans, he just shrugged. Inconceivable! We should definitely explore this route. Let's prepare a peace offering and take it to their representative.

We should designate a relief party of elite soldiers that know how to handle a crisis, just in case the situation turns bad. Send them on some adventures so they know how to quickly respond to unexpected threats!
I'm worried that our wheat fields may wither away in the rainy weather. Let's make a barn out of mahogany wood and store our grain there until the weather clears a little bit.

Very, very deep within the mine, we reached a dead end. We believe there's still something behind the rocks that are in the way, but there's no way for us to get through. So, we've decided to blow the debris away with cannons. It's safe, I promise!
We want to prepare our miners to start excavating in search of minerals. We've got a batch of new recruits here, maybe we can teach them how to mine granite and saltpetre before going down there?

Among other things, sailors are known for their world-class quaffing competitions. We decided to host an official tournament called "All you can quaff"... with our finest brew! The prize is a granite bust of the winner. Let's prepare the mugs!

By now you're used to using saltpetre for making gunpowder, but did you know that it can also be used for spicing up food? And did you know that granite slabs also make for great frying pans? Let's produce some nice food to offer up!

There seems to be a lot of crime in the dark lands. It'd be nice to help the local authorities restore some order. Let's take them out with our soldiers on an adventure, see if they learn a few tricks.
It's really hard to grow crops in the dark lands, due to... well, the lack of sun. I have this theory, however, that magic beans would grow nicely if watered correctly. Let's try it out.

We'd like to offer an incentive to the captains that are sent to our royal garden for peacekeeping. How about a golden brew mug? I think this should be enough to keep the captain's attention on the job for at least a week.
In order to make our share of the garden unique, we should decorate it with some ornaments that can't be found anywhere else. Let's make some using platinum and exotic wood!
Will says that a renowned artisan once taught him how to craft some nice ornaments from granite and exotic wood. He'd like to make one for us as a memento of his visit. What a nice guy he is!

Will is a big detractor of weapons. But even he admits that arquebuses are a wonder of engineering. He thinks that by modifying some, he may be able to make them useful for some non-war related purposes too.
So, remember those missing pets? Yeah, the cat. Yeah... Turns out that may have been an understatement. It's actually much bigger and more fearsome than a cat. We need to set a trap for her.
We'll need to be able to store the pets in a proper cage as the rest of the guild finds them. Let's make the most robust cages we can, using mahogany planks and titanium.

The man with the long beard has asked if we could show him our books, to see if he can learn anything from our culture. He seems to have seen a lot of world and met some interesting people. Take him to the bookbinder!

The wizards have gathered in the tavern, and have started talking about using new materials to create new spells and concoctions. Maybe we can help them out by offering them some of our rarest materials?
A little creature, who looks like an imp, came to us while we were visiting and knew exactly what we were after. He's offered to share all he knows about the legend of the countess... for a price.
If we are to explore the haunted island, we'll need to assemble a force of the bravest soldiers we can muster. It'll be better for them if they have some horses, so train a few mounted units.

This time, we'd like to make a gift to the travelling frogs. We heard that there are some mushrooms that they particularly like, but, unfortunately, they don't grow on this island. Let's search for them while on an adventure.

To commemorate the day of the frogs, we decided to make some sort of monument. Well, actually it's more of a plaque by the pond, but it's the thought that counts. We'll need some granite to place it there.

Wildlife Control is a bit worried about our deer population. They've suggested that we give them time to breed and replenish their numbers by declaring this rabbit season for our hunters. We'll need a few signs to make this clear in the forest!

Wildlife Control mainly deal with animals, but they also care about our forests. They want to make sure that our exotic wood forests are not in danger, and so they're encouraging our foresters to do their bit!
We have to make sure that everyone stays warm when they're out in the snow. How about some eggnog in a golden brew mug? We'll hire someone to make it for us, don't worry!

We'd like to play a game where the kids put a magic bean inside a snowball and throw it as far as they can. Wherever it lands on the island, "their" magic beanstalk will grow. Let's distribute a few to the children and let them play.

The more we help the traveller fix his machine, the faster we get! The guild is already big enough as it is, but maybe we could ask some of our allies to help? Let's take them a gift basket. They can't say no to that!

The traveller's asked if we have some gum he could use to patch up his balloon, but the closest thing we have is grout. He's also looking to decorate his chronicles with a few nice bookfittings. Can we spare some?

In order to keep the prisoners fed, but minimize their chance of hijacking one of the king's ships to escape, the warden suggests planting some magic beans, so we have virtually endless food to feed the prisoners with.
The warden has seen our ranged elite units in action, and suggested they be just what we need to defend the prison. Let's send some marksmen to patrol the prison for a while. They'll be back soon.

The merchants from the yellow caravan want to perform a market study of the effect of including crossbows amongst their wares. To do that, they've asked if they could borrow a few of ours for a bit. Can we spare some?

The merchants want to make the ultimate luxurious item - the platinum brew mug. In order to do that, they want to get a couple of golden brew mugs, fuse them together, and then melt some platinum to coat both of them up. I'm curious to see how this turns out! Can we help?
One of our scientists has requested a few of the heaviest materials we have for research purposes. He's requested some titanium and gold ingots. Can you provide some?
We take pride in taking care of the less fortunate on our island. It's time to organize another campaign to feed the poorest souls. Prepare some bread and sausage, please.

Our titanium reserves are rapidly depleting, and we need to boost our mines. Let's invest in some tools to upgrade them - I'm sure you won't regret it. It's even more efficient if you combine it with some buffs!

A prize-winning chef is visiting our island to prepare some sort of special tasting session for our nobles. She has asked if we can provide saltpetre so she can craft her own salt, and some cloth to make the meal visually appealing. Can you provide these?
You know what's best at keeping our army's morale high? Winning! There's nothing like winning and feeling powerful. Win some battles with your army to remind them that they're the boss!

The best strategists always know how to minimize their losses in a battle. In fact, the ultimate challenge is to win a battle without giving your opponent time to react, and take no losses at all. I'm issuing that challenge to you now. Are you up to the task?
We must be ready for adventure! Our forces can never be too strong, so let's reinforce our numbers with some more troops.

The traitors are at it again, and the king has sent instructions to all our allies, telling us to take care of the traitors in different locations. We've been instructed to go to a very specific island. Let's see to it. For the king!

Sometimes, the best buffs aren't the most expensive ones. On deposits that are running low, a longer lasting buff may be wasted if the deposit depletes. Let's buff a friend with some solid sandwiches.

It's culture day! On culture day we set aside a small space, where we remind our settlers of the importance of reading books and sharing culture with one another. This tradition also allows us to exchange manuscripts with other islands.
Let's not underestimate the importance of bronze swords. They may be cheap weaponry, but they're the ones we use the most, which makes them incredibly valuable to us. Let's stock up on a few extras.

Our generals have suggested that we make some sort of shooting gallery so our marksmen can practice their skills with an arquebus. We should get some arquebuses that are specifically designed for a shooting gallery.
We just received a report that two brothers have gotten lost on a remote island, and their family has asked for our help to find them. Can we spare some time to help these poor children?
Many of our current weapons and units use gunpowder, so we need as much as we can get! Let's boost our gunpowder production as much as we can!

Some friends of the king are on their way to pay us a visit. And by "some" I mean a family. And by "family" I mean 100 people. It's definitely the biggest family I've ever seen. Let's produce a gift basket for every one of them!
Our ecosystem is a very delicate one. The newfound exotic wood forests need to be taken care of carefully, otherwise they'll become extinct! Let's make sure our foresters do their job properly!
Recently, there's been sightings of that mad scientist we encountered, carrying out his shady experiments once again. It's time we put an end to his madness. Take him down!
