We have no clue as to the whereabouts of this song. We should ask the people who live in the town in the center of the island.
It looks like the guards are on edge though... We might have to overpower them for them to let us in. I will tell your men to avoid lethal force.

Bad news - it looks like the song has been somewhat scattered around. In fact, single pages have been passed down through the families of the composer and original performers.
I have identified the individuals who own the pages now, but they aren't willing to part with them for free. Maybe we can help them out in some way, and ask for the sheets in exchange? I don't think we need all of them. King Roxy used to be a talented composer himself. He should be able to fill in some of the blanks if we jog his memory.

Due to a bout of bad luck, one page was blown away by a chill wind when the curse set upon the island. It was seen getting torn to shreds by a pack of wolves. The pieces have probably been scattered all over the island by now - and that's if they haven't been lost to the sea already.

The curse hit a small fishing hamlet on the south-western coast particularly hard. The buildings crumbled as if they were ancient. The fishermen had to withdraw to this town, and lost their livelihoods in the process. One of them owns a page of the Serenade, and will part with it if we help to rebuild the village.
However, it looks like a band of low-life bandits have turned the ruins into their base!
This place is even more wrecked than I'd thought. You'll have to rebuild it from the ground up. They can make do with only the most essential buildings for now, though.

The Woodson siblings are running the community's wood industry, but they've been hit by the curse in more than one way. Woodcutter Jane misplaced her axe, John's sawmill's saw has rusted away, and forester Toby claims that the soil has been sapped of all nutrients. And as if that wasn't enough, the forest has been overrun by some unnaturally aggressive predators!
The Woodsons have promised to hand over their family's page of the Serenade of Joy if you can help them out.
An old hunter claims that he has a page of the song in his hut on the south-eastern shore. We can keep the page if we defeat the bandits who drove him out of his home.

The local priest is concerned about the cultists that, lured by the dark energies unleashed by the curse, have landed on the northern shore and started manipulating the local bandits. They perform all sorts of hideous rituals at their twisted place of worship. The town's church treasury holds two pages of the Serenade of Joy, and the priest is willing to part with them provided you disband the evil cult.

King Roxy lets you know that he has studied the Serenade and managed to fill in the blanks suitably
He also said that if they are going to perform a legendary, magic song, we might as well assemble an audience. It’s not even a joke; the magic will allegedly be more potent the more people listen to the song!

Hey hey! Going on a journey is always so exciting. Remember when I told you about the difficult adventures, and how you can get valuable things from them? I've finally discovered a good route your explorer can use to find them.

Captain Mapparan is about to make a decision! I really hope he'll choose to settle on your island! I had a look at our stocks, and it seems we could use some more gold and platinum ore to really help seal the deal. Once we fill our stocks, I'm going to personally offer Captain Mapparan citizenship. Er, with your permission, of course. Send your generals on adventures, and bring back some gold and platinum ore!

Our elite army is impressive, but it seems our conventional army has been craving some action lately too. Let’s give them a challenge! Take them on a mission where our allies can’t help us, so they can see that they're still important to us.

Scenarios are very different to other adventures. Instead of sending your army in, you'll have to use your resources and skills to create the buffs needed to fix whatever situation you find yourself in. Oh, you say you already knew that? My apologies, I just came back from a VERY long vacation…
It seems our army has been a little agitated as of late. They want to be put to the test with a few adventures, so let's do just that.

Bringing allies on adventures is always helpful, but in some cases it's downright necessary. Some specific missions really teach you the true meaning of co-operation. Let’s take our friends on one of these co-operative missions!
The joys of co-operation! Wouldn’t you agree that adventures are always a lot more fun when someone has your back? Grab some friends and complete two co-operative missions together!

Oh man… Why am I looking so tired, you say? I've just returned from a follow-up adventure. I found it on a regular mission, and it didn't look that difficult, but man was it tricky. On the plus side, I was rewarded with a plethora of resources and buffs, and even blueprints for a building. Not such a bad deal after all!

Come, allow me to introduce you to an unusual acquaintance I made the last time I traveled to this island. This is King Roxy, ghost musician extraordinaire! When we first met, I helped him and his spectral band perform their songs again
Unfortunately, it seems their ghostly status has given their music some unintended qualities, and it's brought a curse upon the island! Fog has engulfed us, the sun has not risen in weeks, and all sorts of mishaps are befalling the populace.
However, legend speaks of a magic song hidden somewhere on this island - the "Serenade of Joy". If they were to perform this melodic masterpiece, I'm sure we could break the curse and restore the island to how it was.

Listen closely my friend, I have a cunning plan. Things aren't looking great as they stand. Our weapons cannot harm its stony skin. Even our cannons are shrugged off like mosquito bites. But there is another way to defeat him.
What animates this golem is its inner fire. If we can extinguish that, it should freeze and turn into stone. We tried regular water, but it had no effect. Perhaps now we should take the concentrated approach, and try purified water instead!
It's worth a shot. Tell your settlers to drop what they're doing and start producing purified water as soon as they can!
Alright, now let’s test those canisters of purified water! Simply click on the golem and a new window will appear. You can use your purified water there.

It works! The pure water has weakened him! Just imagine what a few more canisters would do.
Quick - let's produce enough pure water to bring him down!
- Defeat the golem by using enough pure water.

What?! That golem looks somehow... different? It's bigger! It seems the purified water is no longer effective. What else can we try?
Ah - our settlers do have another technique for making enriched water. Perhaps that could put out the golem's inner fire.
Come on, let's make some enriched water, and bring the greater golem down.
- Defeat the greater golem by using enough enriched water.

Wow, yet another type of golem! This one's even bigger - and it's on fire! Looks like the enriched water isn't working now either. In fact, it almost looks like this thing is protected by a curse of some kind.
For this, I think we'll need to call in the big guns. it's time to break out the holy water and douse this golem's inner fire!
Produce enough holy water to bring the ancient golem down.
- Defeat the ancient golem by using enough holy water.

Before we can overcome the golem, we have to get you to a certain level. There's no way you'll be able to take him on as you are! So just keep on leveling, and I'll come back to you when you're ready.

Have we met before? Your face looks familiar. Anyway, where are my manners?! My name is Eliot, and you look like you're confused about what's happening on your island. Don't worry - I'll talk you through everything you need to know. So, where shall we begin?!

First of all, you should try to get as many pumpkins as you can. Why? Because you can buy cool stuff with them! Even buildings! Buying pumpkin cemeteries is one way to get them. You find them at the merchant. There are different kinds, sizes and speeds available, so why not take a look and buy some?

Of course, you can also collect pumpkins in other ways. Besides pumpkin cemeteries, you can earn them by completing quests, taking part in several adventures, as collectibles in your home zone, buying them at the merchant, or as a reward for defeating a golem. Of course, you can also trade with other players!.Happy collecting!

Fortunately, I have a trump card - some glistening water. There's nothing more powerful than this. I'm sure it'll work!
Produce enough glistening water to bring the supreme golem down.
- Defeat the supreme golem by using enough glistening water.

Another supreme golem has gone astray on your island. I've already gathered everything I need from him, but I expect your settlers would be very grateful if you could defeat this one too.
- Defeat the supreme golem by using enough glistening water on it.

Merry Christmas, old friend! I’ve brought some new things with me to help make this Christmas even better!
Let me show you the new Christmas surprise, and how to get presents!
My reindeers have vanished! Someone must have stolen them! Oh, how am I ever going to deliver those presents now!? Perhaps you could help me out? This is your chance! You can save the day!
I found the evildoer who stole my reindeers! He's hiding on an island. I guess we should set sail and pay him a visit!
I found the evildoer who stole my reindeers! He's hiding on an island. I guess we should set sail and pay him a visit!
I found the evildoer who stole my reindeers! He's hiding on an island. I guess we should set sail and pay him a visit!

Let's take a look at the Christmas surprise! Each day you can open a door, and find valuable things inside.
For special days like Christmas Eve, you can even choose what reward you'd like to have. There are also some special doors that will give you the opportunity to help Santa out in some special gift delivering adventures.
If you miss a door, you can always come back and open it afterwards by spending some gems.

The next thing I want to show you is how you can produce your own Christmas presents.
For this, we'll need some Christmas bells, candy canes and gingerbread. You can find all the required bits and pieces on your island - all you have to do is pick them up.

Now that we've gathered enough stuff to build our presents, we should get to work!
Click on your Mayor's house, select the 'Collections' tab and produce 1 basket of presents.

The last thing I wanted to tell you is that your explorers can also find presents during their treasure searches.
Try it out, and send one of your explorers on a treasure search (short).

Let me tell you a little secret. It's not the reindeers that let my sleigh fly. They're just for show. I mean, I could let kittens drag the sleigh, but just imagine how silly that would look…
The trick here is a magic potion which can make any animal fly. So here's the plan: First, we'll train some horses, and we'll gather some wood to build fake antlers with. After all, they need to look like reindeers when people see them flying!
Then I simply give them my potion, and they should be able to help me deliver my presents.

I'm back, but I'm afraid I can't find the ingredients I need to brew the potion...
Perhaps you could help me out?
Here, take this list. That's everything you need to get. Oh, and could you bring me some malt brew while you’re at it?
Unfortunately, the thing I wanted to show you requires you to be Level 16. Please come back when you've gained enough experience. For someone with your potential, that shouldn't take too long!
For the next task you need to be Level 23. Please come back when you've gained enough experience.
For the next task you need to be Level 26. Please come back when you've gained enough experience.

Unfortunately, the guy who stole my reindeers has bribed the rulers of the island to protect him!
We'll need to take an army with us if we're going to get them back!

I should have known! The evildoer was hired by the Croaker!
Sadly, I don't know where he's hiding right now, but I think we need to build ourselves back up, and get ready for a showdown.

To access information about the Christmas event, open the Event Window. You can reach it via the option panel right below your avatar picture
Will you help Santa deliver some presents? I hid an adventure in the first door of your event calendar. Open the door, start the adventure and off we go!

Now that we know what gifts we need to deliver, we should start to produce them! Go to your provision house, and let's start ticking off the list! If we want to make everyone happy, we'll have to make sure we have everything we need!
Hint: If you have a rarity provision house, you can produce the items there too.

Hint: If you have a rarity provision house, you can produce the items there too.

Hint: If you have a rarity provision house, you can produce the items there too.
Now finish delivering the presents to all the inhabitants on the island. That should give Santa a bit of a helping hand!

The guild market is a collection of delicate items - and you get to decide which ones. The guild market vote is your opportunity to influence what the guild market stocks. Try it out and submit your vote. I've submitted mine already.
Made the wrong choice? That's sad, but don't worry. You can withdraw your vote submission and vote again! Why not try it out?
Let's take a look at the results from past votes. This will show you how the current selection for the guild market was chosen. I can't wait to see the results!
Did you hear about the guild market? I heard they're introducing a new system for their votes. Let's get over there and see what's new.

An unknown village was shortly visible when we flew over the Mountain Range. Due to this unusually dense fog, we couldn't make out who they were. But maybe they know something about the mysterious Mountain Clan.
One of our scouts has reported the village is surrounded by bandits and closed off by barricades. A voice over the barricades told us to get rid of the bandits if we want to meet with them.

Groups of Nord bandits have settled around the foot of the mountains. If we want to explore the region, we'll have to get past them. We'd better be careful though - those long beards look like they could be hiding extra weapons!

The people here seem to stem from a totally different Nord tribe, and welcomed us to their town of Varaldsvik. After we freed them from the Bandits they lost their initial reluctance. They say they are willing to assist us, but they need our help first. We have agreed to rebuild their village - and in return, they will provide us with all the information and help they can offer.

Now that the people of Varaldsvik have become our friends, they have entrusted us with the key to the path up north. We were told not to let any bandits through the gate when we depart, and to be especially careful not to let any "dreadful creatures" through. They seemed to be even more frightened of the creatures than the bandits. I wonder why that is...

One step forward, two steps back. To progress any further, we will have to build some sturdy bridges. Our new friends told us the path into the mountains should be located to the northeast of the village. But where do the other paths lead? As knowledge is power, maybe we should check out the other paths as well...

Those caves over there are emitting a very strong smell. I believe we should approach them carefully. There was a time when I studied the smells of hundreds of animals and beasts, and came to the conclusion that the stronger the smell, the higher the danger. But this particular smell, I do not recognize.

This region apparently hasn't seen a carpenter in a while. In order to proceed, we'll have to build a sturdy bridge that can withstand both the cold, and the strong winds here. The Nords village will benefit if we reconstruct the bridges here - and with their newly built smith, they've provided us with the right materials for the job.
Something seems definitely off with this group of bandits. How do they even survive surrounded by these beasts? We should approach them carefully to avoid running into a trap!
With my spyglasses, I can make out the ruins of what might have been a flourishing village decades ago. Let's take a closer look - we might discover something useful.
If we decide to prolong our stay and explore the region further, we'll have to repair the bridge first.
Wild creatures inhabit the ruins now, and they don't look too friendly. If we even want to try and gain some knowledge of the Mountain Clan, we'll have to deal with the wildlife first.
Some abandoned houses and remnants of fields are visible between the trees. What information could this place be hiding?
Repair the bridge or don't repair the bridge. For me, that's not a question. I want to see what we can discover! But in the end, it's your choice!
This area was abandoned some time ago. Long enough for the wildlife to move in and get in our way, anyway... Let's clear the ruins!

We are woefully unprepared for this weather! And it looks like it'll get even worse farther north. . Apparently, these local phenomena even affect the performance of your troops! I've summarized the effects in your zone-wide buff window.
Our objective, for now, seems clear: find the proper equipment, possibly from the locals, and get out of this valley safely. Just keep in mind that we can only carry up to 3 types of equipment at max.

Before you can deal with the villages, you'll have to get to them. As you can see, the valley is filled with vicious beasts.
The villainous Mountain Clan sends them down to torment us other Nords folk every so often, but these numbers are unusual and concerning...
Anyhoo, visibility is bad, so I'm afraid you'll have to clear the area sector by sector to see what's up ahead.
If you want to survive the north, you'll need more than one type of equipment. You should visit another village to get more. Hope your soldiers are ready!

What is this?! Are those the bandits you battled earlier? They must have known we'd be traveling farther north and laid a trap to get their revenge!
There's no way around it: you'll have to fight your way through!

If it's pelts they want, you might have to battle more beasts. Us Nords have an eye for quality, though. You'll want to defeat the leader caves. You can pick up the pelts there after the battle and pack them up with the other goods the villagers asked for in your provision house.

There are enough beasts and pelts around that we can begin trading with a third village. The weather's not going to get any better on this campaign of yours, believe me.
You should consider your options before you defeat those bandits and continue your journey.
If you rush forward without setting up trade with a third village, you'll face a tougher challenge further up the mountains - but on the plus side, your senses will sharpen, resulting in higher rewards from any subsequent mountain ventures!
If you need more equipment, you'll have to pay a visit to another village. I'm sure they'll appreciate us getting rid of the beasts too.

Well met, strangers! Found yourself in a bit of trouble, eh? It's pretty apparent you have no idea how to survive up here. What you really need is some Nord-made gear.
I'm just a lone hermit, but the villages nearby trade gear all the time.
Gullhaugr produces Snow Shoes, Sjorheimr offers Spikes for your boots, Skaustad makes Warm Clothes, and Jarnbu is famous for its Snow Goggles.
You'll want to get at least two of those for your army, or you're gonna send them to their certain death.

The villagers of Gullhaugr produce wooden snow shoes. Daily labor there involves carrying gold between the mines, the smiths, and the manufacturers, so not getting slowed down by the deep snow is a huge benefit!
The village has agreed to equip your army in exchange for a stack of pelts and resources from your home island.

Sjorheimr sustains itself by fishing in that large lake. When it's frozen, the fishermen and women just cut holes through the ice! When that happens, they attach metal spikes to their boots so they can safely walk on the slippery surface.
Since they aren't hunters, they're running low on pelts. Hunt some wildlife, throw in some resources, and they will gladly trade.

While all clans know how to make decent fur clothing, Skaustad's is of the quality you'll need if you want to head deeper into the mountains. Even the most piercing cold will feel like a gentle autumn breeze if you wear a set of these.
The villagers usually hunt for the pelts themselves, but the wildlife has become a lot more dangerous recently. You'll have to supply them with the necessary pelts to equip your troops, and compensate them for their labor.

Jarnbu is known for their blacksmiths and weaponsmiths. They even developed some special glasses that protect their eyes from the embers. All you need to know is, they also keep wind and snow out of your eyes in a storm!
The people of Jarnbu love decorating their homes with hunting trophies. They would happily trade some "goggles" for pelts, and a few other resources.

There's nothing but canyons and valleys as far as the eye can see. It seems only very experienced climbers will be able to get through here. Needless to say, our armies are anything but. Let's see what we can find in this area. I certainly don't want to double back, as we're well past the point of no return.
As our scouts can't see very well in this fog, climbing higher up could be deadly. The best way forward is probably to tackle each challenge step by step. If only we knew someone who knows the ropes around here...

So you still want to continue your journey into the bloody cold mountains, eh? The only clue I can give you is that somewhere to the north, there should be some kind of structure. I've got no idea what it could be. Unfortunately for you, all the paths seem to be blocked. Probably the doings of this diabolic Mountain Clan.
Maybe we should try and find out more about the bearded Mountain Clan women...

It feels like the path you need to follow now leads to the east. How do I know this? Obviously, we Nords can smell the path through the mountains. But I have no idea what's waiting for us in that direction. I have never been this far into the mountains...

You've probably already heard the terrifying stories about the folk from the mountains. I would advise gathering as much information as possible before we meet them. Maybe we can find some clues in anything they've left behind in this region.

Have you heard the terrible tale Nord parents tell their children? They say if a child misbehaves, the parents ring a bell, and a cart collecting badly behaved children would take them away to work in the Mountain Clan mines. Want to go and see if you can find any proof of it, eh?

Rumors about people being seen in boiling hot water spread like wildfire decades ago.
A long time ago a Nord hunter reported watching a group of unknown people from afar, shrouded in thick fog. The rumor goes that the hunter witnessed how one person threw another into the bubbling water.
The result was many wild theories about the Mountain Clan, and more stories for parents to tell their kids.
Still sure you don´t want to abandon your expedition? Bwahaha...

The Nord explorers returned exhausted and scared. They told stories of bodies that were left hanging on the cliffsides near some Mountain Clan Ruins. Supposedly as a warning to anyone who wanted to enter the Mountain Clan realm.
No offence, but the way your city is right now, it's really not ready to hold the festivities. If you can grow it just a little bit more, we'll be all set!

Surprise! I've brought you a little present since it's Easter, and, well, you know, Easter! Anyway, I need your help with some Easter related tasks. Since I know there are a lot of slackers out there, I've decided to only be generous to those who really help me out.
So, here's the deal: I will give you a special building for your island. It's a special Easter building with a twist: Instead of paying for its upgrades, I want you to do stuff for me. What kind of stuff? Well, let's start at the beginning.

So, what do I need you to do?
Check out the Achievement panel! There are specific Easter-related achievements that you can only do during this event. Each achievement gives you points specific to this event.
I will give you the Easter Achievement building now. Instead of spending resources on upgrades, it can be upgraded when you earn achievements and collect more achievement points from the Easter event. Every new upgrade level will require more points.
Check out what you can do in the Achievement panel!

Of course, before you can start upgrading it and take advantage of this lovely building, you'll need to place it somewhere on your island.
A university, though? Where would you put a university? Maybe near to plenty of residencies? I can imagine people not wanting to walk a long way from their homes?

Oh no, this is bad! These guys are the party crashers. They're trying to ruin our Easter festivities by taking some of our eggs! We can fight them, or we can try to smooth things over peacefully. The choice is yours, but we have to address this problem before they cause more trouble!
I personally believe that this situation can be resolved without fighting. Maybe if we give them something they really like, we can reach a truce and they'll stop bothering us for a while.
So these guys want to prepare for trouble? Then make it double! If we send our troops to "meet them", I'm sure they'll have second thoughts, and will go look for trouble somewhere else.
Ugh... here they are again. These guys seem to be fixated on crashing our party - and this time, they've bought backup! How will we deal with them today?

My cousin has an island there? Where did he get it? Anyway, it doesn't matter. Just make sure you get all eggs he has hidden. Why I am not going? Isn't that obvious? I need an alibi for the time being, so if you need to find me I'll be in the tavern!

Well, the Easter Bunny's first criticism was that I have no friends and no one likes me. I'm the shy type, you know? So what's a loner like me to do? That's right! You can help me buy myself some friends. Find some money, give it to me and we can start buying them up! What? Don't worry, you'll get your money back... probably!

Oh no! It can't be! He already has way more than me. You! You have to help me! I've made a bet with my cousin that I would manage to get more Easter eggs than him, but he's cheating and now I'm way behind. We need to do outdo him, but your storage is way too full! Come on! Make space for the eggs!

I've heard a rumour that there are hidden Easter eggs on this island, and whoever finds them can keep them. Whatever the story, we need these eggs if we're to win the competition. What are you waiting for? Let's go!

The bad news is that he only helps people having a certain reputation… which basically means he dislikes your empty storage. I suppose we should fill your storage again then. Am I right?

After our fabulous efforts, the guy agreed to help us and gave me the location of a new Easter egg island. So grab your stuff and follow me to victory!

There is not much time left, and we need more eggs to win the competition. It doesn't matter how you get them. Just get them so I stand a chance against my cousin.

Here we are! Time to set up camp and hunt those pirates down.
We've finally arrived. Looks like there's a village nearby. We should contact it, and help Lord Walder.
Hmmm... It does smell as if something was burned recently. Not a good sign. We should get moving and help these people.
I'm still not sure I believe the story, but here we are. We should find those pirates and help them.
That's a pretty nice island to get as a gift from a King. Ohh yes, yes you're right - we should search for Gregorid and help his family.
Do you hear that? Silence. We should be careful, the Nords are fearsome warriors.
Welcome to Bastille Island, the most famous prison in the world. We should scout the area and clean-up a little bit.

We have to find a way to cross the river, and reach the Lair of the Frost Giant King. The Mountain Clan call him Risi. They told us he and (as they call them) his generals launch their attacks from an area north of the river.
With the Mountain Clan's help, and the outpost we built here, we should be able to work out a plan to defeat this ancient evil.
I'll keep sending out scouts, and will let you know when we spot anything that might lead us to the Frost Giant King´s Lair.

The Mountain Clan demolished these bridges a long time ago to keep the giant creatures in check. But somehow, they still found a way to cross the river.
We have to repair at least one of them if we want to get across.
The good news is that they also carry materials that could be useful to repair the bridges. We should check out camps near the bridges where they cross over to this side.

Our scouts will let us know when we're getting close to the Frost Giant King's Lair, before we reach the point of no return. If we continue our journey north after that, we won't be able to catch the remaining generals before they're able to regroup with their King and troops.

Risi gains strength when his generals are nearby. We know that much. One theory is that they carry some gear or weapons that they return to Risi when they regroup. If we manage to wipe out the generals before they have a chance to regroup with Risi, we may be able to weaken him.
On the other hand, if we just rush towards the Lair of the Frost Giant King, an alarm will be raised and the generals will have time to retreat and regroup with Risi. We want to avoid that at all costs, or we'll have to face their full power.
With one general down, Risi will need more time before he can attack. With two generals down, he'll lose some of his power, although he'll still be a tough foe. With three generals down, Risi will be weak, and unable to deal anywhere near as much damage. And if we defeat all his generals defeated, Risi will be left alone and vulnerable, unable to even hit a barn with a rock.
That´s all we know. It´s up to you to decide our approach.

This Elk is in a constant rage. Its antlers resemble huge trees, each a deadly weapon. It's fast, hard to hit and tramples over everything in its way.
We have to defeat it, either before or after we reach Risi´s Lair.

Not just a regular Mammoth, this is a smarter, sturdier and deadlier foe. Speaking from personal experience, it's also pretty tough to evade its tusks when it´s chasing you.
We have to defeat it, either before or after we reach Risi´s Lair.

That nasty kitty is responsible for a lot of pain. Many of us would be moved to tears if you can bring it down. But be warned. It might not be as sturdy as the other generals, but it packs a huge punch - so you'd better not get hit!
We have to defeat it, either before or after we reach Risi´s Lair.

This beast has such impressive eyesight, it's able to pick you out from hundreds of miles away, even in a forest at the dead of night. Its huge wings and feathers are an impressive sight, but one only a few have been able to live to recall.
We have to defeat it, either before or after we reach Risi´s Lair.

A young boy was playing on the beach and found a very beautiful stone.
But what kind of stone is it? And is it valuable?
We'll need to clean the stone up a bit before we can take a better look at it. Right now, it's just too dirty.
It's beautiful, but without knowing anything about stones, it's hard to say that much more. Why not ask some experts from the smelters. Of course, they'll want something in exchange for their help...

As we've got a bit of time on our hands, let's go to the beach. I happen to know exactly where that boy found the stone - let's see if we can find any more! Still, we should be careful - some settlers have already got wind of our precious stone...
Oh no! The rumours about your stone are spreading. We cannot defend it on our own.Please send some of your military units to protect your island.
The experts have been waiting for you. They're eager to share what they've learnt.

Of course, before you can start upgrading it and take full advantage of this lovely building, you'll need to place it somewhere on your island.
It looks a little bizarre, doesn't it? Where do you think would it look best?

Now that you've proven yourself, there is something I have to tell you. I myself am a member of the Mountain Clan.
Do not be alarmed! The stories about us are all a fiction - one that we ourselves spread to keep the other clans away... Look. We really need your help. I'll tell you all the details as we go.

As much as you've already proven yourself in my eyes, my clan will be hesitant to simply take my word for it.
It looks like the outpost to the east of here is under attack - a bad sign, but also an opportunity for you to show your worth.
These beasts aren't really sent by our clan; they are the minions of our ancestral enemy.

Look around this war-ravaged land. This was once the majestic and flourishing city fortress Skjoldrborg. But not any more. Now it is much more of a provision base.
The reason we withdrew to the mountains was to make a stand against an ancient evil, the jötnar. Our clan has been fighting these frost giants for a long time now, and while we couldn't defeat them, we at least managed to confine them to these mountains.
But this conflict has started to wear on us. Not just our spirit, but our defenses as well! It looks like the gates to the north of our city fortress have been broken.
If we cannot repair and reinforce them with obsidian, it will only be a matter of time until the jötnar overrun us!

If we don't want the gates to break again, we'll have to re-establish an outpost to the north of them. The ruins of our last fortress may be foreboding, but they should make for a decent foundation.
First, we must clear the area of the jötnar's forces.

Oh no! They broke through! See how the beasts have already dug new caves behind our unreinforced gates?
We must defeat them all before we can focus on your outpost again.
The clan's builders are now safe to work on that outpost, at least for the time being. Think hard about what building would be most useful, and deliver them a Construction Kit from your home island.

Another wave of beasts got past the unsecured gate(s).
Take them out before they do any more damage!

You've earned us another breather, and the clan can spare some workers for your outpost. How about we construct another building? Just make sure it's not the same type as before - that wouldn't help us much in the long run.

Another wave of beasts got past the unsecured gates!
Take them out before they do any more damage!

You've pushed all the enemies back for now, and there's still room for one more building in your outpost.
Remember: If you you want to get the most out of it, you'll want to avoid constructing a building you already have.

When the giants broke into this area, we had to abandon our stone quarry in the south west of the city fortress.
We used to find obsidian there on occasion, so there might just be some left. The clan has developed a method to harden obsidian into an incredibly durable state - something which would be perfect for reinforcing the gates.

Some beasts got past our defences and are harassing our farms!
We'll need all the food we can get if the siege drags on any longer... Though we trust you can break the siege soon, we could always repurpose the obsidian tools for reinforcing our gates.

An old woman lives west of the central fortress all by herself. Some say she's a witch, but I know better - she's a proper, scientific alchemist!
As far as I know, she's been studying obsidian for the past few years. If you can fight your way to her home, she'd probably be willing to share some of her samples with us for our gates.

Our blacksmiths have been working in shifts, day and night, every day, for years. However, it looks like the forge has finally given in to the wear and tear, and has broken down.
We must repair it soon, or we won't be able to keep up the fight much longer.
The clan elders are eager to put that stone quarry back to work, but it's suffered substantial damage. If you can repair it, we might be able to find more Obsidian.

The clan wants to restore the farms you reclaimed to working condition, but our fields have been pushed to their limits for some time. If we want to start growing again, we'll need to restore some nutrients to the ground first.
And don't worry about the obsidian from earlier - we have some spare metal tools we can use.

Laire, the old alchemist, has requested your help with an experiment. She claims to have discovered a way to artificially create obsidian!
Her concoction has been brewing for weeks now, and is almost ready for testing. But now that the whole clan finds itself locked in battle, her supply line has dried up. She's asking if you'd be willing to share your personal resources.

I've just been informed that our well has dried up. That's unusual, as it's being fed by an underground river, and so it should actually be impossible. Sabotage is the only explanation!
The snow around here is too polluted from the constant battles the area's seen. Our only option is to import clean water. Will you help us out yet again?

The deer population is shrinking! You'll need to figure out what's causing it, and find some way of restoring the natural balance.
Find the source of the problem, and help the deers to recover.
First of all, you'll need to get a feel for the size of the deer population. Ask the hunters to create a list of deer.
The number of deer has been falling dramatically over the past few days. But why? You should check in with the hunters again, and ask them about the wolves.
The wolves are behaving pretty normally. They're not overeating, and their population is stable. So how comes the deer population is still dwindling? Best talk with the forester.
You should probably try to give the woodcutters, the foresters, and the sawmills a bit of a helping hand, to thank them for their research.
A very excited settler reached out to me, as he'd seen some strangers poaching our deer. That would explain a lot. We need to track down these strangers, and teach them a lesson.
Yes, seemingly that was the cause of our deer related issues. Let's give the hunter a hand, and give the deer chance to get back to normal.

A girl was playing in the forest, and she found a small puppy. She came to us desperate for help, as the puppy is wounded, and she can't treat its wounds alone. Help her nurse the puppy back to health.
The girl holds the little pup in her arms as it shivers, covered in wounds. Having a warm bed would make a huge difference.
It seems like the puppy's starting to feel a little better - but until we treat his wounds, it's still touch and go.
The puppy is finally starting to pick up. We should make sure he has enough to eat and drink until he's fully recovered.
Let's find out where it's coming from. Maybe the little guy came from another island and got attacked by the local wolves..
The little pup is growing stronger - he's definitely going to make it through. Let's see if it'd be possible to return him to the forest.

Welcome to the Mountain Clan's city fortress, Skjoldrborg!
Let us visit the main hall first. The Clan Elders can brief us on the current situation, and I can report back from my exploratory mission.

A guard on the western gate tower saw a bunch of animals sneaking around in the abandoned stronghold in our hinterland north-west of the city fortress. They're probably devising another of their canny plans to sabotage or destroy our defenses. If we can spare the resources, we should take care of them.
It seems there are still townspeople hiding out in our old mining district north east of the Main Hall. They lit signal fires, so they probably need our help! We'd better hurry!
Alright. We've managed to defuse the situation, but this alone won't help us back on our feet. We have to restore our basic supplies first. Let me check with the Clan Elders on what needs to be done.

Did you hear? The Settlers Football Championship is coming up again! Counties and Kingdoms from all over the continent will be taking part - and we should too, to gain glory and honour for our kingdom. There are prizes to be won, too! By trading the footballs we gather through quests and activities, we could win some amazing stuff! Let me explain how it all works!
Finish all the introduction quests in order to participate in the tournament.
All parties must be at least level 16 to be able to participate in the Football Championship.
Now the first step. To access information about the Football Championship, open the event window. You can reach it via the options panel, which is right beneath your avatar picture.

Did you notice the calendar button next to your avatar's picture? Using it opens the tournament's fixture list. This is the most important part of the tournament. Green doors contain your next tournament opponent, brown doors hold a nice present for you, and golden doors contain a special thank you! However, you can only open a golden door if you've managed to open every door that came before it. By the way, you can open green doors at any time during the event.

At the moment, our Settlers are all going totally crazy about football. As they aren't the tidiest bunch, it's actually possible to find some items by simply collecting the things these football maniacs have left behind.
To find some more exotic items, you can send out your explorers. They'll observe the other teams, and return with interesting items, so we can improve our own tactics.

Once we've collected enough utensils, we should start to transform those into tactics we can use on the playing pitch. Go to your provision house and order a foul. We're going to need it to defeat their midfielder.
Hint: If you have a rarity provision house, you can produce the same items there much faster.

The practice match you found in the fixture list will help us to prepare for the tournament proper. The Knight of Crowrock has agreed to let us practice against his team. Start the match and defeat your opponent!

The tournament has started. To win the Settlers‘ Football Championship we have to win 4 matches in a row. Just remember to regularly check the Football Championship fixture list. You can find your next opponents by opening the green doors.

Now it's getting serious. Our first knock-out match, against the Shire of Oxwater. During the group stage they showed skill in attacking, while maintaining a stabile defence. They play in a 4-2-4 system – that means with four set strikers.

In the quarter finals, we will play the Electorate of Sunflower Grove. They've certainly earned their place amongst the last eight teams in the tournament. Similar to our former opponent they play with a strong attacking squad, although their midfield is a little more balanced. This will be a tough enemy.

Semi-finals… what a wonderful day. If you'd have told me at the beginning of the tournament that we would make it this far, I wouldn’t have believed you. But here we are, up against the grand Duchy of Darkwood. What do you need to know about this opponent? They stand closely staggered in a 1-4-1-4 system and have many strong players.

Can you feel it? The air is filled with a mixture of tension, anticipation, and energy… it’s the day of the finals. Our opponent is the Kingdom of Dragonhead. They were always one of the best teams in the tournament, but they'll soon be second best! All players in this team are strong, and they are confident to boot. But they've never played us. Go out on the field and show them what we're made of!

You are going to host some of this year's tournament games on your island! That's certainly exciting, but it'll also be a lot of work.
Will you be able to handle all the daily responsibilities? Don't worry if you fall behind, though - even if you finish a quest late, the next one will be waiting for you until the end of the tournament.
If your island is to host official matches, you'll need a professional playing field first. It doesn't have to be expensive, but the measurements and markings must be precise.

You'll need plenty of personnel to handle all the jobs that come with organizing and conducting games - not to mention catering for the tourists! Let's find some eager settlers, and prepare some training literature for them.
With the games proper starting in only a few days, we're going to need to provide plenty of tickets for the fans - and that's going to take some work. You should get started soon!
Soccer games are long, and the spectators might get hungry. Seems like a good opportunity to make some coin. But if you want to sell food, you'll need some stands to sell them from first.

I have found the perfect dish to sell on your food stands! It's called a "hot dog", and they've been selling it during matches on other islands. No idea what that name's about though - it's just a sausage in a bun. Both ingredients have to be fresh!

We've received so many visitors, many are having to stay in the far corners of the island. As such, they end up having to walk long distances to the games, and some of them are getting completely lost. Can you organize some wagons to get people to the playing field on time?

For many, traveling to this tournament is a once-in-a-lifetime luxury, and they'd love to take something home to remember it by.
As it so happens, I've already had a few ideas. You could sell dolls in the players' likenesses, soccer balls, or shirts like the players wear on the field.

There have been some reports of a few brawls among the audience during past few games. Some people are saying they don't feel safe, and I think they may have a point. Can you post a few guards to keep an eye on things?
Fans have been asking for autographs, and the players are happy to oblige! Or at least, they would be - but they don't have any pens or paper on them!
Your last formal responsibility as an organizer is to sponsor a set of medals, to be awarded to the winning team and runner ups.
You applied as an organizer and host for this year's tournament, but the other organizers think you're still a little too green behind the ears. Maybe come back when you've gathered more experience?

Your last formal responsibility as an organizer is to sponsor a set of medals, to be awarded to the winning team and runner ups.

You are going to host some of this year's tournament games on your island! That's certainly exciting, but it'll also be a lot of work.
Will you be able to handle all the daily responsibilities? Don't worry if you fall behind, though - even if you finish a quest late, the next one will be waiting for you until the end of the tournament.
If your island is to host official matches, you'll need a professional playing field first. It doesn't have to be expensive, but the measurements and markings must be precise.

You'll need plenty of personnel to handle all the jobs that come with organizing and conducting games - not to mention catering for the tourists! Let's find some eager settlers, and prepare some training literature for them.
With the games proper starting in only a few days, we're going to need to provide plenty of tickets for the fans - and that's going to take some work. You should get started soon!
Soccer games are long, and the spectators might get hungry. Seems like a good opportunity to make some coin. But if you want to sell food, you'll need some stands to sell them from first.

I have found the perfect dish to sell on your food stands! It's called a "hot dog", and they've been selling it during matches on other islands. No idea what that name's about though - it's just a sausage in a bun. Both ingredients have to be fresh!

We've received so many visitors, many are having to stay in the far corners of the island. As such, they end up having to walk long distances to the games, and some of them are getting completely lost. Can you organize some wagons to get people to the playing field on time?

For many, traveling to this tournament is a once-in-a-lifetime luxury, and they'd love to take something home to remember it by.
As it so happens, I've already had a few ideas. You could sell dolls in the players' likenesses, soccer balls, or shirts like the players wear on the field.

Your players' jerseys are starting to show some wear and tear. If they're going to be representing your island, they really should look the part. Luckily, I've already found a decent tailor who can bring the kits up to scratch. She just needs some supplies.
You certainly seem confident that your team is going to win the championship. If you're really sure, you should commission some fireworks for the inevitable victory celebration.

A friendly rival has given me a tip that an unknown, dishonorable opponent is sabotaging competing teams' training equipment. It would be wise to post a couple of elite soldiers outside the store room at night.
Your team is slacking off during practice. It's time to show them what training really means! We'll have them join your troops for a few drills under one of the more notorious drill sergeants.
Your team has so many fans that the stands are threatening to collapse under their combined weight! You must reinforce them with better wood.

Your strikers have been practicing shots for hours - and the practice balls can't take much more. We'll need to have some new balls made - but for that, we'll need some raw materials first. You can ask the butchers to hold on to bladders and leather.

Your settlers would like to support your team however they can, both during and after matches, and have specifically asked about the use of confetti. Only the best paper on the island will make for colourful and light confetti. It seems like a bit of a waste, but motivation goes a long way towards winning the tournament.

Rumbling... Shaking... Aunt Irma´s Gift Basket falling off the table... Something awful is happening on our home island! It seems the big mountain near the archipelago has lost its temper - and its head! Seemingly the volcano wasn´t as dormant as everyone thought... We need take care of this crisis before anyone gets seriously hurt!

We should start by taking a closer look at this newborn volcano. However, in order to get close enough, we'll first have to explore the land surrounding the former mountain, and dispatch any foes blocking our path. This has to be done, for the sake of all Settlers!

An expedition crew has to be sent into the mountain. As this is the first time we've encountered a situation like this, I will lead the expedition personally. We'll have to dig deep if we're going to get any conclusive information about this volcano's activity.

It doesn´t look like the volcano's going to erupt any time soon - but that doesn´t mean it´s harmless, either. Tremors are being felt on a regular basis, and each is enough to put our residents into a flurry. Not to mention all those broken coffee cups!
I found some old diagrams that detail how to build a seismoscope. It may not solve the crisis, but it'll definitely give the residents some peace of mind.

There are legends of a tribe of Nords living high in the mountains. They are experts in mining, smithing, and the construction of huge strongholds. If the legends are true, perhaps you can meet the Nords yourself - and maybe you'll be able to convince them to help you out during this crisis.

Finally, the Mountain Clan can live in peace. For the first time in ages, they can dare to leave their home in the mountains without having to fear the dreadful consequences. As a way of showing their gratitude for everything we´ve done, they've sent their best workers to help us solve our mountain crisis.
But that's not all. They promised that not only will they help stop any further earthquakes, but they can also put the vulcanic might to good use, and power an Epic Forge with it!
Go and build this fiery masterpiece.

Have you had a think about how you're going to house the players and the fans? They'll all need places to stay! You may want to build more residences.
Note: Completing this quest will increase your population growth during the event.

The weather's really hot at the moment. Maybe we should prioritize stocking those snack stands with drinks before we consider food. After all, we don't want our tourists fainting now, do we?
Note: Completing this quest will increase your population growth during the event.

The hot dogs are a great success! Maybe you can expand the menu? Aunt Irma always has good ideas. Why not prepare some gift baskets?
Note: Completing this quest will increase your population growth during the event.

The fans are swarming your snack stands! We didn't anticipate this kind of demand! We need to establish a stable supply line quickly, or we'll have a lot of grumpy tourists on our hands!
Note: Completing this quest will increase your population growth during the event.

The tournament is as good as over, but the tourists like your island a lot and are hesitant to leave. They are feeling a little bored though. How about telling them some stories of your travels?
Note: Completing this quest will increase your population growth during the event.
Sorry, aren't you still a little green behind the ears? Even a fool like me can see that! Shouldn't you be putting a bit more effort into your island before you think about visiting a party?

Oh, hello - when did you get here? We were just about to celebrate this island's discovery, with bright balloons and delicious cake! But hold your horses! If you want to join in, you'll need to help with the preparations. Let this party king show you how.

The celebration will be held in the Festival Hall we erected on the small island on that lake of yours. You don't mind, do you? Actually, why don't you pay it a visit? You can order your settlers to deliver resources to trade for balloons too.

If we serve cake in the festival hall, everyone will be extra motivated - and that means you'll get more balloons in return for your resources!
To make a nice birthday cake, you'll need cake dough, and some pretty candles. Yes, the candles are important! Unfortunately, the last candle shipment was intercepted by pirates - and they've hidden the "treasure" across your and your neighbours' islands.

It looks like you'll have to trade with your neighbours to get the remaining ingredients. Don't worry, though - it looks like they're in a similar situation! When you have enough candles and cake dough, produce the cake in your provision house, and bring it to the Festival Hall.
And do hurry! I'm hungry!

Alright - now I'm both full and rested, let's get to the meat of the matter. You're collecting all these balloons so we can use them for our party. You must deliver them from the storage menu of one of your storehouses. Click the balloons to find the option. Ha ha, what does "click" even mean?

Yaaaaaawn! I know you're busy with the whole balloon business, but I could really use some action, you know? Something big must be going on *somewhere*. Not that any news ever reaches us here... Maybe if your settlement was a little bit more... significant?

Can you believe what this report says?! Buildings - nay, entire landscapes - have magically changed their appearance! And now they look as though they were made of children's toy blocks! Wouldn't it be hilarious to have buildings like that here on your island? I can just see the look of shock on everyone's faces, ha ha ha! Let's investigate!
Wow, it's true! I've just returned from a visit to an affected island, and everything was all funny-looking! I've gotta show you!
Ha ha! A sailor told me about another island with those weird buildings on it. Let's check it out! Go, go, go!

So, here's the deal! This festival will be the greatest the world has ever seen! And you can never have enough balloons, oh no!
Everyone will be helping to get things ready - but I've got a special something to reward you for your personal efforts. Be sure to do your best! Tee hee hee!

I'll keep track of your efforts! Donate enough balloons, and I'll have a surprise for you! To donate balloons, first open the event tab at your Mayor's House. Secondly, select the balloon resource, click on donate and select an amount. That's it!
Gather more balloons to get more rewards. Simple, isn't it?
Why do we need so many balloons? Have you ever heard someone say "Hey, I think we have enough balloons here?" Of course not! You can never have enough balloons!
If you bring me this many balloons, I'll give you a special reward, fresh from my own collection. Tee hee hee, there's no way you'll manage that, though!
Why am I even promising a reward for so many balloons? It's got to be impossible to gather that many! Consider it your very own carrot on a stick! Ha ha ha!

Whoah, slow down, champ - I'm starting to run out of rewards for you now, ha ha... Afraid I'm all out of the big prizes - but please do keep helping to make our festival as great as possible! If you donate more than the target of 1,000 balloons, they'll still count towards the community goal, but I won't be able to count them towards your next round of 1,000 balloons. Why? Ah, don't worry about the technical details - this event is all about the fun, you know!

Everyone must work together to make this as awesome a celebration as possible! We'll be counting balloon donations from all around the world, and will keep updating the numbers every few minutes.
As a special incentive, everyone will receive a special reward if you can meet the objective below before the week is out. There'll be another reward next week, too - so stay tuned!

So, you're all going to cooperate, and keep donating to make this festival the biggest, brightest, and bestest festival ever, yes? Just like last week, all world-wide balloon donations will be tracked below. I'll be sure to update the running total every few minutes! Aren't I the best?
You know the drill. Reach the target in just one week, and everyone will get their reward!

A fisher reports that they found a really interesting message in a bottle. Apparently, it's come from a town under attack by an army of small, but numerous golems! The sea's currents give us a rough idea of the island's potential location, but our maps show nothing there... We'll have to explore the waters if we want to come to their aid.
The distress call was worded with great urgency. I advise you make haste, and send over your troops as soon as you can.

Something terrible is happening on the small island you helped earlier! Yes, the golems are gone, but now ferocious beasts are prowling the wilderness! It seems we have yet to root out the cause of the evil there.
We've finally gotten word from your scientist friend! Let's visit him right away. The townsfolk are depending on you!
This season always brings out all kinds of darkness and evil... A small town on a small island has sent a desperate plea for help. Will you be able to beat the horror back from whence it came?

A horde of small golems emerged from the fog, and attacked the town. This operation should be fairly straight forward. We must deal with the golems, fortify the town against any future waves, and finally investigate and eliminate their source.
The golems have paused their assault to give themselves chance to rest, and are hiding amongst the rubble of the houses they've leveled. This is our chance to strike!
Before we leave town, we must ensure it doesn't get attacked again in our absence. A simple barrier of wood and stone should suffice.

The fog mixes with the darkness, and makes it impossible to see down by the river. Good thing the locals are used to it, and have placed several large braziers along the route. If you make a few torches, we can light the braziers and proceed.

That creepy building must be where the golems are being created. In fact, I can just catch a glimpse of a few through the windows. There's also maniacal laughter coming from inside... Prepare for a fight!

So, the golems weren't the only thing plaguing the island! Now, many a monstrous beast is roaming the land. Whatever, or whoever is behind these terrors, we mustn't leave before we're sure we've gotten to the root of all this!

The scientist who created the golems just confirmed my suspicions - the island's lord must be behind all this! Not only did he lie about making sure the golems wouldn't cause trouble, but the magic influencing the beasts is originating from his castle! We'll have to fight our way up the mountain!
I've been scouting ahead, and can confirm there are more beasts heading our way. The good news is, we're halfway up the mountain now. Pull yourself together, and we can make it!
Time to talk to that so called "lord". I'm sure you've got a question or two for him. Fancy leading the way?

Alright - we're back on the island to finish what we've started. The scientist has found a method that'll let us break that mysterious barrier. Let's follow his plan, so we can confront that "lord" in the name of his charges.

The scientist has researched the invisible barrier, and I'm afraid it really does appear to be magic. However, that doesn't mean it doesn't have a weakness. In order to keep the barrier up, it needs to be channeled non-stop - and we've pinpointed the location of the casters.
Witches are hiding in three towers on this island. If we take them all out, the barrier will disappear.

Oh, I see how it is! Now he's taunting us to come inside and face him, boasting about his evildoings! It's a bit unsettling how his voice seems to echo from all the castle's windows, but I can't wait to beat some sense into this arrogant monster!
The gates are still barricaded through mundane means, but it's nothing a battering ram can't handle.
I feel great unease when I think of our experience on that island... Being prepared for the worst would put my mind at rest.
The scientist is doing everything he can to find a way to break the castle's barrier. The only thing we can do right now is put our trust in him, and wait until he's finished.

Whew! That was quite the achievement - and a lot of work, as we'd expect from such powerful nobles. Still, the first hurdles have been overcome - now you can enjoy your first rewards! Just remember - the best ones are yet to come, during the second phase of the event. Be sure to keep donating those balloons, as they'll all count towards the goal for the second phase!
Your settlers are starting to worry about that new mansion you built... They say it's haunted by ghosts! Let's investigate.

A Mayan ship has arrived on our shores! They report the outbreak of an epidemic in their land, and seek our help in getting things under control - and perhaps even curing the infection! We have to help these people!
First, we have to establish a quarantine zone around the ship. Draft some units to build up the quarantine zone.
The first Mayans have arrived. They look so pale and exhausted from the infection. We should treat them as soon as possible.
It will take some time for the treatment to take effect. We can help them feel better faster by providing fresh food for everyone.
Early reports are suggesting that the treated people are feeling better already. However, more Mayans have arrived, and they need our help too.
While treating the infection will help the Mayans, we have to analyze the infection itself, too. We should travel to other lands, and learn what we can about diseases.
More ill Mayans have arrived. These should be the last ones, though. Help them to recover!
The kingdoms around you are impressed by your military achievements. They send a ship to your shores, asking if you could help them improve their own military strength.
A good defence requires a lot of resources to craft powerful weapons for the troops. Sadly, the kingdom is short of exactly those resources. Help them out by building a steady supply.
The first conscripts have arrived. Provide enough Drill Manuals to train them properly.
Training the troops is one side of winning battles, but strategy is every bit as important. Travel to distant lands, and teach the troops some new strategies for the battles ahead.
The training continues, and more conscripts have arrived at your shores awaiting training.
A proper graduation ceremony will boost the moral of troops by acknowledging their achievements in training. Provide some troops to guard the ceremony.
These should be the last conscripts. Once they're trained, the kingdom should be able to defend itself fully.
There are several new towns being build in distant lands. The mayor of one of these towns asks you to help him build a nice settlement closer to your own.
The first step is to get some inspiration from the architecture of as many different cultures as possible. Travel to distant lands, and soak up the inspiration.
Construction is hungry work, and construction workers need plenty of food to do their job properly. Provide provisions to the workers who arrived at your shores.
We should provide troops to help secure the construction sites in these new towns, to keep them safe from thieves.
More workers have arrived! Provide provisions to them to keep them healthy and strong.
Last but not least, there won't be any buildings without building materials. The mayor asks if you could help them out with some resources!
I just received word that the last batch of construction workers will be here any minute. Help them out with provisions.
One of our allies has been in touch. While preparing land for some new buildings, they found an ancient buried structure. This structure is huge, and they'd appreciate our help in excavating it!
Before we start the excavation, we should properly prepare. Provide some paper to take notes, and draw maps of the site.
Our archaeologists need tools, too! Craft some tools and provide them to the archaeologists.
Your archaeologists have arrived at the site. They say they simply don't have the manpower to both excavate the site, and keep it secure. Can we provide some volunteer troops?
More of our archaeologists are preparing to travel to the excavation site. We should equip them with some tools!
The ancient knowledge we're discovering is amazing. These excavation sites tell us so much about the past. Let's try to find even more of them around the world.
The last group of archaeologists is preparing to travel - but they won't be able to help at the site without any tools.

Your archaeologists have arrived at the site. They say they simply don't have the manpower to both excavate the site, and keep it secure. Can we provide some volunteer troops?
More of our archaeologists are preparing to travel to the excavation site. We should equip them with some tools!
The ancient knowledge we're discovering is amazing. These excavation sites tell us so much about the past. Let's try to find even more of them around the world.
The last group of archaeologists is preparing to travel - but they won't be able to help at the site without any tools.

A Mayan ship has arrived on our shores! They report the outbreak of an epidemic in their land, and seek our help in getting things under control. We must try and help these people, and cure the infection!
First, we have to establish a quarantine zone around the ship. Draft some units to build up the quarantine zone, and help keep it safe.
The first Mayans have arrived. They look so pale and exhausted from the infection. We should treat them as soon as possible.
It will take some time for the treatment to take effect. We can help them feel better faster by providing enough fresh food to go round.
Early reports suggest that the people we've treated are feeling better already. However, more Mayans have arrived, and they need our help too.
While treating the infection will help the Mayans, we have to analyze the infection itself, too. We should travel to other lands, and learn what we can about diseases.
More ill Mayans have arrived! These should be the last ones, though. Help them to recover!
The kingdoms around you are impressed with your military achievements. They send a ship to your shores, asking if you could help them improve their own military strength.
A good defence requires a lot of resources to craft powerful weapons for your troops. Sadly, the kingdom is short of exactly the resources they require. Help them out by building a steady supply.
The first conscripts have arrived. Provide enough Drill Manuals to train them properly.
Training your troops is one side of winning battles, but strategy is every bit as important. Travel to distant lands, and teach the troops some new strategies for the battles ahead.
The training continues, and more conscripts have arrived on your shores awaiting training.
A proper graduation ceremony will boost the morale of troops, by acknowledging their achievements in training. Provide some troops to keep the ceremony safe.
These should be the last conscripts. Once they're trained, the kingdom should be able to fully defend itself.
There are several new towns being built in distant lands. The mayor of one of these towns has asked you to help him build a nice settlement, a little bit closer to your own.
The first step is to get some inspiration from the architecture of as many different cultures as possible. Travel to distant lands, and soak up the inspiration.
Construction is hungry work, and construction workers need plenty of food to do their job properly. Provide provisions to the workers who arrived on your shores.
We should provide troops to help secure the construction sites in these new towns, and keep them safe from thieves.
More workers have arrived! Provide provisions to keep them healthy and strong.
Last but not least, there obviously won't be any buildings without building materials. The mayor asks if you could help them out with some resources!
I just received word that the last batch of construction workers will be here any minute. Help them out with provisions.

The type of Christmas tree you just placed is really special. No-one really knows how or why it happens, but once a week, a new gift appears under each Gift Christmas Tree! Get your gift(s) by selecting a Gift Christmas Tree when the gift icon is hovering above it.
