Oh, hey cutie! I've been on this island for years now, but I don't think we've met? My name's Flora. I'm the one who's been growing, cutting and arranging those lovely flowerbeds all over town. I've actually got a pretty big request for you - hope you're not the type to immediately roll your eyes when you hear stories about love and romance!
I'm here to open my heart to you. My sweetheart fights in your army. They have yet to return from their last mission, but I have no reason to believe they didn't make it. Truth is, my love tends to have a bit of a hazy memory. Sometimes, they even forget how to get back home. I love them very much... but now, just before Valentine´s Day, I fear they might not find their way back in time. Usually, my precious carries a love letter doused with the scent of my flowers, which usually jump-starts their memory... However, I fear it might have been destroyed during battle.
So, would you be willing to be my savior, and help bring my beloved back for Valentine´s Day? My idea is to send flowers across the ocean, so my baby-cakes can smell my flowers again. I´ll talk you through my idea, step by step.
First, let's take a look at how you might be able to help me get my beloved back. Have a flick through the archive, I´ve added some lovely notes there.

To ensure that at least a few flowers reach my love, and their scent can guide my sweet back to me, we need to produce an immense amount of flowers, and send them throughout the world.
If you can, please plant three flower farms on your island, so that the flowers can blossom en masse.

Oh, my dear friend... I´m afraid it won't be enough to only produce one batch of flowers.
The unique scent of my blossoms comes from the manifold mixture of flower seeds, which have been gathered from many different islands and regions around the world. Please, help me gather them, and sow them on your flower farms. I´ll oversee the process, and make sure we create a bloom you can smell for miles.
To help you get started, I've put a pack of flower seeds in your Star Menu. Just apply these on a Flower Farm.

All these beautiful blossoms can be used to produce a wide range of things - but perhaps none as romantic as flower bouquets. Feel free to charm your friends and loved ones with the fruits of your wares, and make your friends' islands overflow with joy and love. As a happy side effect, it'll also help the scent of my flowers spread across thousands of islands, and hopefully, reach my darling´s button nose.
Still, I have yet to hear anything from my love - and none of my darling's comrades or friends could tell me anything, either. Truth be told, I'm really starting to worry now. I know it's still early days, but I just can´t help it. Please, hurry. And let your friends know we need their help too!

It might be far-fetched, but I´d like to ask you another favor - even if it is slightly clutching at straws... If a flower´s fragrance can't cross the oceans intact, perhaps my words of love will. I have a few old love letters my sweetheart and I sent each other. Perhaps sending parts of these oaths of love around will get through to my dearest.
Even if it doesn't, sharing the love should boost the growth of flowers on your friends islands as well, as my flowers are fertilized by love. Don´t laugh!

Please, don't give up! Carry on spreading the love as much as you can, so that my love can come back to me! I believe in you! And of course, your effort will be rewarded...
I can just see it now. When my love comes back, I will jump into their arms, kiss and cuddle them, and never let go.

Hey, you! I'm sorry, my dear - I'm afraid I don´t have much time. First, we need to make sure you have enough influence to be able to help me.
Please, come visit me as soon as possible, when you've been able to expand your reach.

Hello, my dear! My, that certainly is a beautiful love garden. It makes me so happy to see such a lovely place in your town. I want to see this garden full of people, sharing their passion and love with each other. The smell of flowers filling their minds, and the beauty of love inside their hearts. Here - I brought some new flowers! How about we plant them and wait a little longer until some people arrive?

Hey, boss. Happy to see me? Do you have a minute, 'cause I kind of need your help. One of your soldiers said he lost a drill plan on one of the islands he was traveling to. He says he'd rather like to have it back - mumbled something about speeding up the training to get back home to his loved ones sooner. You know I'm always up for an adventure, right? So, when do we set sail?
Oh, good to see you! I got another request from one of our bowmen. Time for another adventure. This one shouldn't be that dangerous - maybe a little boring, if you ask me.

Good day to you! I always love taking a stroll in the garden - the smell of the flowers helps me relax and think a little bit clearer. In fact, I'm glad I met you, as I have a little a request. I've had a bit of a tip off about some important data - apparently, it might help us train your troops faster. I've also got an idea where we can find this data. Can you meet me at the Excelsior? Prepare for a venture!

Good to see you again, boss. My scouts got some reports about some trouble brewing. This one's a bit worrying, so I'd suggest you take some of your friends with you. Wouldn't worry too much though - you still have me on your side, so we should be fine.

You seem to visit this garden quite a lot? I'm not here to complain, though - actually, I have another request. The last report mentioned a rather small issue - some rascals thinking they can terrorize honest people. How about we teach them a lesson?

Phew! I knew I'd find you here in the garden. Listen - I have an urgent matter for you to attend to. One of our scouts has gone missing, and her husband is asking if we can help out. We know where she was sent last, but she has yet to return. Can you please send out one of your specialists to look for her?

I need your help. A friend of mine is drawing a map of some of the islands around us, but he needs a bit of information first. Can you send your explorers out to scout those islands, and find the information he needs?
Your explorer's reported some... disturbing things about a mysterious island. We should send them out again to get as much information as we can. I just want to make sure there are no surprises.

This is quite a special place... How did you manage to get all the people in here? Actually, never mind - I was just hoping you could give me a bit of a hand? A settler wants to impress his loved one with something special from a foreign land, but he's afraid to travel alone. Can you send one of your specialists out to accompany him on his travels?

Huh!? Oh, you caught me by surprise - I was just finalizing my newest creation. What do you think? Actually, I'm glad you're here. I need some more stone for my next project - but not just any stone. I need a special one. Can you help me out, and send one of your geologists to find it?

Imagine meeting you in the garden again! Do you come here often? Actually, I'm glad I bumped into you, as I could use your help... One of my friends wants impress their lover by crafting a special gift out of bronze. It has to be a special alloy - and to craft it, we need some rather pure copper ore. Can you send out a geologist to look for it?

Ohh, it's you! Well, I'm almost done with my new project - but it does feel kind of like it's missing something... A little unique touch, perhaps... Ah, I know! It need some marble! Yes, a nice flash of marble - but not just any marble will suffice. Only the finest will do. Luckily, I know exactly where to find some that fits the bill. Can one of your geologists help me out?

Hmm... I've been thinking. How about we put a fence around this garden? I've been experimenting with a new alloy - it could be just the thing we need. All I need is a special strain of iron. I can tell your geologists exactly where to search for it.
Have you ever heard of graphite? That's one sturdy piece of crystal! I need some for my experiments - your geologists should know where to find it, right?

A friend of mine says he's found a way to make gold out of iron. I want to put it to the test. Can you help me find some of the purest gold around, so I can compare it to the stuff he produces? I've already told your geologists where to search.

Oh, hello! It's a pleasure to meet you again. Have you ever looked at the streets in the park and thought "they could really use some bohus granite"? Well, I have - it's a special form of granite only available in the tundra regions. As a matter of fact, I was talking to your geologists about this granite the other day. They were keen to bring me some samples. If you could give them a nudge, I could use that granite to turn those streets into something special.

Oh man, my hammer just broke! That was a special one made out of titanium, too! Now I've to build a new one... Can you help me out? Your geologists should know where to find the best titanium around, and I need some of it for my hammer.

Saltpeter is so fascinating. There are so many different types of it - and I have to study and analyse them all. Can you help me find some of it? Here's a quick map I made - it'll show your geologists where to look.

Such lovely architecture... I always come here to relax when I'm not teaching my students. Actually, I bumped into one of them earlier. He was heartbroken - his girlfriend lost a necklace when they were traveling. He knows where it happened, but he can't find a way to go and get it back on his own. Could you send one of your explorers to find it for him?

Ohh... Er, just give me a second. Right, OK. As luck would have it, I've just heard about some interesting treasure - it sounds like it's definitely worth investigating. I've marked it on this map for the explorers. Could you take care of it for me?

We need an explorer, and fast! A settler's gone missing! We know his last location, since he was searching for treasure... Our explorers know the lay of the land better than anyone - can you send them out to search? I hope nothing bad's happened...

You know, this garden could really use some fancy stuff. As luck would have it, I happen to know just where to find some. Here's an old map my father gave me - it'll show you where to look. An explorer should be able to find it, no problem. Good luck!

Well, this is a pretty big request... One of your soldiers lost his sword during his last battle. The sword is an heirloom and his lucky charm. He lost it in the desert, but he can't leave his post to go looking for it. Can you help him and bring his sword back?
Oh, it's you again. OK - let's get to it! You've done a great job so far, so now it's up to us to make our preparations. Please come back later, and we'll decide how to progress.

Wondering when you'll be able to find the next gift under your Gift Christmas Tree? Don't worry - I've got it covered. Here you can see when the next gift will appear. The timer will restart after you grab your current gift.

I've sent a scout as a messenger to the city up north. They confirmed the call for help came from them. They told a story of a strange power that draws all kinds of evildoers to their city all year long. And apparently, it gets worse the colder it gets. The attackers are behaving weirdly too. The townspeople usually aren't attacked directly, but nevertheless, they're unable to keep the enemies at bay.
They've requested that we rid their land of evildoers, so they can stock up on resources, share medicine and meet with their loved ones on the other side. They know it will not be long until the next wave of bad guys wash ashore, but it will help them greatly right now.

First, we need to get further inland and close in on both sides of the city.
All this trouble apparently began roughly a decade ago, when a landslide split their city in two. Nowadays, the two halves of the former city have to use boats if they want to get together or share resources. The ground where the landslide occurred is too unstable to cross. They don't want to leave their homes, but now they're on the verge of obliteration, and they need our help to survive.
Defeat the foes on the way to the village, and be prepared for some unusual encounters.

Have you noticed the strange mix of enemies we're encountering? It doesn't look like they have a clear leader who strategically arranges the troops in each camp. It looks like they just... I don't know... like they just banded together on their way to the city. I also don't get why they aren't attacking each other? Thugs and wild animals unite to attack a harmless, impoverished and secluded city without harming the inhabitants? Sure...
Well, at least our task is clear. Defeat the enemies on our way to the city.

People from the continent were left with no choice but to flee, and are now heading for the far away islands of Tavos. Without offering much in the way of specifics, a request went out for Settlers willing to go on adventures to find a new life - and hopefully, a new home. The expenses incurred in shipping settlers over will be covered - and will even be rewarded in gold. But first, some preparations will have to be made.
First, we have to ensure we are able to sustain the growth of our own island and economy. Achieve stability, and we'll be able to continue our endeavor.

Now, let us delegate some settlers to head up this most important of endeavors. A few will have to manage the construction of a suitable site here on our island to keep the process running. Others will need to pave the way and travel ahead to plot a course and eliminate any obstacles. We'll need to wait and see what else has to be taken care of.

The blueprints are ready. Now, we need only a few more resources, and we'll be able to build the key that will unlock many new new domains. With our brand-new harbor, we'll be able to send as many settlers as are willing on their journey to new lands.

With this beauty of a harbor, we'll be able to travel huge distances, and our explorers should be able to find new places to conduct treasure hunts. On top of that, we may even be able to amass riches by supporting our fellow settlers overseas.

Whoo! Whoooo! Helloooooo! We are most grateful to you for placing a Ghost Lantern on your island. Most living beings are afraid of us and think we mean harm. But on the contrary! We are friendly beings, and a crew of adventurers that just cannot give up on this wonderf-whoooo-l world. There's just so much to disc-whooooo-ver. We will not vanish before our thirst for adventure has been quenched! Whooooo-hoo! Our only regret is that nobody ever gave us a home to return to after our ghostly adventures, leaving us to simply wander around helplessly. So please, build as many ghost lanterns on your island as po-whoooo-ssible, so we'll be able to return. We will reward you for every lantern with one mo-whoooooo-re item in a ghostly reward box. We'll give you one box every week. On top of that, we'll provide you with tidings on how you can get your hands on some extra rewards if you fulfill a certain task once a week. But only if you fulfilled the last task we gave you. We're not genies, you know? Just check by our Ghost Ship that yo-whoooooo-u'll find on your west coast - I believe it's hard to overl-whoooooo-k.

Here you can see how long we'll be at sea, whooooo! Bet you can't wait for us to return, huh? We are so glad to have found y-whoooo, and will try our best to reward you with nice things when we return! Don't forget to come by and get your stuff - we won't leave for another adventure until then!
We heard a legend about mini ghosts that live on tiny islands. Doesn't that sound cu-whoooo-te? Help us search for them, and we'll have a small obolus for y-whooooo.

Oh my, oh my... Even 300-year-olds can sometimes bicker like little children. Unbelievab-whooooo-l. Could you show my ghostly sailors how to co-whoooooo-perate? Some don't get along so well only because they were born in different centuries. A small demonstration of co-whoooooo-peration might help with that.

My personal friend, Atlas, with whom I've been travelling the seas for hundreds of years now seems to be more than a little bored. It looks like he needs a change of scenery. Could you take him along on one of your adventures? I'll tell him his task is to watch your every move for anything suspicious - he might enjoy a bit of an espionage mission. It doesn't matter much where you take him, just make sure he gets some fresh air.

The crew needs a challenge. Would you be able to find us a s-whooooo-itable playground to rattle our sabers?
Don't overdo it though - just a minor scuffle will do this time. And please, make sure the fo-whooooo-es are bad guys - you know we're still kind-hearted ghosts, right?

We stumbled upon an old notebook, written in the last days of a wintry, forsaken mother. She wished to experience some mysteries, some adventure, riddles or incredible stories after having spent her life raising a horde of children. But it should be an adventure without violence - that was noted specifically. It looks like the mother never got the chance to leave on such an adventure. Will you go in her stead and takes the notes with you, so her soul may find serenity?

A young man holding a baby in his arms was kneeling and sobbing at the shore. He asked the heavens if they couldn't return his wife and the child's mother. The baby had just started talking, and the first thing it apparently said was "Momma?", in a quiet and sad voice. The atmosphere on board hasn't been the same ever since... But now we've got a new goal. We will find out what happened to the mother! If you can, please keep a look out for her too.

The ship's company is eager for some brawls, and wants to scare some ruffians. They've witnessed some cruel injustices lately, and couldn't do anything about it, so they want to at least hinder the other evildoers from being able to do anything similar. Can you recommend a few places?

One of my ghost crew found a map stuck between the walls of an old manor. Two spots are marked, and although the outlines of the island aren't visible anymore, it surely isn't the same one we found it on. Here take a lo-whooo-ok - maybe you'll recognize the mountains and the forest marked on the map. Maybe you'll find something good there. Will you share it with us?

I've got a riddle for you! If you can't solve it, I'll have you run some errands for me as a forfeit. Deal? OK, here goes! What has 2 wings but cannot fly? 3... 2... 1... Time's up! If you still don't know when you return, I might tell you the answer.

Listen lad, or gal, or, well, I can't see you too clearly without any eyes, so just listen, okay? You need friends. Good friends. And you never know where you might find them. So go and tell someone that you're on "A Quest for Friendship", and ask for their help, OK? And maybe don't just keep asking the same person - that'll get you nowhere. Just say a friendly ghost gave you the push you needed, hee-hee, whooooo!

It's a bit embarrassing to ask, but... could you get us some ballast for our ship? The problem is, we're a bit too friendly, see, and so we're constantly being pulled upwards...We even keep stones in our pockets so we don't fly off before we want to. But our ship needs some additional ballast so as not to fly off. And unfortunately, every now and then a few bricks just drop straight through the ghostly hull of our ship, so we regularly have to restock our ballast. We haven't found any in a while, so if you stumble upon anything that might do the trick, please let me know!
Since we're all such good friends by now, could you do us a favor? We desperately need some wild horses that aren't afraid of ghosts! Please find us some!

A little while back, our ship passed a crisis-ridden island with a town near the coast. It looked like the town had been split in two by a landslide, so we got curious. But unfortunately, we couldn't get as near as we wanted, as wild beasts and foes with strength we'd never seen before were roaming all about. They were wandering around just like lost ghosts. Despite all this, we found a small family hiding out in some ruins near the coast. They told us the story of the island, and how they'd always just about managed to keep going - somehow. But during the winters, it becomes incredibly hard to survive, especially due to the cold. If they take shelter, the beasts will leave them alone, but their stock of coal always runs out too soon, putting them in a dire situation. Would you mind gathering some flammable material?

Whooooo-hoo again! Ever since we settled on your island, we've been able to enjoy many more adventures than before. Unfortunately, this has also made our ghostly weapons dull faster than we expected. Could you get us some iron to resharpen them? We don't actually use the iron ore itself, but we learned how to extract the essence of it and instill it into our weapons, repairing and even strengthening them! During the process, the iron ore does get destroyed nonetheless, though, so I guess you could say we are u-whoooo-sing it up.

Whooooo! During our travels, we've encountered many settlers in p-whoo-or shape! They seem to be have been kidnapped, or got themselves trapped and forced to work for their captors and such. We've made a list of places on the islands we found so you can free them! I wouldn't wait too long, though - some of them really seem close to popping their cloggs.

We've noticed your fishing efforts are driving away the fish swarms! We can gladly help you with that by creating an artificial coral reef for our friends with fins! We love a good colorful reef ourselves, so you only need to provide us with enough material to create the reef. Be sure to bring us the right material though - not every ordinary brick or stone will do. Here's a detailed description how it should look.

Whoooo-hooooo, wow! You should have seen that kraken! It must have been twice the size of our ship, the Flying Ghostman - and it almost managed to send us all to the end of time! I'm still not sure how it actually managed to touch us, but it must have been around for longer than even we've been roaming the seas - and it's clearly picked up plenty of skills along the way! We didn't want to hurt the majestic beastie, so we managed to slip out of its tentacles but for a prize. Unfortunately, that means part of the ship has evaporated into thin air, and a giant hole in the side of our vessel hasn't exactly been helping the crew's morale. Could you please make us this special kind of tool? I know they're pretty archaic, but that's all we know how to use. It won't cost any more than your usual tools - and you can keep them afterwards.

Brrrr-whooooo. While travelling the abyss by foot, we managed to get caught in a ghost lake! Nothing too serious after all, but we're still all dripping wet and we need to dry out! I know it sounds silly, but believe me, a ghost-cold is no fun at all, as it can easily last for a decade - and a constantly sneezing ghost will eventually drive everyone nuts! Please produce some more coal to fire up your smelters a bit more! And don't worry, we won't scare anyone! We'll just hang out on a clothesline nearby for a while.

Quick! We need your help! A band of wandering ghosts have apparently got envious of our ability to freely roam the seas, and they're threatening to banish us! They've figured out a way to wield iron weaponry without injuring themselves, and now they're coming for us! Here are the instructions for what we need you to do to give us chance to defend ourselves. Please hurry - we don't know when they'll be able to reach us!

Help! Help! Whoooo-heeelp! We've been attacked by the most vicious, evil and cruel beings I've ever seen in my entire life - and my entire death! These beasts are relentless. They've been following us for days now, and they just won't stop pecking and quacking. Their number two even gets stuck on our railings! And no-whooooooo, I don't know how this is possible. But what's worse, I don't know how to remove it ! We need something to distract these enormous ducks! We can't simply blast, them can we?

This time, we've come to ask a favor for someone else. It's for another small village, to tell the truth. Their village gets flooded almost every year, destroying what they build up and taking their dreams away with every wave. They have the materials, but what they're lacking is strong men to build up the flood barrier. Could you spare any?

A duke from the continent is arranging a battue to please the noblemen, but it seems he's missing the riders he needs to properly carry it out. This would be a good chance for you to either gain some more respect with the duke - or, go with what we prefer, and sabotage the battue to spare those cute foxes and deers. It's up to you what you want to tell your men, though - we've just come to let you know about the opportunity. If you're up for it, train some riders so they know how to behave in such a no-whooooo-ble event.

Settlers in the north-east of your island seem to be caught in a drought and could really use some rain. We want to repay you for all you've done for us, and we want to help improve the life of your people too. Here's a recipe for some arrows that'll make it rain - but if you want the rain without creating a thunderstorm, you'll have to do it bit by bit, and will need quite a few specially trained bowmen to fulfill this daily task. It's up to you if you want to follow our suggestion thr-whooooooo-h.

We've noticed your folk seems to be somewhat lacking in entertainment options - except for the tavern, that is! Even if that isn't exactly the healthiest of ways to spend their leisure time. Still, although it may not be our place to judge, we've come up with a proposal. We recently saw an incredible show made up of just some simple bowmen. They were shooting flaming arrows at each other in curves, catching them in mid-air, and even playing theater while shooting arrows left and right. I think you could put something like this on too? I'll tell your men how to go about it.

Your tradesmen seem to be moaning behind your back. One of my crew overheard a discussion between them, saying that it's careless that your brew deliveries around the town aren't protected at all. Almost daily, a group of thirsty thieves comes out of the bushes and one of the deliveries vanishes! The deliverers have even stopped reporting the incidents, as it's just become the daily routine. Train some soldiers to escort the deliveries to solve the conflicts peacefully, if possible. Just having troops assigned should improve the situation - and your standing with the tradesmen.

Even we need some time to relax every now and then. But as we seem to scare your Settlers every time we try - even though they've seen us often enough by now - we'd like to find somewhere we can get some rest, without being flustered by stuttered screams every few minutes. Could you keep an eye out for a remote location for us? Preferably it'll have a beach and some palm trees - but as we don't feel any wind or cold, any quiet and remote location would d-whoooo.

Seeing how rough these lands are gives me the shivers. How are people still living here, and why are they so reluctant to leave? According to the scout that just returned, we cannot simply evacuate the residents. They are scattered around the land, from the coast in the south to the natural caves of the north. The people have built winter shelters to retreat to when the weather turns cold. Meanwhile, the elderly simply refuse to leave the home they've lived in for generations. Unfortunately, their children and grandchildren cannot bring themselves to leave them behind, so they are stuck, trying to survive as best they can. As futile as it may seem, we have to free the town again from the invaders. But it won't be as easy as last time. The scout was terrified upon her return - she barely made it back alive. She was chased by furry beasts, but could not describe them any further, as she was running for her life.

Let's get to it. We'll go about this in much the same way as last time. It seems the land hasn't changed all that much since last we were here. Apparently, there are many underground caves and waterways which the people use for hiding. But not all of them are safe. In some, the evil creatures roam like moths to the flame, while others stay completely untouched. But what's the difference? Again, the closer to the town you go, the more concentrated the evil becomes. I will have to investigate this situation thoroughly once the area has been cleared.

Our enemies are, once again, seemingly randomly cobbled together. They don't seem to know what it is they are looking for. They just push relentlessly towards the city, as if infected by some kind of disease. But why aren't we affected as well? Or... maybe... are we affected too? I mean, we are also pushing towards the city. And yes, we have a goal, but... is there something more to it? Or is the reason these bandits go berserk coming from somewhere else? Hmm... There are apes hailing from far-away jungles. There are bandits from the desert that usually stay outside of the city, but when they get close enough, they are drawn here. And also Vikings? What is the connection between them? This is driving me crazy. Ohh... I have to calm down... Excuse me...
Explore the cave and defeat all the enemies!

Oh my, that really was a long journey! I don't think I've ever traveled so far by ship! Maybe not even with the Excelsior... Good thing we have a proper harbor now, though, else this would all have been a lot more troublesome...
Hmm. This land looks somehow familiar, but it feels very different... Like there's some kind of dread in the air... Oh well, it's probably just my imagination. Let's climb this big tree here and use it as a lookout post to check our bearings.

OK! First, we need to rid the village of the immediate threat, and then fight our way through to the Mayor's House. If this really is Laeylorn, the people here should be able to help us find out what happened to Kaedric. Defeat the bandits in the town area!

Let's take a look around town and see who lives here - or perhaps, who lived here, rather? It does seem awfully quiet.
Visiting the Mayor's House would seem to be the most promising approach, seeing as everyone else just slams their doors or runs away as soon as they see us...

Welcome to our beautiful country! At least, what's left of it. I am the acting mayor of what remains of our once prosperous town. You can call me Ferri. You didn't beat those thieves and thugs just to steal what precious few riches we have left, did you?
So, what can I do you for? Ah, I see. So you're looking for a specific person? Though I'm thankful for your help just now, I'm afraid we do have other priorities to take care of at the minute, so I'm afraid we can't be of much use.
Although, if you could help me with some, er... tasks, perhaps we could come to some sort of agreement? Come with me, and I'll explain all.

We desperately need to rebuild the essential buildings on this island. But before we can do that... well, while there's all the residence ruins around the village, no-one will be able to focus on their work. That's because... I almost don't dare to say it... but let's just say, there may have to be some burials performed in parallel... Would you please take this burden upon yourself, to remove the ruins and rebuild the residences? Please! I can't bear asking the other villagers to do so. They've been through enough.

Do you think you could build us some cemeteries, too, please? Our lost friends deserve a fitting final place of rest. Although the years have strengthened my heart, even I would have a hard time burying our friends... The last attacks were particularly devastating. The invaders were simply trying to blow the town up, it seems. Well, you can see the results for yourself. Not to mention, someone very special to me was among the victims... I simply cannot bring myself to do it.

There's still a lot that's left to be done, but for now... could I ask you to leave, and give us some space to mourn? We should be safe for some time, but we really need a bit of time to ourselves. Without invaders... or visitors.
But don't wait too long to come back - we don't know how long it might take for the next enemies to find their way to our island! I'll tell you more later.

Thanks for staying true to your word. As you can see, we are in dire need of your help. Had I anticipated this, I wouldn't have sent you home in the first place... Turns out some bandits had been hiding in the forest south of the village all along.
A group of children were playing in the woods when they saw a handful of them scouting the village. They were talking in such a way that we believe they will ambush the village later tonight. Please, help us! Quick!

A villager just ran into the Main Hall screaming something about a bunch of wild animals marching towards the town from the north. They must have come from the nearby forest. Most likely they're looking for food, as the winter isn't too far away...

That damned pirate... We met a few years back, and he swore he'd get his revenge. It seems now is the time. I guess his pland is to send wave after wave of pirates - and any other creatures they've gathered along the way - at us, just to deal as much damage as possible, before he even dares set foot on the island. Please, I beg you, protect us! If it were just some random bandits we could stand our ground, but we don't stand a chance against trained pirates with such bloodlust in their eyes!
Another pirate attack! Defeat them and protect the village! We're at least kind of your brothers and sisters by now, aren't we?

To bring the constant pirate attacks to a halt, I think we'll need to rebuild the barricades around our village. Being so unprotected seems to make us too easy a target for those pirates. With a proper blockade, we should be able to fend them off for good.

You've already helped us a lot, and I am personally going to see that you get any information we have about that missing person you're looking for. But on top of that, I have an even better proposal I was hoping to put to you...
Even though we don't have much in the way of riches right now, decades ago, when I was a still a small child, Laeylorn was a prosperous city, and one that was famous the world over. Laeylorn was originally just the name of the city, and only later became the name of the island too. That's how big Laeylorn once was. It's a bit confusing, I know, but there is a good reason for it. Only after the town started to shrink, and people began fleeing the island... Oh, I'm getting ahead of myself.
So, my proposal is about twinning our villages, and fraternizing our islands. Your big city, and our tiny village. If we were to do this, I'm sure that Laeylorn, over time, can become as big and as beautiful as it was a century ago. We'll share knowledge and resources. We can also provide you with some of the lost knowledge and wisdom we dig up from Laeylorn, and reward you greatly for all your help. We do still have some treasures left hidden away in our secret caves... I'm getting ahead of myself again, aren't I? So, will you partner up with us?
Excellent! I think a partnering gift would be in order! I'll do my best to provide one from the things we still have, and hope to be able to compensate you further in future. But, as you can probably see, we don't exactly have all that much at the moment... In return, it would be nice if you could provide us with some basic defense troops, so we aren't constantly being hindered in our reconstruction plans. It'd need to be a pretty sizeable force, though, as I'm afraid a small one would only suffice to fend off wildlife and uncoordinated bandits... For the bigger attacks, I- ahem, I think I'm getting ahead of myself. Come visit me when the troops have arrived.

I cannot express how deeply thankful I- no, we ALL are - for you sending across these reinforcements. Now we have these troops protecting us, the pirates will have a much harder job should they attempt to ransack our reconstruction efforts again. However, overall, our defenses are still lacking. Still, first things first. Our food stocks are almost empty, and the people are starving!
Our food reserves have been shrinking faster than we can restock them, but relying on supplies being sent in all the time is too risky, especially in the long-term. Please, help us rebuild a few fields at the edge of the village. This should be far more practical.

It's time to clean this place up! Having those ruins everywhere is getting a bit depressing. Please, get rid of them. That should improve the mood of the people, and will also give us more space to expand the town.

It's time to bare our teeth to any pirate bandits out there! Lets erect some cannon towers to defend ourselves, and hopefully scare them away! They should know that their strength isn't enough to deal with such power!
I hope they give up soon... I guess we'll just have to show them that their efforts are futile, and banish them from Laeylorn!
Don't forget - I'll call for you when another attack is imminent, so you don't have to spend all your time here.

Let's ask around - maybe the villagers know something? Someone ought to have seen Kaedric... He's not a person you could easily forget or overlook. He may have gotten a bit older, but he still has quite the outrageous personality. There's a reason why we haven't become the best of friends...
Look around the village, and see if you can find any hints about Kaedric's visit here.

I have some big favors to ask... But they will bring us new quests and adventures!
I have a feeling this might become the most difficult endeavor we have ever embarked upon...

An old acquaintance of mine asked us to come see him in the tavern, which is very unusual. Normally, he'd just visit me at the Excelsior. This time, he even sent the invite using a stranger as a messenger, instead of just posting a letter or dropping by himself. Of course, I'm curious to hear what he has to say. Let me know when you're ready, and we'll head over.

OK... This isn't funny. Where is he? And why did he leave such a strange message with the barman?
"Need help. Laeylorn. Don't tell anyone. Life and Death!"
Do you know any Laeylorn? Is it a person, or something? Hmm... I guess it might be a place, but if it is, I've never heard of it... This time, I have to ask a personal favor. The acquaintance I talked about is Kaedric, my former mentor in the Explorers' Guild. Although we don't like each other personally, we've always respected each other for our skills, and tried to keep in contact. He helped me out during several adventures with the Excelsior, and I returned the favor. I wonder what kind of mess that old grumbler's got himself into this time?
I guess we'll have to cast the net wide if we want to find out more about this "Laaeeyyloorrnn".

We're going to need a huge amount of materials and provisions if we're going to make it to Laeylorn. There's a chance we might need slightly less once we've finalized the route and all, but for now, let's be better safe than sorry.
Let's start by building several ships to take us there. I don't want place an unnecessary toll on our settlers, so please be sure to not take any resources from our reserves, OK?

Please prepare some additional defenses to guard the island. We want to be sure we avoid any... unpleasant issues while we're travelling. A mixed group of units should improve the island's security sufficiently. We'll order them to patrol the island.

I know I'm asking a lot of you, but this journey might end up being longer than we anticipate - and I really don't want to see any starving sailors. Just don't forget to cure the meat!
Good thing we finally have a proper harbor. Without it, this whole undertaking would be impossible. We'd never manage to load all these ships!

Let's check that everything is in order here before we travel. Give the logistics and appearance of our beloved home a quick once-over. There might be a few things we should improve before we set out!

Here's a short list of extra resources this endeavor will require. Tools, obviously, to repair anything that breaks once we're under way.
Coins, in case we have to trade for more provisions. Horses, to make travel on land much easier in case we have to go cross-country. Hmm... Are we forgetting anything?
OK! Let's put ourselves to the test, and see if we've remembered everything we need. Treat it as a final rehearsal.

I talked to several of our specialists, and made them our official advisers for this adventure. They came up with a whole list of other items they thought we'd require. Well, needless to say, I declined our generals' request to bring along a bunch of spare weapons - we're not setting out to fight a war! But, well, some requests seem reasonable enough.
Coal to keep us warm; water in case we can't find sufficient freshwater springs along the way; sausages, as they take a while to go off; and paper, which apparently has tons of uses I'd never thought of, from taking notes to drawing maps, up to handing out information to anyone we meet, or even sending messages. I hope that's the last of the preparations though - I just want to head out! Right now! *sigh*

We should make sure our production chains are all in optimal condition, just in case we need to replenish our supplies in a hurry. It wouldn't hurt to pay our friends a visit, too. We might need to ask for their help.
Oh, and make sure our miners don't run out of work until we return!

Our advisers have insisted on some more stuff. On the plus side, they did promise that this would be their final set of recommendations.
If we pack what they've suggested to keep the crews healthy and well entertained, it can't hurt, can it? We do want to avoid a mutiny midway through, after all... Oh, and just in case - to ensure we don't get destroyed by a thunderstorm, your specialists want to install some earthing wires. Although I don't understand how that'll work if we're on water...

Let's prepare a few support points on the way towards Laeylorn. You can choose where to set them up. It can't hurt to have a few extra provisions and some additional troops prepared in case we need reinforcements, get chased by foes, or suffer a shipwreck and get washed ashore!

For today, let us take counsel with our pillows and then head out no later then tomorrow. I don't really want to delay things for another night either, but in the end, I agree with our advisers. It's better not to rush into anything just now. Have a good night's rest, and see you tomorrow at the harbor as early as the birds!

Without further ado, let's get started! Oh, wait! I almost forgot! I had a dream last night about running away from some unidentifiable beast - but no matter how hard I tried, I just couldn't get away. So, it got me thinking... Let's produce some horseshoes for our trip, just in case it was a vision, and we find ourselves having to make haste. I also have the feeling we may need to upgrade some of our military equipment. Just trust me on this - I almost never ask favors based on my gut, but this one isn't going to let me rest...

OK, this is important! Ferri asked us to grant his people some time to mourn their lost ones. But we should be doing this more in general. Taking a break, I mean. Let's be sure we take a little time off every now and then, OK?
I just want to be sure you're aware, we can return any time we want . Our progress on Laeylorn will be kept, as long as we fully complete any tasks before we leave. If we abort a mission part-way through, any efforts we made will probably be for naught. After aborting, or in other words, deferring the adventure, you'll be sent a mail. This way you can always go back to Laeylorn, almost like magic.

We need to send some basic defense troops over to Laeylorn, so they aren't wiped while we're not there. But first, we need some volunteers!
This will be the first act of twinning our two towns, bringing some hope to the people of Laeylorn... at the cost of some resources of ours.

OK! Now that we've trained the volunteers, we just need to wait for them to arrive on Laeylorn. Ugh, how I hate all this waiting. Be sure to return to Laeylorn afterwards, and check everything's all in order over there. Are you getting used to all these voyages over seas now? It seems every time we go, something new happens. Remember the time that big thing attacked us? Oh wow, that was something, hahaha...

We received notice that someone snuck into the food reserves on Laeylorn and stole more than half of it. The people on Laeylorn didn't have many supplies left anyway... And we need to provide our troops over there with sufficient supplies too!
We should send some guides to teach the people how to build temporary shelters, so those who are still hiding outside the village at least don't freeze to death or catch and spread diseases. With everything that gets consumed, lost or rots on the long journey to Laeylorn, there are always huge amounts we have to send. And then you've got to plan for the return trip - or do you want to leave the crews stranded over there?

I haven't heard anything from Kaedric for quite some time... I fear the worst. He would have given us a sign of life if he had the chance. He's not the kind to unnecessarily worry others... We must continue our search!

Let us send out more explorers, and task them with performing an undercover search for my mentor, Kaedric. I hope we can learn more soon... But this time, we have to broaden our search radius, and ask even on the farthest outskirts of our reach.

Kaedric always loved to visit the different mines and excavations on our island, to see if anything unexpected had been dug up. Maybe we don't have to look that far? Perhaps there's something useful a bit closer than we thought!
Ask your specialists to take a look at the deposits Kaedric visited last. Maybe they could find a hint as to where we should continue our search.
Let us travel to Laeylorn again. We have to find a clue as to where to look next. If Ferri cannot help us, we'll have to take matters into our own hands. I cannot wait any longer!

It's strange. Some people looked like they might know something, but then they all send us to the mayor, who just says he's still investigating and doesn't have the time to look into it right now. Something's not right. But after this - let us call it "success" - on Laeylorn, I wonder what we can find if we start asking around right here?

With yours and Ferris' permission, I would like to take a closer look around Laeylorn myself. I know it's risky, but I promise, I'll be careful. Oh yeah, sure - you can come with me! Let's see what we can find!
It's time to show we're serious about twinning our town with Laeylorn for the prosperity of both our islands. It won't be long till our help is direly needed.
I knew they'd come sooner rather than later. That damned pirate leader! If I ever get my hand on him, he will pay for all the misfortune he's brought us!
The pirates are attacking again! Please send troops to defeat them, and chase them off the island.

Some of those mischievous pirates have stolen our most treasured secrets! Please, help us reclaim what's rightfully ours! As partners, you'll give me your word you won't steal them either, right? Those sealed texts will stay sealed?

Send a bigger army to ensure the safety of Laeylorn, and reinforce your bond with us as your partner town. The people of Laeylorn are still under constant threat. Our children haven't slept a night through for months. Put an end to this. It won't keep the island safe forever, but at least it'll provide the village with a breather, and a good foundation for further endeavors.

With all the adventuring and fighting that's been going on recently, you should be sure to help your twin town too! After all, an investment in Laeylorn is an investment in your future too! You should decide between a Saltpeter Mine or a Titanium Mine!
Let me explain. Since we're now able to take care of most of our own basic needs, it feels like it's time to see if we can bring Laeylorn's economy back to its feet. But as space is limited, you'll have to choose what you want to build on Laeylorn carefully, as in turn, it'll determine your payoffs! I can only ship things over to you that you helped us to produce in the first place. So, to get started, you should decide if you'd rather mine for saltpeter, or titanium. You cannot mine both! Once you've prepared the materials, come on over to Laeylorn, find the construction site, and get building! It'll pay off soon!

Whatever's below Laeylorn, it is most definitely scary. We should send resources, weapons and troops to Laeylorn so we can explore this cave. Did Ferri know about this? I'd assume he'd have told us about it if he did? Not sure why he'd want to keep something like this a secret...
At some point, we'll have to build a proper outpost on Laeylorn to decrease the cost of these endeavors. For now, let's stash some equipment over there, so we can restock our troops after battles.
Now that we're fully prepared for this huge endeavor, let's head out. I can't wait to explore that huge cave! What are we going to find there? Is Kaedric down there, waiting for help?

This is the first item on our list, and we shouldn't wait too long to tick it off. Still, it's not too far away, so it shouldn't pose too big a problem. Hopefully, we'll start to better understand what Kaedric was doing, as we follow his steps through this adventure.

Oh, this looks dangerous... The air almost reeks of thievery and death up ahead. Kaedric was only able to investigate all these places thanks to his special abilities. He could be really sneaky if he wanted to... Us, on the other hand? We're just going to have to fight our way through, even if we do scout the area before we head in. It's the only way we'll get to take a closer look at the tracks Kaedric left for us.

It's getting darker and more dangerous with every step we tread following Kaedric's footprints. What did he want here? Maybe he was following someone. That would make sense. Maybe someone from Laeylorn was here?

Seriously, how did Kaedric actually manage to move amongst these cultists without being found out and torn to shreds? His skills must have come a long way since the last time I saw him - which is saying something, considering his age.
Now he's gone off in a completely different direction... Kaedric sure has travelled a lot these past few months. I wonder if he's still on the move, or if he was able to draw some conclusions....

Now, here Kaedric definitely wouldn't have been able to disguise himself... Not sure if some of his skills from his years as a young thief helped him out here, or if he's found some other way to pass through such a dangerous place unharmed.
OK. For now, this is the last item on Kaedric's list. But I doubt this was actually his last stop.
I'd say it's business as usual. Let's follow Kaedric's tracks, and see what we can find.

I guess I'll have to confront Ferri now. I don't know why he's so reluctant to help us, but with the clues we've gathered, it's quite clear which direction Kaedric went in. Lets see what Ferri has to say. Could you wait outside the Mayor's House this time? I want to clear the air my way. I'll be back in a jiffy, I promise.
It seems Ferri wasn't underestimating the wilderness out here... Before we can continue our search, we must shoo away those... ahem... beasts?!
Ah, over there! Do you see it? And those! What was he looking at? Oh... I think I see a pattern. Can we collect the tracks and see where he went next?
How curious... This building doesn't look abandoned at all? Perhaps the people living here have met Kaedric?

I'm getting good at this... See these branches? And there - I think those are footprints! These must be some of the ruins Ferri was talking about! But this can't be what Kaedric was interested in... It's just a ruin? Hmm... Maybe I'll check it out. Do you want to do the same? Oh wow, look at these! Such a strong crimson color... I wonder what Kaedric was looking for?

We'll have to ask our specialists to craft some very precise dynamite... Else we'll not only be getitng rid of the rock, but we'll be turning everything nearby into rubble too. Also, I fear we'll have to build some kind of special casing to ensure the dynamite doesn't get wet on the long journey - or even worse, explode due to the lightning storms. I shudder just thinking about this.
Hopefully Kaedric's not just lying behind the mountain in some sort of ditch... Actually, it's worth a try. KAAAAAEEEEDRIIIIIC!!!... Nothing. OK, let's blow this thing up!

You see the spots in the south eastern part of the village? Those are natural deposits of saltpeter and titanium ore. I'm happy to leave the decision about which resource to mine up to you, as you probably have a better understanding of the market value and what would be more useful to us in the long run. We'll send you your cut weekly. But please, be aware - you cannot change your decision afterwards, and we cannot mine both, as this would destroy the mine. The ground in Laeylorn is a bit, ahem... fragile.

Somehow, I've come to enjoy these puzzles and riddles. We should send some specialists to take a closer look at this weird house and its surroundings. These apples are a bit shinier than usual, if I'm not mistaken. But somehow, there's also something a bit... dreadful about them. I'd love to do the investigation myself, but I'm afraid I have neither the time nor the expertise. Do you know anyone who'd be willing to do the job? Oh no... please don't tell me you're thinking about HIM?! Oh, what have I done... I hope he doesn't blow up the whole area.

It's been a pleasure to see you work - although it is unfortunate you couldn't find Kaedric. I hope you find him soon. If we hear anything, I'll be sure to contact you and Sonya personally.
For now, though, we'll get to rebuilding our beatiful town as promised. If you find the time before you leave, be sure you stop by for a good meal and a chat, eh?

Bid your farewell to Laeylorn for now and give your regards to Ferri Felder.
Finishing this quest concludes the first chapter of the Twin Town Quests.

Wondering when you'll be able to find the next gift under your Gift Christmas Tree? Don't worry - I've got it covered. Here you can see when the next gift will appear. The timer will restart after you grab your current gift.

Here you can see how long we'll be at sea, whooooo! Bet you can't wait for us to return, huh? We are so glad to have found y-whoooo, and will try our best to reward you with nice things when we return! Don't forget to come by and get your stuff - we won't leave for another adventure until then!
Over the last few days, temperatures have been rising higher and higher. Today it is almost unbearable. Your squad needs way more drinking water than usual. Provide some from your storage!
One of the tournament’s stadiums needs some safety repairs. You can’t risk any of the crowd getting injured. Provide the materials needed to carry out the repairs!

Traveling actors are visiting your island, and have given a stunning theatrical performance of Shakespeare’s “A Midsummer Night’s Dream”. As a team building measure, you and your squad attended the play. The players left delighted, and so did you! Provide an extra tip for the artists to make sure they come again next summer!
A supportive settler volunteers to produce and hand out stadium magazines during matches. He asks you for some quality materials to print on.
Some of your team’s players are lacking in experience. Arrange a friendly match and assemble a squad of 11 recruits to play against!
To celebrate her 93rd birthday, your oldest living settler, Irma, plans to make her famous pepperoni. But to finish her recipe, she'll need some saltpeter.
Your settlers are planning on holding a horse race - but they'll need some talent on horseback to make it happen.

Traveling actors are visiting your island, and have given a stunning theatrical performance. The settlers left delighted, and so did you! Provide an extra tip for the artists to make sure they come again!
Now the whole archipelago is fully in our hands, it’s time for your settlers to prosper and begin to accumulate wealth.
Take a look at the trade market and sell some goods for gold coins!
You showed great skill with your trades, but your treasurer still isn't happy. He asks you to produce some shiny gold coins.

The last visitors you received at the mayor’s house didn't seem overly impressed with the building’s condition. A particularly fastidious guest even said it appeared rather old-fashioned to him. Let’s give it a new coat of paint.

An alternative practitioner has risen to fame on your archipelago. Many of your settlers claim he's healed them from various illnesses and nuisances. Unfortunately though, he's now run out of the materials he uses for his therapies.
The first thing the practitioner needs is some obsidian ore.
The next thing the practitioner needs is some fresh, home grown oilseed to produce oil for his massage therapy, which he claims helps defend against cold hands and cold feet.
The Bonabertis, a very wealthy and highly influential family dynasty from a neighboring island, have notified you of an upcoming visit.
The Bonabertis are used to an insanely luxurious lifestyle. You should be prepared to accommodate for that, as it will certainly be advantageous to be on good terms with the Bonaberti family.
Now we need some high-quality interiors. It's rumored that the Bonabertis have a soft spot for mahogany.
Incredible! Wild horses have been seen on the main island. What a great opportunity to tame and train them for your military.
The first thing we need to do is to tame the horses, and get them used to having a rider.
Now that the wild horses have been successfully tamed, we need to train them to become battle horses.
“Oh my darling, I love sunflowers so much! Make sure that we never run out of them, and my love will always be yours!” You'd better stock up on that fertilizer!

There are rumors about a belligerent tribe on a nearby island who are on the brink of developing seafaring. Your settlers are afraid - reassure them of your army’s strength by training new elite soldiers!
As a very intelligent man once said: “Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.” Make sure that you make good use of it.
True friends always make sure things are running smoothly, not only for themselves, but for each other. Use machine oil on a friend’s island.

A severe and totally unexpected locust plague is threatening to destroy your wheat fields. Your settlers are in a panic, and are calling for you to help. Fortunately, your best scientist has worked out a formula for a highly effective insecticide. You should provide the necessary materials as soon as possible.

Today, someone dropped a mysterious letter on the mayor's house's doorstep. It reads:
What’s up, buttercup?
My name's Dora, but don’t worry – I'm here to help you. As you might already know, we have something very special coming up. The big bang of birthday parties: The Settlers Online Anniversary Party! You'd better get used to my little letters now, honey, because every morning I'll be dropping one on your doorstep with new instructions for the party. So let’s get to business - get started with the preparations now, will you, my dear?

What’s a birthday party without proper space to celebrate in!? We need to build some nice and cozy venues for the anniversary event – and therefore we need materials, right? Let’s start with some planks, sweetheart.
The interiors would look so much nicer if we used some of our exquisite marble on it, don’t you think?
We definitely should balance work and pleasure: for now, you're free to go out and seek adventure, lovey!
Okay, let's get back to work! The interiors could use some nice metal, don't you think? For stability, and that extra-strong look of course. Oh, the party on anniversary day's gonna be great, honey!
Another thing we'll need is some personnel to help with the construction work. They need to be strong and plenty, my dear!

Another letter from Dora has arrived:
What’s up, buttercup?
Today we’re supposed to make the celebration room nice and jovial. Do you think you could help with that, my dear?
First, we'll need some nice new furniture for the celebration room. Would you be so kind as to send some gold coins for that?
We definitely should balance work and pleasure: for now, you're free to go out and seek adventure, lovey!
Oh my, it seems our new furniture still needs to be assembled! Would it be possible for you to provide some tools, sweetie?
Oh no, it seems we’re out of bolts! How are we supposed to finish our furniture now? Could you produce some metal for bolts, please?

Another letter from Dora has arrived:
What’s up, buttercup?
The anniversary party’s guests can’t feast on air alone. We should provide some high-quality food for the party, don’t you think, sweetheart?
We should provide some high-quality food for the party. First, we should fetch some sausages from your storehouses.
We definitely need to balance work and pleasure: for now, you're free to go out and seek adventure, lovey!
Okay, back to work! We need some bread for our party. Would you be so kind to produce some, honey?
Let's not forget the fresh drinks for the party. Could you please up your water production, my dear?

I'm sure you know by now that many of your settlers regard a decent brew as essential for any party. We have to make sure our production is running as well as it possibly can.

Another letter from Dora:
Dear Mayor,
Unfortunately, I have to interrupt the preparations for today. It seems that a hostile nation’s leader on a neighboring island has heard of our party plans for the anniversary and thinks this would be a good opportunity for a surprise attack. You absolutely should not let your guard down, even in times of celebration. I think we should brace for the attack...

Whew! That was quite the achievement - and a lot of work, as we'd expect from such powerful nobles. Still, the challenges have been completed, and you've earned yourself some free time. Enjoy the festivities!

So, you're all going to cooperate and keep donating to make this the best festival ever, right? Just like the last two weeks, the worldwide balloon donations total will be tracked below. I'll be sure to update the running total every few minutes! Aren't I the best? You know the drill. Reach the target in a week, and everyone will get their reward!

The case of the strange island and the suddenly appearing mist... I wonder what's behind it all? I guess all we can do is explore the island and defeat any evildoers we find along the way. It seems they don't have any leaders with them, either. I wonder if that'll make it easier, or not?

Greetings. You can call me Darkhood. It is of incredible importance that you complete the following rituals. Who am I really? That doesn't matter. No, don't come any closer!
Do what I tell you, and you'll be rewarded greatly thihihi...I mean, muahahaha! If not, you'll have to face the consequences!
Go gather the ingredients. We need them fresh and oozing life energy.
Harvest some emotion-energy from your friends. Hihi...erm muahaha! I wonder if they'll like your "gifts".
Let your friends feast on your emotions too!
Go out and prepare your people for the worst!
Stock up your reserves. You'll need plenty of "fertilizer" soon, muhahahihihihahah.
Get some action. You look tired.
There is still more we need, but I cannot tell you exactly what. You might be shocked. So just get a lot of everything!
This might seem tedious, but at least you have a choice: don't be lazy, get it done! Or else!
Let some evildoers repent!
Strengthen your bond to those dearest to you! Or just anyone, really... It doesn't matter. Just don't do it all on your own!
This is really important! I know someone who really likes to eat fish and... I mean, this is important for the "R-i-t-u-a-l-l-l" hihi-cough-muahaha.
To complete the process, we'll need people to dig a hole- I mean to prepare the ritual site.
And we'll need some dark resources. Coal should do. Yes, this is verrry important. Coal. Coal is always important.

Ah! I was just going to leave, then I realized I hadn't shown you how to care for this beautiful thing! I just love all kinds of plants. Whoops! It seems my hood slipped a bit... Well, OK - I think it's fine anyway, hihihi.
You know, this kind of tree is brimming with a special energy. Because of this, many even fear its seeds, and far fewer dare to plant them. But this tree is so incredibly rare, it almost vanished completely. And it's not the tree's fault it was used for evil deeds! There are just a few of these trees left - but luckily, I was able to get my hands on the one I gave to you. The others can only be traded for.
Please treat it with care and nurture, as best you can.

An emissary of the King is coming.
He states that his mission is to audit the inner workings of your island, to help you make the necessary changes to survive these troubling times - and every other challenge the world can throw at you.
Get your island ready for the arrival of the auditor.

Greetings! My name is Dunning Foozler. I'm an envoy of the King, and have been sent here to oversee your settlement and make sure everything is in agreement with our regulations - and that you have everything you need to succeed in future.
But first things first, I need you to find me a proper place to stay and set up my equipment.
I have been told that your hospitality is legendary. If you please, I'd like to stay at your very best.

Ah! I know what's wrong. The location you chose is not conducive to a properly productive environment.
Let's find a better spot, shall we?
My luggage hasn't been taken to my lodgings. I need my equipment so I can set up my office before I can start working. Would you kindly...?

First in the docket, I have this new formula for a... um... "fauna performance enhancer". Yes, that's what it says here.
In theory, this beauty should dramatically increase game meat available for settlers.
But first, we need to gather the resources needed to develop it. These need to be fresh - stored goods lack the necessary potency.

To begin with, we need to study the nature of the local fauna.
Let's start with learning about the piscine variety.
For this task, I'll need you to bring me some recently captured aquatic wildlife.

That's the fish dealt with - now we need to focus our efforts on understanding land-based creatures.
We'll need to examine your own livestock, as well as the wild creatures that dwell in the woods.

Here - my concoction for improving the yield of your livestock is ready.
I guarantee it is completely safe to use, and the results will more than make up for your troubles.

After the last... um... "incident", I've come to the conclusion that it'd be safer if we conducted our tests somewhere a bit more out of the way. At least, until my formulas are stable.
WHICH THEY SHOULD BE!
My calculations are well known for their precision. So I've been told.
Happily, I happened to stumble upon the coordinates for this nearby deserted island, which will serve as a perfectly safe test site.
To get to the island, we'll need to build a ship. And to build a ship, we need wood. And lots of it.

Now, we'll need some nails to... Er... nail all those planks together into something that resembles a ship.
Iron is the best material for the task ahead.
Again, it needs to be freshly mined iron. Rusty old stock just won't make the cut.
Now we just need to deliver all the produced materials to the nearest shipyard, so we can start building your first ship.

Use the ticket I gave you earlier. Onward, to the island!
I'm quivering with anxiety just thinking about the discoveries we'll be able to make once we get there.

Like I said before - I've had an epiphany.
I believe I've devised a formula for a buff that will dramatically increase your production output.
This time, it's also completely free of unwanted side effects.
The numbers don't lie!

Minerals are essential for proper nutrition. And nutrition is an important part of my elixirs.
Please, could you provide me with the minerals in this list?

The second most important ingredient is a type of vegetable protein, easily extractable from the grain you produce locally.
I don't want to frighten you with big words. The key point is that we need copious amounts of grain.

I will now provide you with clear instructions on how to properly administer the elixir.
Would you kindly provide me with a pen and paper?

The moment of truth is upon us! Go forth and use your new buff to usher in a new era of unprecedented productivity.
We should be proud of what we are about to achieve.
These documents contain the final formula. I took the liberty of adding a little extra to put off the fires and make up for what has been lost.
Unsurprisingly, the key ingredient for the formula is water. Lots and lots of fresh water.

Let us not take any chances this time. We will proceed by doing controlled tests.
First up is livestock.

The initial tests went very well. No side effects, and the animals look even more lively than before.
For the next step, I'll need the exact goods listed here in this paper.

I'm done with dinner, so now I will proceed to test the elixir with some human testing.
For that, I will need some desperate souls... I mean, brave volunteers.
If all goes according to plan, I will return to you with a final batch of elixir shortly.

Oh my goodness! Something must have gone wrong.
I am quite sure I read the coordinates correctly. The island should be here!
Don't just stand there glaring at me, help those poor sailors!
Quick! Go back to your provision house and make some floaters with these schematics.
Great, you're back. Use the floaters you produced to save the drowning sailors, before it's too late!

Mr. Foozler left a note behind. It reads
"Dear Mayor... Apologies for any trouble I may or may not have caused you. Go ahead and try the Zone Refresher. You won't regret it.
Yours truly, DF"

The Balloon Creator always needs some time for his new special creations. He is very careful, and only presents the best of his work. Give him some more time and come back when he is ready. But don't forget to visit him again. He will not begin work on another creation until the previous one is collected.

The case of the strange island and the suddenly appearing mist... I wonder what's behind it all? I guess all we can do is explore the island and defeat any evildoers we find along the way. It seems they don't have any leaders with them, either. I wonder if that'll make it easier, or not?

This is so exciting! Pay a visit to the Balloon Market Tribute and say "Hi" to the balloon creator. He has a special creation, just for you! You can find your balloon present in your Star Menu after paying a visit at the Balloon Market Tribute.

The balloon creator always needs a bit of time to work on his new special creations. He is very careful, and only reveals the very best of his work. Give him some time and come back when he’s ready. But don't forget to visit him again - he’ll not start work on another creation until the old one has been collected.
Something looms over the horizon.

A massive flash of light in the sky signals that times might be changing for the unsuspecting settlers of this island.
Everyone’s feeling unsettled, but Explorer Rina is leading the efforts to uncover this mystery.

Well hello there, Mayor! I'm Rina, one of the explorers. As you might be aware, we've got ourselves a bit of a situation...
I’ve taken the the liberty of organizing an expedition to find out what we’re facing - and I have a feeling we need to find out fast!

Regarding the expedition I mentioned earlier, we've got two things we need to tackle. First, we’ll need to recruit explorers - good ones.
I need the finest explorers we have to join me.

Secondly, I’ll need you to send these fine recruits out on treasure searches.
Their findings will give me a better idea of what we’re dealing with.

Our initial search has discovered some fragments - dust motes, if you will - which are part of something much more larger which has fallen from the sky.
We should do as follows.

I don't like the look of these motes.
Mayor, I’ll need the resources from the following list to create the equipment we need to safely retrieve the foreign objects.
I’ll also need some brave volunteers.

Here's a sketch I made of what we'll need to provide in terms of the necessary safety equipment.
I know it looks sketchy, but that’s exactly what a sketch means, and it is the best I was able to devise at such short notice.
You’ll be able to find what we need at the Provision House.
Now that everybody’s properly outfitted for the task ahead, we should head out and collect the motes.

So the dust motes have been safely retrieved?
Perfect!
There’s something both mesmerizing and terrifying about their otherworldly glow.
We need to take them somewhere we can properly study them and find out more about their nature.

To be honest, Mayor. I'm not entirely comfortable about carrying out the research in such a populated area.
These dust motes could be dangerous.

And now, we wait...
I trust the investigations are in the most capable hands you could find.

We cannot allow these "Fallen Stars" to taint the environment they came into contact with, let alone the people.
We need a new kind of facility that could properly store these stars, and allow us to study them as far from everything we hold dear as possible.
I believe I have just the thing...

This project needs copious amounts of wood for it to fly.
Here’s a list with the specifications, varieties, cut sizes, and last but not least, quantities we need.

We need to turn this, quite frankly, impressive stock of wood into hull parts.
The plans have been already delivered to your Provision House.

I know that cloth isn’t the first thing that comes to mind when you hear "high security facility".
Things are a bit up the air right now, but trust me - it’ll all make sense in time.
If we’re not able to keep up with the production demands for this project, maybe we can trade for the materials we need?

These patterns show how to properly cut and stitch together all this cloth into the shapes we need.
You can find them at the Provision House.

As unorthodox as it sounds, we’ll need copious amounts of highly fermentable products.
These are of the utmost importance if we want this project to lift off.

Here’s the recipe and formulations for how to ferment these raw materials into a gas with the necessary properties for our little project.
Everything is ready to go at the Provision House.

The pieces of the puzzle are all in place, Mayor. Allow me to present you with the schematics for the Airship.
I’ve taken the liberty of delivering them to the Provision House, because I cannot wait to see her fly.

The ship is ready to make her maiden voyage, Mayor!
All she needs now is a proper name.
…How about the Forerunner?
Please, do the honors at your house.

Now that she’s up and running, we have work to do!
Please, join me on the bridge. We have much to discuss.

With a floating headquarters and science facility, we can fly all over the island and retrieve any dust motes quickly.
Unlike last time, we’re now well prepared to produce the right equipment to procure said motes safely.

The captain has pinpointed the location of the dust motes.
We should put those collection kits we made earlier to good use.

I have... not so great news, Mayor.
These fallen stars are emanating an energy that is harmful to the land and all who dwell upon it.
With the dust motes we collected earlier, we can track down the larger Fallen Star fragments.

We’ll need to find remove any fragments as soon as we can, before they cause irreversible damage.
Deliver the survey to the captain so we can make our way to the fragments.

As I mentioned before, we need to prepare the tools we need to extract the fallen stars from our land.
The Forerunner is equipped with the facilities to construct such tools, but not a lot of storage space... Trade offs.

With the materials in place, we can now construct the mechanical wonders we need to tear through hard structure of the fallen stars.
We’ll need one tool for each fallen star we detect.
The S.C.R.A.P.P.E.R.s are ready and waiting. Remember, these are single use tools, but I designed them to have minimal waste material after they’ve done their job.

Well, I'll be! The crystalline structure of the fallen star is proving to be a challenge even for our S.C.R.A.P.P.E.R.s.
They’ll take some time to finish their work.

Even though they cannot be allowed to come into contact with the land, these shards have interesting properties.
We’ll keep this one aboard the Forerunner for safekeeping.

We would like to carry out some experiments in the Forerunner’s onboard laboratory.
Each research task requires a large amount of star shards, but I assure you, the discoveries we could make are well worth the effort.

Hello again, Mayor.
As I predicted, it seems the star showers we previously experienced are part of an ongoing phenomena.
We’d better get the Forerunner ready.

The Forerunner, as impressive as she is, is a very demanding lady.
All the advanced equipment we have onboard needs quite a bit of maintenance.
If you'd be kind enough to provide the necessary materials and spare parts, we can have her up and running in no time.

We’ll need to collect Stardust Motes to pinpoint the touchdown location of the Fallen Stars.
This time we have a much improved version of the collection kits, which will make the ordeal much safer.

Deliver the Stardust Motes to the onboard lab so we can analyze them and chart a course.
Once we have our heading, deliver it to the captain so we can make way.

We have have our heading. It's time to ready the extraction equipment.
The Forerunner lab onboard is already fired up and ready.

The S.C.R.A.P.P.E.R.s are ready and well oiled.
Place them on a Star Shard deposit so the removal procedure can commence.

These S.C.R.A.P.P.E.R.s are wonders of ingenuity - however, that does not mean there is no room from improvement.
I have devised a formula for a special lubricant that will substantially increase their operational efficiency.
Now that lubricant is bottled in convenient... bottles... it is ready to be applied on the extractors.
Make sure to keep the S.C.R.A.P.P.E.R.s working at peak performance for maximum effect.
As mentioned before, we’ll store the bulk of the Star Shards on board. Nevertheless, it is only fair that you have some to use at your leisure, in return for all the support you’ve provided.

Hello again, Mayor.
As I predicted, it seems the star showers we previously experienced are part of an ongoing phenomena.
We’d better get the Forerunner ready.

The Forerunner, as impressive as she is, is a very demanding lady.
All the advanced equipment we have onboard needs quite a bit of maintenance.
